metadata.title: A blueprint for the formalization of Carleson's theorem on convergence of Fourier series

extraction_notes.note: The axiomatic structures (compatible collection, grid structure, tile structure, n-forest) are defined in running text over several sentences with their defining properties as numbered equations; each is one definition node with the property equations nested in it.

Parts of the proofs of finitary Carleson and of the weak (1,1) lemma are argued in running text before the auxiliary lemmas; they are prose proof nodes linked to the later proof environments by a continuation uses edge.
The definition of Omega includes the in-line argument that the minimal parent cube J is unique; kept inside the definition rather than split into a claim.

Objects defined inside proofs (the separated set S in the proof of correlation separated trees, B(p) and A(p) in the dens1 proof) are reused by later lemmas, but per step rule 4 they stay proof steps with no definition node.

Historical results stated in one prose sentence each (Kolmogorov, Hunt, Billard) and the uncited facts about doubling spaces were kept as external theorem/claim nodes; they could also be read as mere citations.
Four numbered equations have bodies too short for the finishing step to match them to their environments (a>=4, I subset J, p<=p', ||f||_2); they are kept as equation nodes.

The proof of frequency ball growth cites eqref firstdb1 where seconddb1 is meant (the ref edge is kept), and the proof of integer ball cover concludes membership in B_1 in its last case where B_3 is meant.
Historical survey of later work (Stein-Wainger, Lie, polynomial Carleson operators), acknowledgements, section overviews and remarks on the Lean formalization process were not extracted.

metadata.extraction_comment: Defined-term edges (pass 2) were added for every finishing-step warning of a definition used without an edge, mapped to the containing Level-1 node; all other dependencies come mostly from the paper's dense \Cref/\eqref cross-references.

nodes.name: trigonometric polynomial $S_N$
nodes.statement_short: A trigonometric polynomial is $S_N(x)=\sum_{|n|\le N} c_n e^{inx}$.

nodes.name: Equation (1)
nodes.statement: S_N(x):= \sum_{n=-N}^N c_n e^{inx} \ .
nodes.label: eq:trig-series

nodes.name: Fourier series
nodes.statement:
The Fourier series is then defined as the limit $f$ of such a sequence $S_N$
as $N$ tends to $\infty$.

nodes.name: Fourier coefficients
nodes.statement:
The first question has a fairly canonical and standard answer, provided by the Fourier integral formula:
\begin{equation} c_n:=\widehat{f}_n:=\frac 1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}f(x) e^{- i nx}\, dx,
\end{equation}
 where the precise interpretation of the integral depends on the chosen theory of integration.
nodes.statement_short: The Fourier coefficients are $\hat f_n = \frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} f(x)e^{-inx}dx$.

nodes.name: Equation (2)
nodes.statement: c_n:=\widehat{f}_n:=\frac 1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}f(x) e^{- i nx}\, dx,
nodes.label: eq:fourier-coefficients

nodes.name: Luzin's conjecture
nodes.statement:
Such convergence
was conjectured by N. Luzin \cite{Luzin13}
for the space
$L^2(0,2\pi)$, see also the collected works \cite{Luzin53}.
nodes.statement_short: Fourier series of $L^2(0,2\pi)$ functions converge almost everywhere.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov's example
nodes.statement: Kolmogorov's example \cite{Kolmogorov} of an $L^1$ function whose Fourier series diverges at almost every point seemed to provide some evidence against Luzin's conjecture.
nodes.statement_short: There is an $L^1$ function whose Fourier series diverges almost everywhere.
conclusions: an $L^1$ function whose Fourier series diverges at almost every point

nodes.name: classical Carleson theorem
nodes.statement: Let $f$ be a $2\pi$-periodic complex-valued continuous function on $\mathbb{R}$. Then for almost all $x \in \mathbb{R}$ we have \begin{equation} \lim_{N\to\infty}S_N f(x) = f(x), \end{equation} where $S_N f$ is the $N$-th partial Fourier sum of $f$ defined in \eqref{eq:trig-series} with coefficients \eqref{eq:fourier-coefficients}.
assumptions: Let $f$ be a $2\pi$-periodic complex-valued continuous function on $\mathbb{R}$
nodes.statement_short: Fourier partial sums of a continuous $2\pi$-periodic function converge to it almost everywhere.
nodes.label: classical-carleson

nodes.name: Equation (3)
nodes.statement: \lim_{N\to\infty}S_N f(x) = f(x),
nodes.label: eq:fourier-limit

nodes.name: Hunt's theorem
nodes.statement:
Shortly after Carleson's breakthrough, Hunt \cite{MR238019} proved the analogous result for $L^p$ functions
with $p>1$ and for functions in $L^1\log(L)^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Almost everywhere convergence of Fourier series for $L^p$, $p>1$, and $L\log^2 L$.
assumptions:
for $L^p$ functions
with $p>1$ and for functions in $L^1\log(L)^2$

nodes.name: Billard's theorem
nodes.statement:
Billard \cite{MR217510} adapted Carleson's arguments to prove almost everywhere convergence of Walsh-Fourier series
for functions in $L^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Walsh-Fourier series of $L^2$ functions converge almost everywhere.

nodes.name: Carleson's operator
nodes.statement:
In \cite{fefferman}, C. Fefferman gave an alternative proof of Carleson's theorem via an a priori
bound for Carleson's operator, the maximally modulated singular integral
\begin{equation} Tf(x):=\sup_{N} \int_{-\pi}^\pi e^{iNy}f(x-y)\frac 1y {dy}\, .
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Carleson's operator is the maximally modulated Hilbert transform $\sup_N|\int e^{iNy} f(x-y) dy/y|$.

nodes.name: Equation (4)
nodes.statement: Tf(x):=\sup_{N} \int_{-\pi}^\pi e^{iNy}f(x-y)\frac 1y {dy}\, .
nodes.label: eq:feffermancarleson

nodes.name: doubling metric measure space
nodes.statement:
A doubling metric measure space $(X,\rho,\mu, a)$ is a complete
and locally compact metric space $(X,\rho)$
equipped with a non-zero locally finite Borel measure $\mu$ that satisfies the doubling condition that for all $x\in X$ and all $R>0$ we have
\begin{equation} \mu(B(x,2R))\le 2^a\mu(B(x,R))\,,
\end{equation}
where we have denoted by $B(x,R)$ the open ball of radius $R$ centered at $x$:
\begin{equation} B(x,R):=\{y\in X: \rho(x,y)<R\}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1.1 Statement of the metric space Carleson theorems
nodes.statement_short: A complete locally compact metric space with a Borel measure satisfying $\mu(B(x,2R))\le 2^a\mu(B(x,R))$.

nodes.name: Equation (6)
nodes.statement: \mu(B(x,2R))\le 2^a\mu(B(x,R))\,,
nodes.section: 1.1 Statement of the metric space Carleson theorems
nodes.label: doublingx

nodes.name: Equation (7)
nodes.statement: B(x,R):=\{y\in X: \rho(x,y)<R\}.
nodes.section: 1.1 Statement of the metric space Carleson theorems
nodes.label: eq-define-ball

nodes.name: properties of doubling spaces
nodes.statement: In a doubling metric measure space the closed balls are compact and $\mu$ is positive on all non-empty open sets.
nodes.section: 1.1 Statement of the metric space Carleson theorems
conclusions: $\mu$ is positive on all non-empty open sets
assumptions: In a doubling metric measure space

nodes.name: compatible collection
nodes.statement:
A collection $\Mf$ of real valued continuous functions on the doubling metric measure space $(X,\rho,\mu,a)$ is called compatible,
if there is a point $o\in X$ where all the functions are equal to $0$,
and if there exists for each ball $B \subset X$ a metric $d_B$ on $\Mf$,
such that the following five properties \eqref{osccontrol}, \eqref{firstdb}, \eqref{monotonedb}, \eqref{seconddb}, and \eqref{thirddb} are satisfied.
For every ball $B \subset X$
\begin{equation} \sup_{x,y\in B}|\mfa(x)-{\mfa(y)}- \mfb(x)+{\mfb(y)}| \le d_{B}(\mfa,\mfb)\,.
\end{equation}
For any two balls $B_1=B(x_1,R)$, $B_2= B(x_2,2R)$ in $X$ with $x_1\in B_2$ and any $\mfa,\mfb\in \Mf$,
\begin{equation} d_{B_2}(\mfa,\mfb)\le 2^a d_{B_1}(\mfa,\mfb) .
\end{equation}
For any two balls $B_1, B_2$ in $X$ with $B_1 \subset B_2$ and any $\mfa, \mfb \in \Mf$
\begin{equation} d_{B_1}(\mfa,\mfb) \le d_{B_2}(\mfa, \mfb)
\end{equation}
and for any two balls
$B_1=B(x_1,R)$, $B_2= B(x_2,2^aR)$
with $B_1\subset B_2$, and $\mfa,\mfb\in \Mf$,
\begin{equation} 2d_{B_1}(\mfa,\mfb)
\le d_{B_2}(\mfa,\mfb) .
\end{equation}
For every ball $B$ in $X$ and every $d_B$-ball $\tilde B$ of radius $2R$ in $\Mf$, there is a collection $\mathcal{B}$ of
at most $2^a$ many $d_B$-balls of radius $R$ covering $\tilde B$, that is,
\begin{equation} \tilde B\subset \bigcup \mathcal{B}.
\end{equation}
nodes.section: 1.1 Statement of the metric space Carleson theorems
nodes.genus: collection $\Mf$ of real valued continuous functions
nodes.statement_short: A family of functions vanishing at $o$ with ball-indexed metrics $d_B$ satisfying oscillation control, doubling and covering properties.

nodes.name: Equation (8)
nodes.statement: \sup_{x,y\in B}|\mfa(x)-{\mfa(y)}- \mfb(x)+{\mfb(y)}| \le d_{B}(\mfa,\mfb)\,.
nodes.section: 1.1 Statement of the metric space Carleson theorems
nodes.label: osccontrol

nodes.name: Equation (9)
nodes.statement: d_{B_2}(\mfa,\mfb)\le 2^a d_{B_1}(\mfa,\mfb) .
nodes.section: 1.1 Statement of the metric space Carleson theorems
nodes.label: firstdb

nodes.name: Equation (10)
nodes.statement: d_{B_1}(\mfa,\mfb) \le d_{B_2}(\mfa, \mfb)
nodes.section: 1.1 Statement of the metric space Carleson theorems
nodes.label: monotonedb

nodes.name: Equation (11)
nodes.statement: 2d_{B_1}(\mfa,\mfb) \le d_{B_2}(\mfa,\mfb) .
nodes.section: 1.1 Statement of the metric space Carleson theorems
nodes.label: seconddb

nodes.name: Equation (12)
nodes.statement: \tilde B\subset \bigcup \mathcal{B}.
nodes.section: 1.1 Statement of the metric space Carleson theorems
nodes.label: thirddb

nodes.name: cancellative collection
nodes.statement:
Further, a compatible collection $\Mf$ is called cancellative, if
for any ball $B$ in $X$ of radius $R$, any Lipschitz function $\varphi: X\to \C$
supported on $B$, and any $\mfa,\mfb\in \Mf$ we have
\begin{equation} |\int_B e(\mfa(x)-{\mfb(x)}) \varphi(x) d\mu(x)|\le 2^a \mu(B)\|\varphi\|_{\Lip(B)}
(1+d_B(\mfa,\mfb))^{-\frac{1}{a}},
\end{equation}
where $\|\cdot\|_{\Lip(B)}$ denotes the inhomogeneous Lipschitz norm on $B$:
$$
    \|\varphi\|_{\Lip(B)} = \sup_{x \in B} |\varphi(x)| + R \sup_{x,y \in B, x \neq y} \frac{|\varphi(x) - \varphi(y)|}{\rho(x,y)}\,.
$$
nodes.section: 1.1 Statement of the metric space Carleson theorems
nodes.statement_short: Oscillatory integrals $\int_B e(\mfa-\mfb)\varphi$ decay like $(1+d_B(\mfa,\mfb))^{-1/a}$ for Lipschitz $\varphi$.

nodes.name: Equation (13)
nodes.statement: |\int_B e(\mfa(x)-{\mfb(x)}) \varphi(x) d\mu(x)|\le 2^a \mu(B)\|\varphi\|_{\Lip(B)} (1+d_B(\mfa,\mfb))^{-\frac{1}{a}},
nodes.section: 1.1 Statement of the metric space Carleson theorems
nodes.label: eq-vdc-cond

nodes.name: one-sided Calderón–Zygmund kernel
nodes.section: 1.1 Statement of the metric space Carleson theorems
nodes.statement_short: A kernel with size bound $2^{a^3}/V(x,y)$ and Hölder smoothness in the second variable.

nodes.name: metric space Carleson theorem
nodes.statement: For all integers $a \ge 4$ and real numbers $1<q\le 2$ the following holds. Let $(X,\rho,\mu,a)$ be a doubling metric measure space. Let $\Mf$ be a cancellative compatible collection of functions and let $K$ be a one-sided Calder\'on--Zygmund kernel on $(X,\rho,\mu,a)$. Assume that for every bounded measurable function $g$ on $X$ supported on a set of finite measure we have \begin{equation} \|T_{*}g\|_{2} \leq 2^{a^3} \|g\|_2\,, \end{equation} where $T_{*}$ is defined in \eqref{def-tang-unm-op}. Then for all Borel sets $F$ and $G$ in $X$ and all Borel functions $f:X\to \C$ with $|f|\le \mathbf{1}_F$, we have, with $T$ defined in \eqref{def-main-op}, \begin{equation} \left|\int_{G} T f \, \mathrm{d}\mu\right| \leq \frac{2^{443a^3}}{(q-1)^6} \mu(G)^{1-\frac{1}{q}} \mu(F)^{\frac{1}{q}}\, . \end{equation}

nodes.name: linearised metric Carleson theorem
nodes.statement: For all integers $a \ge 4$ and real numbers $1<q\le 2$ the following holds. Let $(X,\rho,\mu,a)$ be a doubling metric measure space. Let $\Mf$ be a cancellative compatible collection of functions. Let $\tQ:X\to \Mf$ be a Borel function with finite range. Let $K$ be a one-sided Calder\'on--Zygmund kernel on $(X,\rho,\mu,a)$. Assume that for every $\mfa\in \Mf$ and every bounded measurable function $g$ on $X$ supported on a set of finite measure we have \begin{equation} \|T_{\tQ}^\mfa g\|_{2} \leq 2^{a^3} \|g\|_2\,, \end{equation} where $T_{\tQ}^\mfa$ is defined in \eqref{def-lin-star-op}. Then for all Borel sets $F$ and $G$ in $X$ and all Borel functions $f:X\to \C$ with $|f|\le \mathbf{1}_F$, we have, with $T_\tQ$ defined in \eqref{def-lin-main-op}, \begin{equation} \left|\int_{G} T_\tQ f \, \mathrm{d}\mu\right| \le \frac{2^{443a^3}}{(q-1)^6} \mu(G)^{1-\frac{1}{q}} \mu(F)^{\frac{1}{q}}\, . \end{equation}

nodes.name: remark on the constants
nodes.statement: The value of the constant factor $2^{443a^3}$ in Theorems~\ref{metric-space-Carleson} and~\ref{linearised-metric-Carleson} is by no means sharp. One source of non-sharpness is our choice to write for readability most constants in the form $2^{na^3}$ for some explicit constant $n$. An a posteriori byproduct of the Lean formalization of this document is that Theorems~\ref{metric-space-Carleson} and~\ref{linearised-metric-Carleson} remain true with $2^{44a^3}$ instead of $2^{443a^3}$. This is obtained by changing the parameter $D$ introduced in~\eqref{defineD} from $2^{100a^2}$ to $2^{7a^2}$, checking that exactly the same proof goes through, tracking the constants, and getting $2^{44a^3}$ in the end. This value is again by no means sharp. In the formalization we define the parameter $D$ as $2^{\mathbb{c}a^2}$ and the constants in this blueprint are obtained by setting $\mathbb{c} = 100$.

nodes.name: grid structure
nodes.statement:
A grid structure $(\mathcal{D}, c, s)$ on $X$ consists of a finite collection $\mathcal{D}$ of pairs $(I, k)$ of Borel
sets in $X$ and integers $k \in [-S, S]$, the projection $s\colon \mathcal{D}\to [-S, S], (I, k) \mapsto k$ to the second component which is assumed to be surjective and
called scale function, and a function $c:\mathcal{D}\to X$
called center function such that the five properties
\eqref{coverdyadic}, \eqref{dyadicproperty}, \eqref{subsetmaxcube},
\eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, and \eqref{eq-small-boundary} hold. We call the elements of $\mathcal{D}$ dyadic cubes. By abuse of notation, we will usually write just $I$ for the cube $(I,k)$, and we will write $I \subset J$ to mean that for two cubes $(I,k), (J, l) \in \mathcal{D}$ we have $I \subset J$ and $k \le l$.

For each dyadic cube $I$ and each $-S\le k<s(I)$ we have
\begin{equation} I\subset \bigcup_{J\in \mathcal {D}: s(J)=k}J\, .
\end{equation}
Any two non-disjoint dyadic cubes $I,J$ with $s(I)\le s(J)$ satisfy
\begin{equation} I\subset J.
\end{equation}
There exists a $I_0 \in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(I_0) = S$ and $c(I_0) = o$



and for all cubes $J \in \mathcal{D}$, we have
\begin{equation} J \subset I_0\,.
\end{equation}

For any dyadic cube $I$,
\begin{equation} c(I)\in B(c(I), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(I)}) \subset I \subset B(c(I), 4 D^{s(I)})\,.
\end{equation}
For any dyadic cube $I$ and any $t$ with $tD^{s(I)} \ge D^{-S}$,
\begin{equation} \mu(\{x \in I \ : \ \rho(x, X \setminus I) \leq t D^{s(I)}\}) \le 2 t^\kappa \mu(I)\,.
\end{equation}

nodes.name: $n$-forest
nodes.statement:
Let $n\ge 0$.
An $n$-forest is a pair $(\fU, \mathfrak{T})$
where $\fU$ is a subset of $\fP$
and $\mathfrak{T}$ is a map assigning to
each $\fu\in \fU$ a nonempty set $\fT (\fu)\subset \fP$ called tree
such that the following properties
\eqref{forest1}, \eqref{forest2},
\eqref{forest3},
\eqref{forest4},
\eqref{forest5}, and
\eqref{forest6}
hold.

For each $\fu\in \fU$ and each $\fp\in \fT(\fu)$
we have $\scI(\fp) \ne \scI(\fu)$ and
\begin{equation} 4\fp\lesssim \fu.
\end{equation}
For each $\fu \in \fU$ and each $\fp,\fp''\in \fT(\fu)$ and $\fp'\in \fP$
we have
\begin{equation} \fp, \fp'' \in \mathfrak{T}(\fu), \fp \leq \fp' \leq \fp'' \implies \fp' \in \mathfrak{T}(\fu).
\end{equation}
We have
\begin{equation} \|\sum_{\fu\in \fU} \mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fu)}\|_\infty \leq 2^n\,.
\end{equation}
We have for every $\fu\in \fU$
\begin{equation} \dens_1(\fT(\fu))\le 2^{4a + 1-n}\, .
\end{equation}
We have for $\fu, \fu'\in \fU$ with $\fu\neq \fu'$ and $\fp\in \fT(\fu')$ with $\scI(\fp)\subset \scI(\fu)$ that
\begin{equation} d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp), \fcc(\fu))>2^{Z(n+1)}\, .
\end{equation}
We have for every $\fu\in \fU$ and $\fp\in \fT(\fu)$ that
\begin{equation} B(\pc(\fp), 8D^{\ps(\fp)})\subset \scI(\fu).
\end{equation}
nodes.section: 2 Proof of Metric Space Carleson, overview
nodes.statement_short: An $n$-forest is a family of trees $\fT(\fu)$ indexed by $\fu\in\fU$ with convexity, bounded overlap $2^n$, density, separation and nesting properties.

nodes.name: Proof of ball metric entropy
nodes.statement: By applying property \eqref{thirddb} $k$ times, we obtain a collection $\mathcal{Z}' \subset \Mf$ with $|\mathcal{Z}'| = 2^{ka}$ and $$ B_{B'}(\mfa,r2^k) \subset \bigcup_{z' \in \mathcal{Z}'} B_{B'}(z', \frac{r}{2})\,. $$ Then each $z \in \mathcal{Z}$ is contained in one of the balls $B(z', \frac{r}{2})$, but by the separation assumption no such ball contains more than one element of $\mathcal{Z}$. Thus $|\mathcal{Z}| \le |\mathcal{Z}'| = 2^{ka}$.

nodes.name: Proof of monotone cube metrics
nodes.statement: If $s(I) \ge s(J)$ then \eqref{dyadicproperty} and the assumption $I\subset J$ imply $I = J$. Then the lemma holds by reflexivity. If $s(J) \ge s(I)+1$, then using the monotonicity property \eqref{monotonedb}, \eqref{defineD} and \eqref{seconddb}, we get \begin{equation} d_{I^\circ}(\mfa, \mfb) \le d_{B(c(I), 4 D^{s(I)})}(\mfa, \mfb) \le 2^{-100a} d_{B(c(I), 4D^{s(J)})}(\mfa, \mfb)\,. \end{equation} Using \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, together with the inclusion $I \subset J$, we obtain $$ c(I) \in I \subset J \subset B(c(J), 4 D^{s(J)}) $$ and consequently by the triangle inequality $$ B(c(I), 4 D^{s(J)}) \subset B(c(J), 8 D^{s(J)})\,. $$ Using this together with the monotonicity property \eqref{monotonedb} and \eqref{firstdb} in \eqref{eq-dIJ-est}, we obtain \begin{align*} d_{I^\circ}(\mfa, \mfb) &\le 2^{-100a} d_{B(c(J), 8D^{s(J)})}(\mfa, \mfb)\\ &\le 2^{-100a + 5a} d_{B(c(J), \frac{1}{4}D^{s(J)})}(\mfa, \mfb)\\ &= 2^{-95a}d_{J^\circ}(\mfa, \mfb)\,. \end{align*} This proves the second inequality claimed in the Lemma, from which the first follows since $a \ge 4$ and hence $2^{-95a} \le 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on scales; chain the metric comparisons \eqref{monotonedb}, \eqref{seconddb}, \eqref{firstdb}.

nodes.name: Proof of kernel summand
nodes.statement: By Definition \eqref{defks}, the function $K_s$ is the product of $K$ with a function which is supported in the set of all $x,y$ satisfying \eqref{supp-Ks}. This proves \eqref{supp-Ks}. Using \eqref{eqkernel-size} and the lower bound in \eqref{supp-Ks} we obtain \begin{equation} |K_s(x,y)|\le |K(x,y)|\le \frac{2^{a^3}}{\mu(B(x,\frac 14 D^{s-1}))} \end{equation} Using $D=2^{100a^2}$ and the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $2 +100a^2$ times estimates the last display by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{2a+101a^3}}{\mu(B(x, D^{s}))}\, . \end{equation} Using $a\ge 4$ proves \eqref{eq-Ks-size}. To prove \eqref{eq-Ks-smooth} when $2\rho(y,y') > \rho(x,y)$, use the lower bound in \eqref{supp-Ks} and the inequality $2\rho(y,y') > \frac{1}{4}D^{s-1}$. Then \eqref{eq-Ks-smooth} follows from the triangle inequality, \eqref{eq-Ks-size} and $a \ge 4$. If $2\rho(y,y') \le \rho(x,y)$, we rewrite $|K_s(x,y)-K_s(x, y')|$ as \begin{equation} |(K(x,y)-K(x,y')) \psi(D^{-s}\rho(x,y)) + K(x,y)(\psi(D^{-s}\rho(x,y))-\psi(D^{-s}\rho(x,y')))|\,. \end{equation} An upper bound for $|K(x,y)-K(x, y')|$ is obtained similarly to the proof of \eqref{eq-Ks-size}, using \eqref{eqkernel-y-smooth} and the lower bound in \eqref{supp-Ks} \begin{equation} |K(x,y)-K(x, y')|\le \frac{2^{a^3}}{\mu(B(x, \frac 14 D^{s-1}))} \left(\frac{ \rho(y,y')}{\frac 14 D^{s-1}}\right)^{\frac 1a}\,. \end{equation} As above, this is estimated by \begin{equation} \le \frac{4D 2^{2a+101a^3}}{\mu(B(x, D^{s}))} \left(\frac{ \rho(y,y')}{D^{s}}\right)^{\frac 1a} = \frac{2^{2+2a+100a^2+101a^3}}{\mu(B(x, D^{s}))} \left(\frac{ \rho(y,y')}{D^{s}}\right)^{\frac 1a}\,. \end{equation} We have the trivial bound $|\psi(D^{-s}\rho(x,y))| \leq 1$, and \eqref{eq-Ks-aux} provides a bound for $|K(x,y)|$. Finally, we show that \begin{equation} |\psi(D^{-s}\rho(x,y))-\psi(D^{-s}\rho(x,y'))|\le 4D \left(\frac{\rho(y, y')}{D ^ s}\right)^{\frac 1a} \end{equation} by considering separately the cases $\rho(y,y')/D^s \ge 1$ and $\rho(y,y')/D^s < 1$. In the former case, the inequality is trivial; in the latter case, it follows from the fact that $\psi$ is Lipschitz with constant $4D$. Combining the above bounds and using $a\ge 4$ proves \eqref{eq-Ks-smooth} when $2\rho(y,y') \le \rho(x,y)$.
nodes.statement_short: Support from $\psi$; size via the kernel bound and doubling; smoothness split into far and near cases using the Lipschitz bound of $\psi$.

nodes.name: int continuous
nodes.statement: Let $f$ be a measurable function with $|f| \le 1$. Then the function \[ G: X \times \Theta \times (0,\infty) \times (0, \infty) \to \mathbb{C} \] \[ G(x, \mfa, R_1, R_2) := \int_{R_1 < \rho(x,y) < R_2} K(x,y) f(y) e(\mfa(y)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \] is continuous in $\mfa$ for fixed $x, R_1, R_2$. It is right-continuous in $R_1$ for fixed $x, \vartheta, R_2$ and left-continuous in $R_2$ for fixed $x, \vartheta, R_1$. Finally, it is measurable in $x$ and bounded for fixed $\vartheta, R_1, R_2$.
assumptions: Let $f$ be a measurable function with $|f| \le 1$.
conclusions: is continuous in $\mfa$ for fixed $x, R_1, R_2$.
It is right-continuous in $R_1$ for fixed $x, \vartheta, R_2$ and left-continuous in $R_2$ for fixed $x, \vartheta, R_1$.
Finally, it is measurable in $x$ and bounded for fixed $\vartheta, R_1, R_2$.
nodes.statement_short: The truncated modulated singular integral is continuous in the frequency, one-sidedly continuous in the radii, and measurable and bounded in $x$.
