nodes.name: wiggle order 1
nodes.statement: If $n\fp \lesssim m\fp'$ and $n' \ge n$ and $m \ge m'$ then $n'\fp \lesssim m'\fp'$.
assumptions:
If $n\fp \lesssim m\fp'$ and
    $n' \ge n$ and $m \ge m'$
nodes.label: wiggle-order-1

nodes.name: Proof of wiggle order 1
nodes.statement: This follows immediately from the definition \eqref{wiggleorder} of $\lesssim$ and the two inclusions $B_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp), n) \subset B_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp), n')$ and $B_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fp'), m') \subset B_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fp'), m)$.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the definition of $\lesssim$ and monotonicity of balls.

nodes.name: wiggle order 2
nodes.statement: Let $n, m \ge 1$ and $k > 0$. If $\fp, \fp' \in \fP$ with $\scI(\fp) \ne \scI(\fp')$ and \begin{equation} n \fp \lesssim k \fp' \end{equation} then \begin{equation} (n + 2^{-95 a} m) \fp \lesssim m\fp'\,. \end{equation}
assumptions: Let $n, m \ge 1$ and $k > 0$.
If $\fp, \fp' \in \fP$ with $\scI(\fp) \ne \scI(\fp')$ and
nodes.label: wiggle-order-2

nodes.name: Equation (217)
nodes.statement: n \fp \lesssim k \fp'
nodes.label: eq-wiggle1

nodes.name: Equation (218)
nodes.statement: (n + 2^{-95 a} m) \fp \lesssim m\fp'\,.
nodes.label: eq-wiggle2

nodes.name: Proof of wiggle order 2
nodes.statement: The assumption \eqref{eq-wiggle1} together with the definition \eqref{wiggleorder} of $\lesssim$ implies that $\scI(\fp) \subsetneq \scI(\fp')$. Let $\mfa \in B_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fp'), m)$. Then we have by the triangle inequality $$ d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp), \mfa) \le d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp), \fcc(\fp')) + d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp'), \mfa) $$ The first summand is bounded by $n$ since $$ \fcc(\fp') \in B_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fp'), k) \subset B_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp), n), $$ using \eqref{wiggleorder}. For the second summand we use \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} to show that the sum is estimated by $$ n + 2^{-95a} d_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fp'), \mfa) < n + 2^{-95a} m\,. $$ Thus $B_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fp'),m) \subset B_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp),n + 2^{-95a}m)$. Combined with $\scI(\fp) \subset \scI(\fp')$, this yields \eqref{eq-wiggle2}.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality in $d_{\fp}$ with \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} for the second term.

nodes.name: wiggle order 3
nodes.statement: The following implications hold for all $\fq, \fq' \in \fP$: \begin{equation} \fq \le \fq' \ \text{and} \ \lambda \ge 1.1 \implies \lambda \fq \lesssim \lambda \fq'\,, \end{equation} \begin{equation} 10\fq \lesssim \fq' \ \text{and} \ \scI(\fq) \ne \scI(\fq') \implies 100 \fq \lesssim 100 \fq'\,, \end{equation} \begin{equation} 2\fq \lesssim \fq' \ \text{and} \ \scI(\fq) \ne \scI(\fq') \implies 4 \fq \lesssim 500 \fq'\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Three implications between the order $\le$ and the relations $\lambda\fq\lesssim\lambda'\fq'$.
nodes.label: wiggle-order-3

nodes.name: Equation (219)
nodes.statement: \fq \le \fq' \ \text{and} \ \lambda \ge 1.1 \implies \lambda \fq \lesssim \lambda \fq'\,,
nodes.label: eq-sc1

nodes.name: Equation (220)
nodes.statement: 10\fq \lesssim \fq' \ \text{and} \ \scI(\fq) \ne \scI(\fq') \implies 100 \fq \lesssim 100 \fq'\,,
nodes.label: eq-sc2

nodes.name: Equation (221)
nodes.statement: 2\fq \lesssim \fq' \ \text{and} \ \scI(\fq) \ne \scI(\fq') \implies 4 \fq \lesssim 500 \fq'\,.
nodes.label: eq-sc3

nodes.name: Proof of wiggle order 3
nodes.statement: \eqref{eq-sc2} and \eqref{eq-sc3} are easy consequences of \Cref{wiggle-order-1}, \Cref{wiggle-order-2} and the fact that $a \ge 4$. For \eqref{eq-sc1}, if $\scI(\fq) = \scI(\fq')$ then we get $\fq = \fq'$ by \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} and \eqref{straightorder}. If $\scI(\fq) \ne \scI(\fq')$, then from \eqref{straightorder}, \eqref{wiggleorder} and \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} it follows that $\fq \lesssim 0.2\fq'$, and \eqref{eq-sc1} follows from an easy calculation using \Cref{wiggle-order-2}.
nodes.statement_short: Consequences of \Cref{wiggle-order-1} and \Cref{wiggle-order-2}; the first with a case split on equal cubes.

nodes.name: convex collection of tiles
Equation (222)
nodes.statement: \fp \le \fp' \le \fp'' \ \text{and} \ \fp, \fp'' \in \mathfrak{A} \implies \fp' \in \mathfrak{A}\,.
nodes.label: eq-convexity

nodes.name: P convex
nodes.statement: For each $k$, the collection $\fP(k)$ is convex.
conclusions: For each $k$, the collection $\fP(k)$ is convex.
nodes.label: P-convex

nodes.name: Proof of P convex
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\fp \le \fp' \le \fp''$ and $\fp, \fp'' \in \fP(k)$. By \eqref{eq-defPk} we have $\scI(\fp), \scI(\fp'') \in \mathcal{C}(G,k)$, so there exists by \eqref{muhj1} some $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $$ \scI(\fp') \subset \scI(\fp'') \subset J $$ and $\mu(G \cap J) > 2^{-k-1} \mu(J)$. Thus \eqref{muhj1} holds for $\scI(\fp')$. On the other hand, by \eqref{muhj2}, there exists no $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $\scI(\fp) \subset J$ and $\mu(G \cap J) > 2^{-k} \mu(J)$. Since $\scI(\fp) \subset \scI(\fp')$, this implies that \eqref{muhj2} holds for $\scI(\fp')$. Hence $\scI(\fp') \in \mathcal{C}(G,k)$, and therefore by \eqref{eq-defPk} $\fp' \in \fP(k)$.
nodes.statement_short: Check both density conditions defining $\mathcal{C}(G,k)$ for the middle cube.

nodes.name: C convex
nodes.statement: For each $k,n$, the collection $\fC(k,n)$ is convex.
conclusions: For each $k,n$, the collection $\fC(k,n)$ is convex.
nodes.label: C-convex

nodes.name: Proof of C convex
nodes.statement: Let $\fp \le \fp' \le \fp''$ with $\fp, \fp'' \in \fC(k,n)$. Then, in particular, $\fp, \fp'' \in \fP(k)$, so, by \Cref{P-convex}, $\fp' \in \fP(k)$. Next, we show that if $\fq \le \fq' \in \fP(k)$ then $\dens'_k(\{\fq\}) \ge \dens_k'(\{\fq'\})$. If $\fp \in \fP(k)$ and $\lambda \ge 2$ with $\lambda \fq' \lesssim \lambda \fp$, then it follows from $\fq \le \fq'$, \eqref{eq-sc1} of \Cref{wiggle-order-3} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ that $\lambda \fq \lesssim \lambda \fp$. Thus the supremum in the definition \eqref{eq-densdef} of $\dens_k'(\{\fq\})$ is over a superset of the set the supremum in the definition of $\dens_k'(\{\fq'\})$ is taken over, which shows $\dens'_k(\{\fq\}) \ge \dens_k'(\{\fq'\})$. From $\fp' \le \fp''$, $\fp'' \in \fC(k,n)$ and \eqref{def-cnk} it then follows that $$ 2^{4a}2^{-n} < \dens_k'(\{\fp''\}) \le \dens_k'(\{\fp'\})\,. $$ Similarly, it follows from $\fp \le \fp'$, $\fp \in \fC(k,n)$ and \eqref{def-cnk} that $$ \dens_k'(\{\fp'\}) \le \dens_k'(\{\fp\}) \le 2^{4a}2^{-n+1}\,. $$ Thus $\fp' \in \fC(k,n)$.

nodes.name: C1 convex
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the collection $\fC_1(k,n,j)$ is convex.
conclusions: For each $k,n,j$, the collection $\fC_1(k,n,j)$ is convex.
nodes.label: C1-convex

nodes.name: Proof of C1 convex
nodes.statement: Let $\fp\le\fp'\le\fp''$ with $\fp, \fp'' \in \fC_1(k,n,j)$. By \Cref{C-convex} and the inclusion $\fC_1(k,n,j) \subset \fC(k,n)$, which holds by definition \eqref{defcnkj}, we have $\fp' \in \fC(k,n)$. By \eqref{eq-sc1} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ we have that $\fq \le \fq'$ and $100 \fq' \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$ imply $100 \fq \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$. So, by \eqref{defbfp}, $\mathfrak{B}(\fp'') \subset \mathfrak{B}(\fp') \subset \mathfrak{B}(\fp)$. Consequently, by \eqref{defcnkj} $$ 2^j \le |\mathfrak{B}(\fp'')|\le |\mathfrak{B}(\fp')| \le |\mathfrak{B}(\fp)| < 2^{j+1}\,, $$ thus $\fp' \in \fC_1(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of $\fC(k,n)$ plus monotonicity of $\mathfrak{B}$ along $\le$.

nodes.name: C2 convex
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the collection $\fC_2(k,n,j)$ is convex.
conclusions: For each $k,n,j$, the collection $\fC_2(k,n,j)$ is convex.
nodes.label: C2-convex

nodes.name: Proof of C2 convex
nodes.statement: Let $\fp \le \fp' \le \fp''$ with $\fp, \fp'' \in \fC_2(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-C2-def}, we have \begin{equation*} \fC_2(k,n,j) \subset \fC_1(k,n,j)\ . \end{equation*} Combined with \Cref{C1-convex}, it follows that $\fp' \in \fC_1(k,n,j)$. If $\fp=\fp'$ the statement is trivially true, otherwise suppose that $\fp' \notin \fC_2(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-C2-def}, this implies that there exists $0 \le l' \le Z(n+1)$ with $\fp' \in \fL_1(k,n,j,l')$. By the definition \eqref{eq-L1-def} of $\fL_1(k,n,j,l')$, this implies that $\fp'$ is minimal with respect to $\le$ in $\fC_1(k,n,j) \setminus \bigcup_{l < l'} \fL_1(k,n,j,l)$. Since $\fp\le\fp'$ and $\fp\in\fC_2(k,n,j)$, $\fp=\fp'$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of $\fC_1$ and minimality of the removed layers.

nodes.name: C3 convex
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the collection $\fC_3(k,n,j)$ is convex.
conclusions: For each $k,n,j$, the collection $\fC_3(k,n,j)$ is convex.
nodes.label: C3-convex

nodes.name: Proof of C3 convex
nodes.statement: Let $\fp \le \fp' \le \fp''$ with $\fp, \fp'' \in \fC_3(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-C3-def} and \Cref{C2-convex} it follows that $\fp' \in \fC_2(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-C3-def} and \eqref{eq-L2-def}, there exists $\fu \in \fU_1(k,n,j)$ with $2\fp'' \lesssim \fu$ and $\scI(\fp'') \subsetneq \scI(\fu)$. From $\fp' \le \fp''$, \eqref{eq-sc1} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ we then have $2\fp' \lesssim \fu$ and $\scI(\fp') \subsetneq \scI(\fu)$, so $\fp' \in \fC_3(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of $\fC_2$ and transfer of $2\fp''\lesssim\fu$ down the order.

nodes.name: C4 convex
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the collection $\fC_4(k,n,j)$ is convex.
conclusions: For each $k,n,j$, the collection $\fC_4(k,n,j)$ is convex.
nodes.label: C4-convex

nodes.name: Proof of C4 convex
nodes.statement: The proof is entirely analogous to \Cref{C2-convex}, substituting $\fC_4$ for $\fC_2$, $\fC_3$ for $\fC_1$ and $\fp'\le\fp''$ for $\fp\le\fp'$.

nodes.name: C5 convex
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the collection $\fC_5(k,n,j)$ is convex.
conclusions: For each $k,n,j$, the collection $\fC_5(k,n,j)$ is convex.
nodes.label: C5-convex

nodes.name: Proof of C5 convex
nodes.statement: Let $\fp \le \fp' \le\fp''$ with $\fp, \fp'' \in \fC_5(k,n,j)$. Then $\fp, \fp'' \in \fC_4(k,n,j)$ by \eqref{defc5}, and thus by \Cref{C4-convex} $\fp' \in \fC_4(k,n,j)$. It suffices to show that if $\fp' \in \fL_4(k,n,j)$ then $\fp \in \fL_4(k,n,j)$ by contraposition; this is true by \eqref{eq-L4-def} and $\fp\le\fp'$.
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of $\fC_4$ and downward closure of $\fL_4$.

nodes.name: dens compare
nodes.statement: We have for every $k\ge 0$ and $\fP'\subset \fP(k)$ \begin{equation} \dens_1(\fP')\le \dens_k'(\fP')\, . \end{equation}
assumptions: We have for every $k\ge 0$ and $\fP'\subset \fP(k)$
nodes.label: dens-compare

nodes.name: Equation (223)
nodes.statement: \dens_1(\fP')\le \dens_k'(\fP')\, .

nodes.name: Proof of dens compare
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that for all $\fp'\in \fP'$ and $\lambda\ge 2$ and $\fp\in \fP(\fP')$ with $\lambda \fp' \lesssim \lambda \fp$ we have \begin{equation} \frac{\mu({E}_2(\lambda, \fp))}{\mu(\scI(\fp))} \le \sup_{\fp'' \in \fP(k): \lambda \fp' \lesssim \lambda \fp''} \frac{\mu({E}_2(\lambda, \fp''))}{\mu(\scI(\fp''))}. \end{equation} Let such $\fp'$, $\lambda$, $\fp$ be given. It suffices to show that $\fp\in \fP(k)$, that is, it satisfies \eqref{muhj1} and \eqref{muhj2}. We show \eqref{muhj1}. As $\fp\in \fP(\fP')$, there exists $\fp''\in \fP'$ with $\scI(\fp')\subset \scI(\fp'')$. By assumption on $\fP'$, we have $\fp''\in \fP(k)$ and there exists $J\in \mathcal{D}$ with $\scI(\fp'')\subset J$ and \begin{equation} \mu(G\cap J)>2^{-k-1} \mu(J). \end{equation} Then also $\scI(\fp')\subset J$, which proves \eqref{muhj1} for $\fp$. We show \eqref{muhj2}. Assume to get a contradiction that there exists $J\in \mathcal{D}$ with $\scI(\fp)\subset J$ and \begin{equation} \mu(G\cap J)>2^{-k} \mu(J). \end{equation} As $\lambda\fp'\lesssim \lambda\fp$, we have $\scI(\fp')\subset \scI(\fp)$, and therefore $\scI(\fp')\subset J$. This contradicts $\fp'\in \fP'\subset \fP(k)$. This proves \eqref{muhj2} for $\fp$.
nodes.statement_short: Show each competitor in $\dens_1$ lies in $\fP(k)$ by checking the two density conditions.

nodes.name: Equation (224)
nodes.statement: \frac{\mu({E}_2(\lambda, \fp))}{\mu(\scI(\fp))} \le \sup_{\fp'' \in \fP(k): \lambda \fp' \lesssim \lambda \fp''} \frac{\mu({E}_2(\lambda, \fp''))}{\mu(\scI(\fp''))}.

nodes.name: Equation (225)
nodes.statement: \mu(G\cap J)>2^{-k-1} \mu(J).

nodes.name: Equation (226)
nodes.statement: \mu(G\cap J)>2^{-k} \mu(J).
nodes.label: mugj

nodes.name: C dens1
nodes.statement: For each set $\mathfrak{A} \subset \mathfrak{C}(k,n)$, we have $$ \dens_1(\mathfrak{A}) \le 2^{4a}2^{-n+1}\,. $$
assumptions: For each set $\mathfrak{A} \subset \mathfrak{C}(k,n)$
nodes.label: C-dens1

nodes.name: Proof of C dens1
nodes.statement: We have by \Cref{dens-compare} that $\dens_1(\mathfrak{A}) \le \dens_k'(\mathfrak{A})$. Since $\mathfrak{A} \subset \fC(k,n)$, it follows from monotonicity of suprema and the definition \eqref{eq-densdef} that $ \dens_k'(\mathfrak{A}) \le \dens_k'(\fC(k,n))\,. $ By \eqref{eq-densdef} and \eqref{def-cnk}, we have $$ \dens_k'(\fC(k,n)) = \sup_{\fp \in \fC(k,n)} \dens_k'(\{\fp\}) \le 2^{4a}2^{-n+1}\,. $$
nodes.statement_short: Compare with $\dens_k'$ by \Cref{dens-compare} and use the definition of $\fC(k,n)$.

nodes.name: set $\fC_6(k,n,j)$
nodes.statement:
Define
$$
    \fC_6(k,n,j)
$$
to be the set of all tiles $\fp \in \fC_5(k,n,j)$ such that $\scI(\fp) \not\subset G'$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: trees $\mathfrak{T}_1(\fu)$
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Equation (227)
nodes.statement: \mathfrak{T}_1(\fu):= \{\fp \in \fC_1(k,n,j) \ : \scI(\fp)\neq \scI(\fu), \ 2\fp \lesssim \fu\}\,.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: eq-T1-def

nodes.name: set $\fU_2(k,n,j)$
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Equation (228)
nodes.statement: \fU_2(k,n,j) := \{ \fu \in \fU_1(k,n,j) \, : \, \mathfrak{T}_1(\fu) \cap \fC_6(k,n,j) \ne \emptyset\}\,.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: eq-U2-def

nodes.name: relation $\sim$ on $\fU_2$
nodes.statement:
Define a relation $\sim$ on $\fU_2(k,n,j)$
by setting $\fu\sim \fu'$
for $\fu,\fu'\in \fU_2(k,n,j)$
if $\fu=\fu'$ or there exists $\fp$ in $\mathfrak{T}_1(\fu)$
with $10 \fp\lesssim \fu'$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: relation geometry
nodes.statement: If $\fu \sim \fu'$, then $\scI(u) = \scI(u')$ and \begin{equation*} B_{\fu}(\fcc(\fu), 100) \cap B_{\fu'}(\fcc(\fu'), 100) \neq \emptyset\ . \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
assumptions: If $\fu \sim \fu'$
nodes.label: relation-geometry

nodes.name: Proof of relation geometry
nodes.statement: Let $\fu, \fu' \in \fU_2(k,n,j)$ with $\fu \sim \fu'$. If $\fu = \fu'$ then the conclusion of the Lemma clearly holds. Else, there exists $\fp \in \fC_1(k,n,j)$ such that $\scI(\fp) \ne \scI(\fu)$ and $2 \fp \lesssim \fu$ and $10 \fp \lesssim \fu'$. Using \Cref{wiggle-order-1} and \eqref{eq-sc2} of \Cref{wiggle-order-3}, we deduce that \begin{equation} 100 \fp\lesssim 100 \fu\,, \qquad 100 \fp \lesssim 100\fu'\,. \end{equation} Now suppose that $B_{\fu}(\fcc(\fu), 100) \cap B_{\fu'}(\fcc(\fu'), 100) = \emptyset$. Then we have $\mathfrak{B}(\fu) \cap \mathfrak{B}(\fu') = \emptyset$, by the definition \eqref{defbfp} of $\mathfrak{B}$ and the definition \eqref{wiggleorder} of $\lesssim$, but also $\mathfrak{B}(\fu) \subset \mathfrak{B}(\fp)$ and $\mathfrak{B}(\fu') \subset \mathfrak{B}(\fp)$, by \eqref{defbfp}, \eqref{wiggleorder} and \eqref{eq-Fefferman-trick0}. Hence, $$ |\mathfrak{B}(\fp)| \geq |\mathfrak{B}(\fu)| + |\mathfrak{B}(\fu')| \geq 2^{j} + 2^j = 2^{j+1}\,, $$ which contradicts $\fp \in \fC_1(k,n,j)$. Therefore we must have \begin{equation*} B_{\fu}(\fcc(\fu), 100) \cap B_{\fu'}(\fcc(\fu'), 100) \ne \emptyset\, . \end{equation*} It follows from $2\fp \lesssim \fu$ and $10\fp \lesssim \fu'$ that $\scI(\fp) \subset \scI(\fu)$ and $\scI(\fp) \subset \scI(\fu')$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, it follows that $\scI(\fu)$ and $\scI(\fu')$ are nested. Combining this with the conclusion of the last paragraph and definition \eqref{defunkj} of $\fU_1(k,n,j)$, we obtain that $\scI(\fu) = \scI(\fu')$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Fefferman's counting trick: disjoint $100$-balls would give $|\mathfrak{B}(\fp)|\ge 2^{j+1}$, contradicting $\fp\in\fC_1(k,n,j)$; nested cubes then coincide by the definition of $\fU_1$.

nodes.name: Equation (229)
nodes.statement: 100 \fp\lesssim 100 \fu\,, \qquad 100 \fp \lesssim 100\fu'\,.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: eq-Fefferman-trick0

nodes.name: equivalence relation
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the relation $\sim$ on $\fU_2(k,n,j)$ is an equivalence relation.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
conclusions:
the relation $\sim$ on
$\fU_2(k,n,j)$ is an equivalence relation.
nodes.label: equivalence-relation

nodes.name: Proof of equivalence relation
nodes.statement:
Reflexivity holds by definition. For transitivity, suppose that  egin{equation*}  u,  u',  u'' \in  U_1(k,n,j) \end{equation*} and $ u \sim  u'$, $ u' \sim  u''$. By \Cref{relation-geometry}, it follows that $\scI( u) =\scI( u') = \scI( u'')$, that there exists  egin{equation*} \mfa \in B_{ u}( cc( u), 100) \cap B_{ u'}( cc( u'), 100) \end{equation*} and that there exists  egin{equation*} \mfb \in B_{ u'}( cc( u'), 100) \cap B_{ u''}( cc( u''), 100)\, . \end{equation*} If $ u =  u'$, then $ u \sim  u''$ holds by assumption. Else, there exists by the definition of $\sim$ some $ p \in \mathfrak{T}_1( u)$ with $10 p\lesssim  u'$. Then we have $2 p \lesssim  u$ and $ p 
e  u$ by definition of $\mathfrak{T}_1( u)$, so $4  p \lesssim 500  u$ by \eqref{eq-sc3}. For $q \in B_{ u''}( cc( u''), 1)$ it follows by the triangle inequality that  egin{align*} d_{ u}( cc( u), q) &\le d_{ u}( cc( u), \mfa) + d_{ u}(\mfa,  cc( u'))\ &\quad+ d_{ u}( cc( u'), \mfb) + d_{ u}(\mfb,  cc( u'')) + d_{ u}( cc( u''), q)\,. \end{align*} Using \eqref{defdp} and the fact that $\scI( u) = \scI( u') = \scI( u'')$ this equals  egin{align*} &\quad d_{ u}( cc( u), \mfa) + d_{ u'}(\mfa,  cc( u'))\ &\quad+ d_{ u'}( cc( u'), \mfb) + d_{ u''}(\mfb,  cc( u'')) + d_{ u''}( cc( u''), q)\ &< 100 + 100 + 100 + 100 + 1 < 500\,. \end{align*} Since $4 p \lesssim 500  u$, it follows that $d_{ p}( cc( p), q) < 4 < 10$. We have shown that $B_{ u''}( cc( u''), 1) \subset B_{ p}( cc( p), 10)$, combining this with $\scI( u'') = \scI( u)$ gives $ u \sim  u''$. For symmetry suppose that $ u \sim  u'$. By Lemma \eqref{relation-geometry}, it follows that $\scI( u) = \scI( u')$ and that there exists $\mfa \in B_{ u}( cc( u), 100) \cap B_{ u'}( cc( u'), 100)$. Again, for $ u =  u'$ symmetry is obvious, so suppose that $ u 
e  u'$. There exists $ p \in \mathfrak{T}_1( u')$, which then satisfies $2 p\lesssim  u'$ and $\scI( p) 
eq \scI( u')$. By \Cref{wiggle-order-1} and \eqref{eq-sc3}, it follows that  egin{equation} 10 p \lesssim 4 p \lesssim 500  u'\,. \end{equation} If $q \in B_{ u}( cc( u),1)$ then we have from the triangle inequality and the fact that $\scI( u) = \scI( u')$:  egin{align*} d_{ u'}( cc( u'), q) &\le d_{ u'}( cc( u'), \mfa) + d_{ u'}(\mfa,  cc( u)) + d_{ u'}( cc( u), q)\ &= d_{ u'}( cc( u'), \mfa) + d_{ u}(\mfa,  cc( u)) + d_{ u}( cc( u), q)\ &< 100 + 100 + 1 < 500\,. \end{align*} Combining this with \eqref{eq-rel1} and \eqref{wiggleorder}, we get  egin{equation*} B_{ u}( cc( u), 1) \subset B_{ p}( cc( p), 10)\, . \end{equation*} Since $2 p \lesssim  u'$, we have $\scI( p) \subset \scI( u') = \scI( u)$. Thus, $10 p \lesssim  u$ which completes the proof of $ u' \sim  u$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Reflexivity by definition; transitivity and symmetry via \Cref{relation-geometry} and chains of triangle inequalities in $d_{\fu}$.

nodes.name: Equation (230)
nodes.statement: 10\fp \lesssim 4\fp \lesssim 500 \fu'\,.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: eq-rel1

nodes.name: representatives $\fU_3(k,n,j)$
nodes.statement:
Choose a set $\fU_3(k,n,j)$ of representatives for the equivalence
classes of $\sim$ in $\fU_2(k,n,j)$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: trees $\fT_2(\fu)$
nodes.statement:
Define for each $\fu\in \fU_3(k,n,j)$
\begin{equation} \fT_2(\fu):=
   \bigcup_{\fu\sim \fu'}\mathfrak{T}_1(\fu')\cap \fC_6(k,n,j)\, .
\end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Equation (231)
nodes.statement: \fT_2(\fu):= \bigcup_{\fu\sim \fu'}\mathfrak{T}_1(\fu')\cap \fC_6(k,n,j)\, .
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: definesv

nodes.name: C6 forest
nodes.statement: We have \begin{equation} \fC_6(k,n,j)=\bigcup_{\fu\in \fU_3(k,n,j)}\mathfrak{T}_2(\fu)\, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.statement_short: $\fC_6(k,n,j)$ is the union of the trees $\fT_2(\fu)$, $\fu\in\fU_3(k,n,j)$.
nodes.label: C6-forest

nodes.name: Equation (232)
nodes.statement: \fC_6(k,n,j)=\bigcup_{\fu\in \fU_3(k,n,j)}\mathfrak{T}_2(\fu)\, .
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Proof of C6 forest
nodes.statement: Let $\fp \in \fC_6(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-C4-def} and \eqref{defc5}, we have $\fp \in \fC_3(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-L2-def} and \eqref{eq-C3-def}, there exists $\fu \in \fU_1(k,n,j)$ with $2\fp \lesssim \fu$ and $\scI(\fp) \ne \scI(\fu)$, that is, with $\fp \in \mathfrak{T}_1(\fu)$. Then $\mathfrak{T}_1(\fu)$ is clearly nonempty, so $\fu \in \fU_2(k,n,j)$. By the definition of $\fU_3(k,n,j)$, there exists $\fu' \in \fU_3(k,n,j)$ with $\fu \sim \fu'$. By \eqref{definesv}, we have $\fp \in \mathfrak{T}_2(\fu')$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Each tile of $\fC_6$ lies in some $\mathfrak{T}_1(\fu)$ and hence in the tree of its representative.

nodes.name: forest geometry
nodes.statement: For each $\fu\in \fU_3(k,n,j)$, the set $\mathfrak{T}_2(\fu)$ satisfies \eqref{forest1}.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: forest-geometry

nodes.name: Proof of forest geometry
nodes.statement: Let $\fp \in \mathfrak{T}_2(\fu)$. By \eqref{definesv}, there exists $\fu' \sim \fu$ with $\fp \in \mathfrak{T}_1(\fu')$. Then we have $2\fp \lesssim \fu'$ and $\scI(\fp) \ne \scI(\fu')$, so by \eqref{eq-sc3} $4\fp \lesssim 500\fu'$. Further, by \Cref{relation-geometry}, we have that $\scI(\fu') = \scI(\fu)$ and there exists $\mfa \in B_{\fu'}(\fcc(\fu'),100) \cap B_{\fu}(\fcc(\fu),100)$. Let $\mfb \in B_{\fu}(\fcc(\fu), 1)$. Using the triangle inequality and the fact that $\scI(\fu') =\scI(\fu)$, we obtain \begin{align*} d_{\fu'}(\fcc(\fu'), \mfb) &\le d_{\fu'}(\fcc(\fu'), \mfa) + d_{\fu'}(\fcc(\fu), \mfa) + d_{\fu'}(\fcc(\fu), \mfb)\\ &= d_{\fu'}(\fcc(\fu'), \mfa) + d_{\fu}(\fcc(\fu), \mfa) + d_{\fu}(\fcc(\fu), \mfb)\\ &< 100 + 100 + 1 < 500\,. \end{align*} Combining this with $4\fp \lesssim 500\fu'$, we obtain $$ B_{\fu}(\fcc(\fu), 1) \subset B_{\fu'}(\fcc(\fu'), 500) \subset B_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp), 4)\,. $$ Together with $\scI(\fp) \subset \scI(\fu') = \scI(\fu)$, this gives $4\fp \lesssim \fu$, which is \eqref{forest1}.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Transfer $4\fp\lesssim 500\fu'$ to $\fu$ using \Cref{relation-geometry} and the triangle inequality.

nodes.name: forest convex
nodes.statement: For each $\fu\in \fU_3(k,n,j)$, the set $\mathfrak{T}_2(\fu)$ satisfies the convexity condition \eqref{forest2}.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: forest-convex

nodes.name: Proof of forest convex
nodes.statement:
Let $ p,  p'' \in \mathfrak{T}_2( u)$ and $ p' \in  P$ with $ p \le  p' \le  p''$. By \eqref{definesv} we have $ p,  p'' \in  C_6(k,n,j) \subset  C_5(k,n,j)$. By \Cref{C5-convex}, we have $ p' \in  C_5(k,n,j)$. Since $ p \in  C_6(k,n,j)$ we have $\scI( p) 
ot \subset G'$, so $\scI( p') 
ot \subset G'$ and therefore also $ p' \in  C_6(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{definesv} there exists $ u' \in  U_2(k,n,j)$ with $ p'' \in \mathfrak{T}_1( u')$ and hence $2 p'' \lesssim  u'$ and $\scI( p'') 
e \scI( u')$. Together this implies $\scI( p'') \subsetneq \scI( u')$. With the inclusion $\scI( p') \subset \scI( p'')$ from $ p' \le  p''$, it follows that $\scI( p') \subsetneq \scI( u')$ and hence $\scI( p') 
e \scI( u')$. By \eqref{eq-sc1} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ we further have $2 p' \lesssim  u'$, so $ p' \in \mathfrak{T}_1( u')$. It follows that $ p' \in \mathfrak{T}_2( u)$, which shows \eqref{forest2}.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of $\fC_5$ (\Cref{C5-convex}) and transfer of $2\fp''\lesssim\fu'$ to the middle tile.

nodes.name: forest separation
nodes.statement: For each $\fu,\fu'\in \fU_3(k,n,j)$ with $\fu\neq \fu'$ and each $\fp \in \fT_2(\fu)$ with $\scI(\fp)\subset \scI(\fu')$ we have \begin{equation} d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp), \fcc(\fu')) > 2^{Z(n+1)}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
assumptions: For each $\fu,\fu'\in \fU_3(k,n,j)$ with $\fu\neq \fu'$ and each $\fp \in \fT_2(\fu)$ with $\scI(\fp)\subset \scI(\fu')$
nodes.label: forest-separation

nodes.name: Equation (233)
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Proof of forest separation
nodes.statement:
By the definition \eqref{eq-C2-def} of $ C_2(k,n,j)$, there exists a tile $ p' \in  C_1(k,n,j)$ with $ p' \le  p$ and $\ps( p') \le \ps( p)- Z(n+1)$. By \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} we have $$ d_{ p}( cc( p),  cc( u')) \ge 2^{95a Z(n+1)} d_{ p'}( cc( p),  cc( u'))\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-sc1} we have $2 p' \lesssim 2 p$, so by transitivity of $\lesssim$ there exists $\mathfrak{v} \sim  u$ with $2 p' \lesssim \mathfrak{v}$ and $\scI( p') 
e \scI(\mathfrak{v})$. Since $ u,  u'$ are not equivalent under $\sim$, we have $\mathfrak{v} 
ot \sim  u'$, thus $10 p' 
ot\lesssim  u'$. This implies that there exists $q \in B_{ u'}( cc( u'), 1) \setminus B_{ p'}( cc( p'), 10)$. From $ p' \le  p$, $\scI( p') \subset \scI( p) \subset \scI( u')$ and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} it then follows that  egin{align*} &\quad d_{ p'}( cc( p),  cc( u'))\ &\ge -d_{ p'}( cc( p),  cc( p')) + d_{ p'}( cc( p'), q) - d_{ p'}(q,  cc( u'))\ &\ge -d_{ p'}( cc( p),  cc( p')) + d_{ p'}( cc( p'), q) - d_{ u'}(q,  cc( u'))\ &> -1 + 10 - 1 = 8\,. \end{align*} The lemma follows by combining the two displays with the fact that $95 a \ge 1$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.statement_short: A lower tile $\fp'$ many scales below is far from $\fu'$ in frequency since $\fu,\fu'$ are inequivalent; \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} amplifies this.

nodes.name: forest inner
nodes.statement: For each $\fu\in \fU_3(k,n,j)$ and each $\fp \in \mathfrak{T}_2(\fu)$ we have \begin{equation} B(\pc(\fp), 8 D^{\ps(\fp)}) \subset \scI(\fu). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: forest-inner

nodes.name: Equation (234)
nodes.statement: B(\pc(\fp), 8 D^{\ps(\fp)}) \subset \scI(\fu).
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Proof of forest inner
nodes.statement: Let $\fp \in \mathfrak{T}_2(\fu)$. Then $\fp \in \fC_4(k,n,j)$, hence there exists a chain $$ \fp \le \fp_{Z(n+1)} \le \dotsb \le \fp_0 $$ of distinct tiles in $\fC_3(n,k,j)$. We pick such a chain and set $\fq = \fp_0$. Then we have from distinctness of the tiles in the chain that $\ps(\fp) \le \ps(\fq) - Z(n+1)$. By \eqref{eq-C3-def} there exists $\fu'' \in \fU_1(k,n,j)$ with $2\fq \lesssim \fu''$ and $\ps(\fq) < \ps(\fu'')$. Then we have in particular by \Cref{wiggle-order-1} that $10 \fp \lesssim \fu''$. Let $\fu' \sim \fu$ be such that $\fp \in \mathfrak{T}_1(\fu')$. By the definition of $\sim$, it follows that $\fu' \sim \fu''$. By transitivity of $\sim$, we have $\fu \sim \fu''$. By \Cref{relation-geometry}, we have $\ps(\fu'') = \ps(\fu)$, hence $\ps(\fq) < \ps(\fu)$ and $\ps(\fp) \le \ps(\fq) - Z(n+1) \le \ps(\fu) - Z(n+1) - 1$. Thus, there exists some cube $I \in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(I) = \ps(\fu) - Z(n+1) - 1$ and $I \subset \scI(\fu)$ and $\scI(\fp) \subset I$. Since $\fp \in \fC_5(k,n,j)$, we have that $I \notin \mathcal{L}(\fu)$, so $B(c(I), 8D^{s(I)}) \subset \scI(\fu)$. By the triangle inequality, \eqref{defineD} and $a \ge 4$, the same then holds for the subcube $\scI(\fp) \subset I$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.statement_short: A long chain above $\fp$ in $\fC_3$ shows $\fp$ is many scales below the top; then $\fp\notin\fL_4$ keeps its ball inside $\scI(\fu)$.

nodes.name: forest stacking
nodes.statement: It holds for $k\le n$ that \begin{equation} \sum_{\fu \in \fU_3(k,n,j)} \mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fu)} \le (4n+12)2^{n}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
assumptions: for $k\le n$
nodes.label: forest-stacking

nodes.name: Equation (235)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\fu \in \fU_3(k,n,j)} \mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fu)} \le (4n+12)2^{n}\,.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Proof of forest stacking
nodes.statement: Suppose that a point $x$ is contained in more than $(4n + 12)2^n$ cubes $\scI(\fu)$ with $\fu \in \fU_3(k,n,j)$. Since $\fU_3(k,n,j) \subset \fC_1(k,n,j)$ for each such $\fu$, there exists $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ such that $100\fu \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$. We fix such an $\mathfrak{m}(\fu) := \mathfrak{m}$ for each $\fu$, and claim that the map $\fu \mapsto\mathfrak{m}(\fu)$ is injective. Indeed, assume for $\fu\neq \fu'$ there is $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ such that $100\fu \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$ and $100\fu' \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, either $\scI(\fu) \subset \scI(\fu')$ or $\scI(\fu') \subset \scI(\fu)$. By \eqref{defunkj}, $B_{\fu}(\fcc(\fu),100) \cap B_{\fu'}(\fcc(\fu'), 100) = \emptyset$. This contradicts $\Omega(\mathfrak{m})$ being contained in both sets by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}. Thus $x$ is contained in more than $(4n + 12)2^n$ cubes $\scI(\mathfrak{m})$, $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$. Consequently, we have by \eqref{eq-Aoverlap-def} that $x \in A(2n + 6, k,n) \subset G_2$. Let $\scI(\fu)$ be an inclusion minimal cube among the $\scI(\fu'), \fu' \in \fU_3(k,n,j)$ with $x \in \scI(\fu)$. By the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have $\scI(\fu) \subset \scI(\fu')$ for all cubes $\scI(\fu')$ containing $x$. Thus $$ \scI(\fu) \subset \{y \ : \ \sum_{\fu \in \fU_3(k,n,j)} \mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fu)}(y) > 1 + (4n+12)2^{n}\} \subset G_2\,. $$ Thus $\mathfrak{T}_1(\fu) \cap \fC_6(k,n,j) = \emptyset$. This contradicts $\fu \in \fU_2(k,n,j)$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: high overlap of tree tops forces high overlap of maximal tiles, placing the minimal top cube inside $G_2$.

nodes.name: Proof of forest union
nodes.statement: We first fix $k,n, j$. By \eqref{definetp} and \eqref{defineep}, we have that $\mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fp)} T_{\fp}f(x) = T_{\fp}f(x)$ and hence $\mathbf{1}_{G \setminus G'} T_{\fp}f(x)= 0$ for all $\fp \in \fC_5(k,n,j) \setminus \fC_6(k,n,j)$. Thus it suffices to estimate the contribution of the sets $\fC_6(k,n,j)$. By \Cref{forest-stacking}, we can decompose $\fU_3(k,n,j)$ as a disjoint union of at most $4n + 12$ collections $\fU_4(k,n,j,l)$, $1 \le l \le 4n+12$, each satisfying $$ \sum_{\fu \in \fU_4(k,n,j,l)} \mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fu)} \le 2^n\,. $$ By Lemmas \ref{forest-geometry}, \ref{forest-convex}, \ref{forest-separation}, \ref{forest-inner} and \ref{C-dens1}, the pairs $$ (\fU_4(k,n,j,l), \mathfrak{T}_2|_{\fU_4(k,n,j,l)}) $$ are $n$-forests for each $k,n,j,l$, and by \Cref{C6-forest}, we have $$ \fC_6(k,n,j) = \bigcup_{l = 1}^{4n + 12} \bigcup_{\fu \in \fU_4(k,n,j,l)} \mathfrak{T}_2(\fu)\,. $$ Since $\scI(\fp) \not\subset G_1$ for all $\fp \in \fC_6(k,n,j)$, we have $\fC_6(k,n,j) \cap \fP_{F,G} = \emptyset$ and hence $$ \dens_2(\bigcup_{\fu \in \fU_4(k,n,j,l)} \mathfrak{T}_2(\fu)) \le 2^{2a + 5} \frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)}\,. $$ Using the triangle inequality according to the splitting by $k,n,j$ and $l$ in \eqref{disclesssim1} and applying \Cref{forest-operator} to each term, we obtain the estimate $$ \sum_{k \ge 0}\sum_{n \ge k} (2n+3)(4n+12) 2^{440a^3}2^{-(1-\frac{1}{q})n}(2^{2a+5} \frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)})^{\frac{1}{q} - \frac{1}{2}} \|f\|_2 \|\mathbf{1}_{G\setminus G'}\|_2 $$ for the left hand side of \eqref{disclesssim1}. Since $|f| \le \mathbf{1}_F$, we have $\|f\|_2 \le \mu(F)^{1/2}$, and we have $\|\mathbf{1}_{G\setminus G'}\|_2 \le \mu(G)^{1/2}$. We get a bound $$ 2^{440a^3} \mu(F)^{\frac{1}{q}} \mu(G)^{1 -\frac{1}{q}} 2^{2a+5}\sum_{k \ge 0}\sum_{n \ge k}(2n+3)(4n+12) 2^{-(1-\frac{1}{q})n}\,. $$ Interchanging the order of summation, the last factor equals $$ 2^{2a+5} \sum_{n \ge 0} (2n+3)(4n+12) (n+1) 2^{-\frac{q-1}{q}n}\,. $$ Up to an explicit constant, the sum is bounded by $\sum n^3 2^{-\frac{q-1}{q}n}$, which is at most some constant times $1/(q-1)^4$ by comparing to an integral. Since $a \ge 4$, this is overall bounded by $2^{a^3}/(q-1)^4$, which completes the proof of the lemma.

nodes.statement_short: Decompose $\fC_6(k,n,j)$ into $4n+12$ $n$-forests, apply \Cref{forest-operator} to each, and sum over $k,n,j,l$.

nodes.name: Proof of antichain decomposition
nodes.statement: Let $\fp \in \fP_2 \cap \fP_{G \setminus G'}$. Clearly, for every cube $J = \scI(\fp)$ with $\fp \in \fP_{G \setminus G'}$ there exists some $k \ge 0$ such that \eqref{muhj1} holds, and for no cube $J \in \mathcal{D}$ and no $k < 0$ does \eqref{muhj2} hold. Thus $\fp \in \fP(k)$ for some $k \ge 0$. Next, since $E_2(\lambda, \fp') \subset \scI(\fp')\cap G$ for every $\lambda \ge 2$ and every tile $\fp' \in \fP(k)$ with $\lambda\fp \lesssim \lambda \fp'$, it follows from \eqref{muhj2} that $\mu(E_2(\lambda, \fp')) \le 2^{-k} \mu(\scI(\fp'))$ for every such $\fp'$, so $\dens_k'(\{\fp\}) \le 2^{-k}$. Combining this with $a \ge 0$, it follows from \eqref{def-cnk} that there exists $n\ge k$ with $\fp \in \fC(k,n)$. Since $\fp \in \fP_{G \setminus G'}$, we have in particular $\scI(\fp) \not \subset A(2n + 6, k, n)$, so there exist at most $1 + (4n + 12)2^n < 2^{2n+4}$ tiles $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ with $\fp \le \mathfrak{m}$. It follows that $\fp \in \fL_0(k,n)$ or $\fp \in \fC_1(k,n,j)$ for some $1 \le j \le 2n + 3$. In the former case we are done, in the latter case the equality to be shown follows from the definitions of the collections $\fC_i$ and $\fL_i$.
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Locate each tile in some $\fP(k)$ and $\fC(k,n)$, then in $\fL_0$ or some $\fC_1(k,n,j)$ using that it is not inside $G_2$.

nodes.name: L0 antichain
nodes.statement: We have that $$ \fL_0(k,n) = \dot{\bigcup_{0 \le l < n}} \fL_0(k,n,l)\,, $$ where each $\fL_0(k,n,l)$ is an antichain.

nodes.name: Proof of L0 antichain
nodes.statement:
It suffices to show that $ L_0(k,n)$ contains no chain of length $n + 1$. Suppose that we had such a chain $ p_0 \le  p_1 \le \dotsb \le  p_{n}$ with $ p_i 
e  p_{i+1}$ for $i =0, \dotsc, n-1$. By \eqref{def-cnk}, we have that $\dens_k'(\{ p_n\}) > 2^{-n}$. Thus, by \eqref{eq-densdef}, there exists $ p' \in  P(k)$ and $\lambda \ge 2$ with $\lambda  p_n \le \lambda  p'$ and  egin{equation}  rac{\mu(E_2(\lambda,  p'))}{\mu(\scI( p'))} > \lambda^{a} 2^{4a} 2^{-n}\,. \end{equation} Let $\mathfrak{O}$ be the set of all $ p'' \in  P(k)$ such that we have $ \scI( p'') = \scI( p')$ and $B_{ p'}( cc( p'), \lambda) \cap \Omega( p'') 
eq \emptyset$. We now show that  egin{equation} |\mathfrak{O}| \le 2^{4a}\lambda^a\,. \end{equation} The balls $B_{ p'}( cc( p''), 0.2)$, $ p'' \in \mathfrak{O}$ are disjoint by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}, and by the triangle inequality contained in $B_{ p'}( cc( p'), \lambda+1.2)$. By assumption \eqref{thirddb} on $\Theta$, this ball can be covered with $$ 2^{a\lceil \log_2(\lambda+1.2) + \log_2(5)ceil} \le 2^{a(\log_2(\lambda) + 4)} = 2^{4a}\lambda^a $$ many $d_{ p'}$-balls of radius $0.2$. Here we have used that for $\lambda \ge 2$ $$ \lceil \log_2(\lambda + 1.2) + \log_2(5) ceil \le 1+ \log_2(1.6 \lambda) + \log_2(5) = 4 + \log_2(\lambda)\,. $$ By the triangle inequality, each such ball contains at most one $ cc( p'')$, and each $ cc( p'')$ is contained in one of the balls. Thus we get \eqref{eq-O-bound}. By \eqref{definee1} and \eqref{definee2} we have $E_2(\lambda,  p') \subset  igcup_{ p'' \in \mathfrak{O}} E_1( p'')$, thus $$ 2^{4a}\lambda^a 2^{-n} < \sum_{ p'' \in \mathfrak{O}}  rac{\mu(E_1( p''))}{\mu(\scI( p''))}\,. $$ Hence there exists a tile $ p'' \in \mathfrak{O}$ with  egin{equation*} \mu(E_1( p'')) \ge 2^{-n} \mu(\scI( p'))\,. \end{equation*} By the definition \eqref{mnkmax} of $\mathfrak{M}(k,n)$, there exists a tile $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ with $ p' \leq \mathfrak{m}$. From \eqref{eq-p'}, the inclusion $E_2(\lambda,  p') \subset \scI( p')$ and $a\ge 1$ we obtain $$ 2^n \geq 2^{4a} \lambda^{a} \geq \lambda\,. $$ From the triangle inequality, \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and $a \ge 1$, we now obtain for all $\mfa \in B_{\mathfrak{m}}( cc(\mathfrak{m}), 1)$ that  egin{align*} &\quad d_{ p_0}( cc( p_0), \mfa)\ &\leq d_{ p_0}( cc( p_0),  cc( p_{n})) + d_{ p_0}( cc( p_{n}),  cc( p')) + d_{ p_0}( cc( p'),  cc( p''))\ &\quad+ d_{ p_0}( cc( p''),  cc(\mathfrak{m})) + d_{ p_0}( cc(\mathfrak{m}), \mfa)\ &\leq 1 + 2^{-95an} (d_{ p_{n}}( cc( p_n),  cc( p')) + d_{ p'}( cc( p'),  cc( p''))\ &\quad+ d_{ p''}( cc( p''),  cc(\mathfrak{m})) + d_{\mathfrak{m}}( cc(\mathfrak{m}), \mfa))\ &\leq 1 + 2^{-95an}(\lambda + (\lambda + 1) + 1 + 1) \leq 100\,. \end{align*} Thus, by \eqref{straightorder}, $100 p_0 \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$, a contradiction to $ p_0 
otin  C(k,n)$.
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma
nodes.statement_short: A chain of length $n+1$ in $\fL_0$ would, via a dense tile $\fp'$ and a counting bound, place $\fp_0$ below a maximal tile with $100\fp_0\lesssim\mathfrak{m}$, a contradiction.

nodes.name: Proof of L2 antichain
nodes.statement:
Suppose that there are $ p_0,  p_1 \in  L_2(k,n,j)$ with $ p_0 
e  p_1$ and $ p_0 \le  p_1$. By \Cref{wiggle-order-1} and \Cref{wiggle-order-2}, it follows that $2 p_0 \lesssim 200 p_1$. Since $ L_2(k,n,j)$ is finite, there exists a maximal $l \ge 1$ such that there exists a chain $2 p_0 \lesssim 200  p_1 \lesssim \dotsb \lesssim 200  p_l$ with all $ p_i$ in $ C_1(k,n,j)$ and $ p_i 
e  p_{i+1}$ for $i = 0, \dotsc, l-1$. If we have $ p_l \in  U_1(k,n,j)$, then it follows from $2 p_0 \lesssim 200  p_l \lesssim  p_l$ and \eqref{eq-L2-def} that $ p_0 
ot\in  L_2(k,n,j)$, a contradiction. Thus, by the definition \eqref{defunkj} of $ U_1(k,n,j)$, there exists $ p_{l+1} \in  C_1(k,n,j)$ with $\scI( p_l) \subsetneq \scI( p_{l+1}) $ and $\mfa \in B_{ p_l}( cc( p_l), 100) \cap B_{ p_{l+1}}( cc( p_{l+1}), 100)$. Using the triangle inequality and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}, one deduces that $200  p_l \lesssim 200 p_{l+1}$. This contradicts maximality of $l$.

nodes.statement_short: A maximal chain argument with \Cref{wiggle-order-1}, \Cref{wiggle-order-2} and the definition of $\fU_1$ leads to a contradiction.

nodes.name: Proof of L1 L3 antichain
nodes.statement: By its definition \eqref{eq-L1-def}, each set $\fL_1(k,n,j,l)$ is a set of minimal elements in some set of tiles with respect to $\le$. If there were distinct $\fp, \fq \in \fL_1(k,n,j,l)$ with $\fp \le \fq$, then $\fq$ would not be minimal. Hence such $\fp, \fq$ do not exist. Similarly, by \eqref{eq-L3-def}, each set $\fL_3(k,n,j,l)$ is a set of maximal elements in some set of tiles with respect to $\le$. If there were distinct $\fp, \fq \in \fL_3(k,n,j,l)$ with $\fp \le \fq$, then $\fp$ would not be maximal.
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Sets of minimal (resp. maximal) elements are antichains.

nodes.name: Proof of forest complement
nodes.statement: If $\fp \not\in \fP_{G \setminus G'}$, then $\mu(\scI(\fp) \cap (G \setminus G')) = 0$. By \eqref{definetp} and \eqref{definee1}, it follows that $\mathbf{1}_{G \setminus G'} T_{\fp}f(x) = 0$ for almost every $x$. We thus have, almost everywhere, $$ \mathbf{1}_{G\setminus G'} \sum_{\fp \in \fP_2} T_{\fp}f(x) = \mathbf{1}_{G\setminus G'} \sum_{\fp \in \fP_2 \cap \fP_{G \setminus G'}} T_{\fp}f(x)\,. $$ Let $\fL(k,n)$ denote any of the terms $\fL_i(k,n,j,l) \cap \fP_{G \setminus G'}$ on the right hand side of \eqref{eq-fp'-decomposition}, where the indices $j, l$ may be void. Then $\fL(k,n)$ is an antichain, by Lemmas \ref{L0-antichain},\ref{L2-antichain}, \ref{L1-L3-antichain}. Further, we have \begin{equation*} \dens_1(\fL(k,n)) \le 2^{4a+1 - n} \end{equation*} by \Cref{C-dens1}, and we have \begin{equation*} \dens_2(\fL(k,n)) \le 2^{2a+5} \frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)}, \end{equation*} since \begin{equation*} \fL(k,n) \cap \fP_{F,G} \subset \fP_{G \setminus G'} \cap \fP_{F, G} = \emptyset. \end{equation*} Applying now the triangle inequality according to the decomposition coming from \Cref{antichain-decomposition}, and then applying \Cref{antichain-operator} to each term, we obtain the estimate \begin{multline*} \le \sum_{k \ge 0} \sum_{n \ge k} (n + (2n+4) + 2(2n+4) (1+Z(n+1))) \\ \times 2^{117a^3}(q-1)^{-1} (2^{4a+1-n})^{\frac{q-1}{8a^4}} (2^{2a+5} \frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)})^{\frac{1}{q} - \frac{1}{2}} \|f\|_2\|\mathbf{1}_{G\setminus G'}\|_2\,. \end{multline*} Because $|f| \le \mathbf{1}_F$, we have $\|f\|_2 \le \mu(F)^{1/2}$, and we have $\|\mathbf{1}_{G\setminus G'}\|_2 \le \mu(G)^{1/2}$. Using this and \eqref{defineZ}, we bound $$ \le 2^{118a^3} (q - 1)^{-1} \mu(F)^{\frac{1}{q}} \mu(G)^{\frac{1}{q'}} \sum_{k \ge 0} \sum_{n \ge k} n^2 2^{-n\frac{q-1}{8a^4}}\,. $$ The last sum equals, by changing the order of summation, $$ \sum_{n \ge 0} n^2(n+1) 2^{-n\frac{q-1}{8a^4}} \le \frac{2^{2a^3}}{(q-1)^4}\,. $$ This completes the proof.

nodes.statement_short: Restrict to tiles meeting $G\setminus G'$, split into antichains by \Cref{antichain-decomposition}, bound the densities and apply \Cref{antichain-operator}.

nodes.name: Proof of tile disjointness
nodes.statement: Let $\fp,\fp'$ and $x$ be given. Assume without loss of generality that $\ps(\fp)\le \ps(\fp')$. As we have $x\in E(\fp)\subset \scI(\fp)$ and $x\in E(\fp')\subset \scI(\fp')$ by Definition \eqref{defineep}, we conclude for $i=1,2$ that $\tQ(x)\in\fc(\fp)$ and $\tQ(x)\in\fc(\fp')$. By \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic} we have $\fc(\fp')\subset \fc(\fp)$. By Definition \eqref{straightorder}, we conclude $\fp\le \fp'$. As $\mathfrak{A}$ is an antichain, we conclude $\fp=\fp'$. This proves the lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of maximal bound antichain
nodes.statement: Fix $x\in X$. By \Cref{tile-disjointness}, there is at most one $\fp \in \mathfrak{A}$ such that $T_{\fp} f(x)$ is not zero. If there is no such $\fp$, the estimate \eqref{hlmbound} follows. Assume there is such a $\fp$. By definition of $T_{\fp}$ we have $x\in E(\fp)\subset \scI(\fp)$ and by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} \begin{equation} \rho(x, \pc(\fp))\le 4D^{\ps(\fp)}\, . \end{equation} Let $y\in X$ with $K_{\ps(\fp)}(x,y)\neq 0$. By Definition \eqref{defks} of $K_{\ps(\fp)}$ we have \begin{equation} \frac{1}{4} D^{\ps(\fp)-1} \leq \rho(x,y) \leq \frac{1}{2} D^{\ps(\fp)}\, . \end{equation} The triangle inequality with \eqref{eqtttt0} and \eqref{supp-Ks1} implies \begin{equation} \rho(\pc(\fp),y) < 8D^{\ps(\fp)}\, . \end{equation} Using the kernel bound \eqref{eqkernel-size} and the lower bound in \eqref{supp-Ks} we obtain \begin{equation} |K_{\ps(\fp)}(x,y)|\le \frac{2^{a^3}}{\mu(B(x,\frac 14 D^{{\ps(\fp)}-1}))}\, . \end{equation} Using $D=2^{100a^2}$ and the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $5 +100a^2$ times estimates the last display by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{5a+101a^3}}{\mu(B(x, 8D^{\ps(\fp)}))}\, \end{equation} which, thanks to the closeness of the points $x$ and $\pc(\fp)$ shown in \eqref{eqtttt0}, is in turn bounded by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{6a+101a^3}}{\mu(B(\pc(\fp), 8D^{\ps(\fp)}))}\, . \end{equation} Using that {$|e(\mfa)|$} is bounded by $1$ for every $\mfa\in \Mf$, we estimate with the triangle inequality and the above information \begin{equation} | T_{\fp} f(x)| \le \frac{2^{6a+101 a^3}}{\mu(B(\pc(\fp), 8D^{\ps(\fp)}))} \int _{\mu(B(\pc(\fp), 8D^{\ps(\fp)}))} |f(y)|\, dy \end{equation} This together with $a\ge 4$ proves the Lemma.
nodes.statement_short: At most one tile is active at $x$; bound its kernel by the size estimate and doubling to get a maximal average.

nodes.name: Proof of dens2 antichain
nodes.statement: We have $f=\mathbf{1}_Ff$. Using H\"older's inequality, we obtain for each $x\in B'$ and each $B'\in \mathcal{B}$ using $1<\tilde{q}\le 2$ \begin{equation} \frac 1{\mu(B')}\int_{B'} |f(y)|\, d\mu(y) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \left(\frac 1{\mu(B')}\int_{B'} |f(y)|^{\frac {2{\tilde{q}}}{3\tilde{q}-2}}\, d\mu(y)\right)^{\frac 32-\frac 1{\tilde{q}}} \left(\frac 1{\mu(B')}\int_{B'} \mathbf{1}_F(y)\, d\mu(y)\right)^{\frac 1{\tilde{q}}-\frac 12} \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \left(M_{\mathcal{B}} (|f|^{\frac {2{\tilde{q}}}{3{\tilde{q}}-2}})(x)\right)^{\frac 32-\frac 1{\tilde{q}}} \dens_2(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1{\tilde{q}}-\frac 12}\, . \end{equation} Taking the maximum over all $B'$ containing $x$, we obtain \begin{equation} M_{\mathcal{B}}|f|\le M_{\mathcal{B},\frac {2{\tilde{q}}}{3{\tilde{q}}-2} } |f| \dens_2(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1{\tilde{q}}-\frac 12}\, . \end{equation} We have with \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood} \begin{equation} \left\|M_{\mathcal{B}, \frac {2{\tilde{q}}}{3{\tilde{q}}-2}} f\right\|_2\le 2^{2a}(3\tilde{q}-2)(2\tilde{q}-2)^{-1}\|f\|_2\, . \end{equation} Using $1<\tilde{q}\le 2$ estimates the last display by \begin{equation} 2^{2a+2} (\tilde{q}-1)^{-1} \|f\|_2\, . \end{equation} We obtain with Cauchy-Schwarz and then \Cref{maximal-bound-antichain} \begin{equation} |\int \overline{g(x)} \sum_{\fp \in \mathfrak{A}} T_{\fp} f(x)\, d\mu(x)| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \|g\|_2 \Big\| \sum_{\fp \in \mathfrak{A}} T_{\fp} f \Big\|_2 \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{102a^3}\|g\|_2 \| M_{\mathcal{B}}f \|_2 \end{equation} With \eqref{eqttt1} and \eqref{eqttt2} we can estimate the last display by \begin{equation} \le 2^{102a^3+2a+2}(\tilde{q}-1)^{-1} \|g\|_2 \|f\|_2\dens_2(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1{\tilde{q}}-\frac 12} \end{equation} Using $a\ge 4$ and $(\tilde q - 1)^{-1} = (q+1)/(q-1) \le 3(q-1)^{-1}$ proves the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Hölder with $\mathbf{1}_F$ inside each ball, the maximal function bound and \Cref{maximal-bound-antichain}.

nodes.name: Proof of dens1 antichain
nodes.statement: We write for the expression inside the absolute values on the left-hand side of \eqref{eqttt3} \begin{equation} \sum_{\fp \in \mathfrak{A}}\iint \overline{g(x)} \mathbf{1}_{E(\fp)}(x) {K_{\ps(\fp)}(x,y)}e(\tQ(x)(y) - \tQ(x)(x)) f(y)\, d\mu(y)\,d\mu(x) \end{equation} \begin{equation} =\int \sum_{\fp \in \mathfrak{A}} \overline{T_{\fp} ^*g(y)} f(y)\, d\mu(y) \end{equation} with the adjoint operator \begin{equation} T_{\fp}^*g(y)=\int_{E(\fp)} \overline{K_{\ps(\fp)}(x,y)}e(-\tQ(x)(y)+ \tQ(x)(x))g(x)\, d\mu(x)\, . \end{equation} We have by expanding the square \begin{equation} \int \Big|\sum_{\fp\in \mathfrak{A}}T^*_{\fp}g(y)\Big|^2\, d\mu(y)= \int \left(\sum_{\fp\in \mathfrak{A}} T^*_{\fp}g(y)\right) \left(\sum_{\fp'\in \mathfrak{A}}\overline{T^*_{\fp'}g(y)}\right)\, d\mu(y) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \sum_{\fp\in \mathfrak{A}} \sum_{\fp'\in \mathfrak{A}} \Big|\int T^*_{\fp}g(y)\overline{T^*_{\fp'}g(y)}\, d\mu(y)\Big|\,. \end{equation} We split the sum into the terms with $\ps(\fp')\le \ps(\fp)$ and $\ps(\fp)< \ps(\fp')$. Using the symmetry of each summand, we may switch $\fp$ and $\fp'$ in the second sum. Using further positivity of each summand to replace the condition $\ps(\fp')< \ps(\fp)$ by $\ps(\fp')\le \ps(\fp)$ in the second sum, we estimate \eqref{eqtts1} by \begin{equation} \le2 \sum_{\fp\in \mathfrak{A}} \sum_{\fp'\in \mathfrak{A}: \ps(\fp')\le \ps(\fp)} \Big|\int T^*_{\fp}g(y)\overline{T^*_{\fp'}g(y)}\, d\mu(y)\Big|\,. \end{equation} Define for $\fp\in \fP$ \begin{equation} B(\fp):=B(\pc(\fp), 14D^{\ps(\fp)}) \end{equation} and define \begin{equation} \mathfrak{A}(\fp):=\{\fp'\in\mathfrak{A}: \ps(\fp')\leq \ps(\fp) \land \scI(\fp') \subset B(\fp)\}. \end{equation} Note that by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} applied $6$ times we have \begin{equation} \mu(B(\fp))\le 2^{6a} \mu(\scI(\fp))\, . \end{equation} Using \Cref{tile-correlation} and \eqref{eqttt4}, we estimate \eqref{eqtts2} by \begin{equation} \le 2^{232a^3+6a+1} \sum_{\fp\in \mathfrak{A}} \int_{E(\fp)}|g|(y) h(\fp)\, d\mu(y) \end{equation} with $h(\fp)$ defined as \begin{equation} \frac 1{\mu(B(\fp))}\int \sum_{\fp'\in \mathfrak{A}(\fp)} {(1+d_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fp'), \fcc(\fp))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}}(\mathbf{1}_{E(\fp')}|g|)(y')\, d\mu(y')\,. \end{equation} Note that $p>4$ since $a\ge 4$. Let $p'$ be the dual exponent of $p$, satisfying $1/p+1/p'=1$. We estimate $h(\fp)$ as defined in \eqref{def-hp} with H\"older using $|g|\le \mathbf{1}_G$ and $E(\fp')\subset B(\fp)$ by \begin{equation} \frac{\|g\mathbf{1}_{B(\fp)}\|_{p'}}{\mu(B(\fp))} \Big\|\sum_{\fp\in\mathfrak{A}(\fp)}(1+d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp), \fcc(\fp'))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}\mathbf{1}_{E(\fp)}\mathbf{1}_G\Big\|_{p}\, . \end{equation} Then we apply \Cref{antichain-tile-count} to estimate this by \begin{equation} \le 2^{5a} \frac{\|g\mathbf{1}_{B(\fp)}\|_{p'}}{\mu(B(\fp))} \dens_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}\mu(B(\fp))^{\frac 1p}\,. \end{equation} Let $\mathcal{B}'$ be the collection of all balls $B(\fp)$ with $\fp\in \mathfrak{A}$. Then for each $\fp\in \mathfrak{A}$ and $x\in B(\fp)$ we have by definition \eqref{def-hlm} of $M_{\mathcal{B}',p'}$ \begin{equation} \|g\mathbf{1}_{B(\fp)}\|_{p'}\le \mu(B(\fp))^{\frac 1{p'}} M_{\mathcal{B}',p'}g(x) \, . \end{equation} Hence we can estimate \eqref{eqttt5} by \begin{equation} \le 2^{5a} (M_{\mathcal{B}', p'}g(x)) \dens_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}\, . \end{equation} With this estimate of $h(\fp)$, using $E(\fp)\subset B(\fp)$ by construction of $B(\fp)$, we estimate \eqref{eqtts3} by \begin{equation} \le 2^{232a^3+11a + 1} { \dens_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}}\sum_{\fp\in \mathfrak{A}} \int_{E(\fp)}|g|(y)M_{\mathcal{B}', p'}g(y) \, dy\,. \end{equation} Using \Cref{tile-disjointness}, the last display is observed to be \begin{equation} \le 2^{232a^3+11a + 1} {\dens_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}} \int |g|(y)(M_{\mathcal{B}', p'}g)(y) \, dy\,. \end{equation} Applying Cauchy-Schwarz and using \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood} and $1<p'<\frac 32$ estimates the last display by \begin{equation} \le 2^{232a^3+11a + 1} \dens_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p} \|g\|_2 \|M_{\mathcal{B}', p'} g\|_2 \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{232a^3+12a+3} \dens_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}\|g\|_2 ^2\,. \end{equation} Now \Cref{dens1-antichain} follows by applying Cauchy-Schwarz on the left-hand side and using $a\ge 4$.
nodes.statement_short: $TT^*$ argument: expand $\|\sum T^*_{\fp}g\|_2^2$, bound pair correlations by \Cref{tile-correlation}, then use \Cref{antichain-tile-count} and maximal functions.

nodes.name: Proof of correlation kernel bound
nodes.statement: If $\varphi(y)$ is not zero, then $K_{s_1}(x_1, y)$ is not zero and thus \eqref{supp-Ks} gives \eqref{eqt10}. We next have for $y$ with \eqref{eq-Ks-size} \begin{equation} |\varphi(y)|\le \frac{2^{204 a^3}}{\mu(B(x_1, D^{s_1}))\mu(B(x_2, D^{s_2}))} \end{equation} and for $y'\neq y$ additionally with \eqref{eq-Ks-smooth} \begin{equation} |\varphi(y)-\varphi(y')| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le |K_{s_1}(x_1,y)-K_{s_1}(x_1,y'))|| K_{s_2}(x_2, y)| \end{equation} \begin{equation}+|K_{s_1}(x_1, y')| |K_{s_2}(x_2, y) - K_{s_2}(x_2, y'))| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{229 a^3}}{\mu(B(x_1, D^{s_1}))\mu(B(x_2, D^{s_2}))} \left(\left(\frac{ \rho(y,y')}{D^{s_1}}\right)^{1/a}+ \left(\frac{ \rho(y,y')}{D^{s_2}}\right)^{1/a}\right) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{230 a^3}}{\mu(B(x_1, D^{s_1}))\mu(B(x_2, D^{s_2}))} \left(\frac{ \rho(y,y')}{D^{s_1}}\right)^{1/a}\,. \end{equation} Adding the estimates \eqref{suppart} and \eqref{holderpart} gives \eqref{eqt11}. nodes.name: Proof of tile uncertainty
nodes.statement: Let $i\in \{1,2\}$. By Definition \eqref{defineep} of $E$, we have $\tQ(x_i)\in \fc(\fp_i)$ With \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} we then conclude \begin{equation} d_{\fp_i}(\tQ(x_i),\fcc(\fp_i)) < 1\, . \end{equation} We have by the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} that $\scI(\fp_1) \subset B(\pc(\fp_2),14D^{\ps(\fp_2)})$. Thus, using again \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the doubling property \eqref{firstdb} \begin{equation} d_{\fp_1}(\tQ(x_2), \fcc(\fp_2)) \le 2^{6a} d_{\fp_2}(\tQ(x_2), \fcc(\fp_2)) \le 2^{6a}\,. \end{equation} By the triangle inequality, we obtain from \eqref{dponetwo} and \eqref{tgeo0.5} \begin{equation} 1+d_{\fp_1}(\fcc(\fp_1), \fcc(\fp_2))\le 2 + 2^{6a} +d_{\fp_1}(\tQ(x_1), \tQ(x_2))\, . \end{equation} As $x_1\in \scI(\fp_1)$ by Definition \eqref{defineep} of $E$, we have by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} \begin{equation} d(x_1,\pc(\fp_1))\le 4D^{\ps(\fp_1)} \end{equation} and thus by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} again and the triangle inequality \begin{equation} \scI(\fp_1)\subset B(x_1,8D^{\ps(\fp_1)})\, . \end{equation} We thus estimate the right-hand side of \eqref{tgeo1} with monotonicity \eqref{monotonedb} of the metrics $d_B$ by \begin{equation} \le 2 + 2^{6a} + d_{B(x_1,8D^{\ps(\fp_1)})}(\tQ(x_1), \tQ(x_2))\, . \end{equation} This is further estimated by applying the doubling property \eqref{firstdb} three times by \begin{equation} \le 2 + 2^{6a} +2^{3a}d_{B_1(x_1, D^{\ps(\fp_1)})}(\tQ(x_1), \tQ(x_2))\, . \end{equation} Now \eqref{tgeo} follows with $a\ge 4$.

nodes.name: Proof of tile correlation
nodes.statement: We begin with \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est}. By Lemma \ref{tile-range-support}, the left-hand side of \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est} vanishes if $B(\pc(\fp'),5D^{\ps(\fp')}) \cap B(\pc(\fp),5D^{\ps(\fp)}) = \emptyset$. Thus we can assume for the remainder of the proof that \begin{equation} B(\pc(\fp'),5D^{\ps(\fp')}) \cap B(\pc(\fp),5D^{\ps(\fp)}) \neq \emptyset\,. \end{equation} We expand the left-hand side of \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est} as \begin{equation} \left|\int \int_{E(\fp')} \overline{K_{\ps(\fp')}(x_1,y)}e(-\tQ(x_1)(y)+ \tQ(x_1)(x_1))g(x_1)\, d\mu(x_1) \right. \end{equation} \begin{equation} \times \left.\int_{E(\fp)} {K_{\ps(\fp)}(x_2,y)}e(\tQ(x_2)(y) -\tQ(x_2)(x_2))\overline{g(x_2)}\, d\mu(x_2)\, d\mu(y)\right|\, . \end{equation} By Fubini and the triangle inequality and the fact $|e(\tQ(x_i)(x_i))|=1$ for $i=1,2$, we can estimate \eqref{tstartstar} and \eqref{tstartstar'} from above by \begin{equation} \int_{E(\fp')} \int_{E(\fp)} {\bf I}(x_1, x_2)\, d\mu(x_1)d\mu(x_2)\,. \end{equation} with \begin{equation} {\bf I}(x_1, x_2):= \left|\int e(-\tQ(x_1)(y)+\tQ(x_2)(y))\varphi_{x_1,x_2}(y) d\mu(y) \, g(x_1)g(x_2)\right| \end{equation} We estimate for fixed $x_1\in E(\fp')$ and $x_2\in E(\fp)$ the inner integral of \eqref{eqa1} with \Cref{Holder-van-der-Corput}. The function $\varphi:=\varphi_{x_1,x_2}$ satisfies the assumptions of \Cref{Holder-van-der-Corput} with $z = x_1$ and $R = D^{s_1}$ by \Cref{correlation-kernel-bound}. We obtain with $B':= B(x_1, D^{\ps(\fp')})$, \begin{equation*} {\bf I}(x_1, x_2) \le 2^{8a} \mu(B') \|{\varphi}\|_{C^\tau(B')} (1 + d_{B'}(\tQ(x_1),\tQ(x_2)))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}|g(x_1)g(x_2)| \end{equation*} \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{231a^3+8a}} {\mu(B(x_2, D^{\ps(\fp)}))} (1 + d_{B'}(\tQ(x_1),\tQ(x_2)))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}\,. \end{equation} Using \eqref{intersec5B}, \Cref{tile-uncertainty} and $a\ge 1$ estimates \eqref{eqa1.5} by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{231a^3 + 8a + 1}} {\mu(B(x_2, D^{\ps(\fp)}))} (1+d_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fp'), \fcc(\fp)))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}|g(x_1)g(x_2)|\,. \end{equation} As $x_2\in \scI(\fp)$ by Definition \eqref{defineep} of $E$, we have by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} \begin{equation} \rho(x_2,\pc(\fp)) < 4D^{\ps(\fp)} \end{equation} and thus by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} again and the triangle inequality \begin{equation} \scI(\fp)\subset B(x_2,8D^{\ps(\fp)})\, . \end{equation} Using three iterations of the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} give \begin{equation} \mu(\scI(\fp))\le 2^{3a}\mu(B(x_2,D^{\ps(\fp)}))\, . \end{equation} With $a\ge 4$ and \eqref{eqa2} we conclude \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est}. Now assume the left-hand side of \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est} is not zero. There is a $y\in X$ with \begin{equation} T^*_{\fp'}g(y)\overline{T^*_{\fp}g(y)}\neq 0 \end{equation} By the triangle inequality and \Cref{tile-range-support}, we conclude \begin{equation} \rho(\pc(\fp),\pc(\fp'))\le \rho(\pc(\fp),y) +\rho(\pc(\fp'),y) \le 5D^{\ps(\fp)}+5D^{\ps(\fp')}\le 10 D^{\ps(\fp)}\, . \end{equation} By the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality, we conclude \begin{equation} \scI(\fp') \subset B(\pc(\fp), 14D^{\ps(\fp)})\, . \end{equation} This completes the proof of Lemma \ref{tile-correlation}.

nodes.name: Proof of tile reach
nodes.statement: By \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}, we have \begin{equation} d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp'),\mfa) \le d_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fp'),\mfa) \le 2^{N} \, . \end{equation} Together with \eqref{eqassumedismfa} and the triangle inequality, we obtain \begin{equation} d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp'),\fcc(\fp))\le 2^{N+1} \, . \end{equation} Now assume \begin{equation} \mfa'\in B_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fp'),2^{N+2}). \end{equation} By the doubling property \eqref{firstdb}, applied five times, we have \begin{equation} d_{B(\pc(\fp'),8D^{\ps(\fp')})}(\fcc(\fp'),\mfa') < 2^{5a+N+2}\, . \end{equation} We have by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} \begin{equation} \pc(\fp)\in B(\pc(\fp'),4D^{\ps(\fp')})\, . \end{equation} Hence by the triangle inequality \begin{equation} B(\pc(\fp), 4D^{\ps(\fp')}) \subseteq B(\pc(\fp'),8D^{\ps(\fp')})\, . \end{equation} Together with \eqref{ageo1} and monotonicity \eqref{monotonedb} of $d$ \begin{equation} d_{B(\pc(\fp),4D^{\ps(\fp')})}(\fcc(\fp'),\mfa') < 2^{5a+N+2}\, . \end{equation} Using the doubling property \eqref{seconddb} $5a+2$ times gives \begin{equation} d_{B(\pc(\fp),2^{2-5a^2-2a}D^{\ps(\fp')})}(\fcc(\fp'),\mfa') < 2^{N}\, . \end{equation} Using $\ps(\fp)<\ps(\fp')$ and $D=2^{100a^2}$ and $a\ge 4$ gives \begin{equation} d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp'),\mfa') < 2^{N}\, . \end{equation} With the triangle inequality and \eqref{eqdistqpqp}, \begin{equation} d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp),\mfa') < 2^{N+2}\, . \end{equation} This shows \begin{equation} B_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fp'),2^{N+2})\subset B_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp),2^{N+2})\, . \end{equation} This implies \eqref{lp'lp''} and completes the proof of the lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of stack density
nodes.statement: Let $\mfa,N,L$ be given and set \begin{equation} \mathfrak{A}':=\{\fp\in\mathfrak{A}_{\mfa,N}:\scI(\fp)=L\}\, . \end{equation} Let $\fp\in\mathfrak{A}'$. We have by Definition \eqref{definedens1} using $\lambda=2$ and the squeezing property \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} \begin{equation} \mu(E(\fp)\cap G)\le \mu(E_2(2, \fp))\le 2^{a}\dens_1(\mathfrak{A}')\mu(L)\, . \end{equation} By the covering property \eqref{thirddb}, applied $N+4$ times, there is a collection $\Mf'$ of at most $2^{a(N+4)}$ elements such that \begin{equation} B_{\fp}(\mfa, 2^{N+1})\subset \bigcup_{\mfa'\in \Mf'} B_{\fp}(\mfa', 0.2)\, . \end{equation} As each $\fcc(\fp')$ with $\fp'\in \mathfrak{A}'$ is contained in the left-hand-side of \eqref{eqanti-4} by definition (because $\scI(\fp') = \scI(\fp))$, it is in at least one $B_{\fp}(\mfa', 0.2)$ with $\mfa'\in \Mf'$. For two different $\fp',\fp''\in \mathfrak{A}'$, we have by \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} that $\fc(\fp')$ and $\fc(\fp'')$ are disjoint and thus by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} we have for every $\mfa'\in \Mf'$ \begin{equation} \mfa'\not\in B_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp'), 0.2)\cap B_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp''), 0.2)\, . \end{equation} Hence at most one of $\fcc(\fp')$ and $\fcc(\fp'')$ is in $B_{\fp}(\mfa', 0.2)$. It follows that there are at most $2^{a(N+4)}$ elements in $\mathfrak{A}'$. Adding \eqref{eqanti-3} over $\mathfrak{A}'$ proves \eqref{eqanti-1}.

nodes.name: Proof of local antichain density
nodes.statement: Let $\fp$ be any tile in $\mathfrak{A}_{\mfa,N}$ with $\ps(\fp_{\mfa})<\ps(\fp)$. By definition of $E$, the tile contributes zero to the sum on the left-hand side of \eqref{eqanti-0.5} unless $\scI(\fp)\cap \scI(\fp_{\mfa}) \neq \emptyset$, which we may assume. With $\ps(\fp_{\mfa})<\ps(\fp)$ and the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty} we conclude $\scI(\fp_{\mfa})\subset \scI(\fp)$. We conclude from $\fp \in \mathfrak{A}_{\mfa,N}$ that \begin{equation} \mfa \in B_\fp(\fcc(\fp), 2^{N+1})\, . \end{equation} With \Cref{tile-reach} and the assumption on $\fp_\mfa$, we conclude \begin{equation} 2^{N+3}\fp_{\mfa} \lesssim 2^{N+3}\fp \, . \end{equation} By Definition \eqref{definee2} of $E_2$, we conclude \begin{equation} E(\fp)\cap G \cap \scI(\fp_{\mfa}) \subset E_2(2^{N+3},\fp_{\mfa})\, . \end{equation} Using disjointedness of the various $E(\fp)$ with $\fp\in \mathfrak{A}$ by \Cref{tile-disjointness}, we obtain \eqref{eqanti-0.5}. This proves the lemma.

{Fix $\mfa$ and $N$. Let $\mathfrak{A}'$ be the set of $ p\in\mathfrak{A}_{\mfa,N}$ such that $\scI( p)\cap G$ is not empty and $s( p) > -S$. Let $\mathfrak{A}_{-S}$ be the set of $ p\in\mathfrak{A}_{\mfa,N}$ such that $\scI( p)\cap G$ is not empty and $s( p) = -S$ } Then we have  egin{equation*} \sum_{ p\in\mathfrak{A}_{\mfa,N}}\mu(E( p)\cap G) = \sum_{ p\in\mathfrak{A}'}\mu(E( p)\cap G) + \sum_{ p\in\mathfrak{A}_{-S}}\mu(E( p)\cap G) \end{equation*} We start by estimating the contribution of $\mathfrak{A}_{-S}$. Let $\mathcal{L}_{-S}$ be the collection of dyadic cubes $\scI( p)$ with $ p \in \mathfrak{A}_{-S}$. They all have scale $-S$, by definition of $\mathcal{L}_{-S}$, and hence they are pairwise disjoint by the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty}. We write \[ \sum_{ p\in\mathfrak{A}_{-S}}\mu(E( p)\cap G) = \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}_{-S}} \sum_{ p\in\mathfrak{A}_{-S}, \scI( p) = L} \mu(E( p)\cap G), \] and using \Cref{stack-density}, we estimate  egin{equation} \le 2^{a(N+5)} \dens_1(\mathfrak{A}) \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}_{-S}} \mu(L) \le 2^{a(N+5)} \dens_1(\mathfrak{A}) \mu\left(\cup_{ p\in\mathfrak{A}}I_{ p}ight). \end{equation} We turn to $\mathfrak{A}'$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the collection of dyadic cubes $I\in\mathcal{D}$ such that $I \le \scI( p)$ for some $ p\in\mathfrak{A}'$ and such that $\scI( p)
ot \subset I$ for all $ p\in\mathfrak{A}'$. By \eqref{coverdyadic}, for each $ p \in \mathfrak{A}'$ and each $x\in \scI( p)\cap G$, there is $I\in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(I)=-S$ and $x\in I$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have $I\subset \scI( p)$. Since for all $ p' \in \mathfrak{A}'$ we have $s( p') > -S$, we have $I \in \mathcal{L}$. Hence  egin{equation} \scI( p)\subset  igcup\{I\in \mathcal{D}: s(I)=-S, I\subset \scI( p)\}\subset  igcup \mathcal{L}\, . \end{equation} As each $I\in \mathcal{L}$ satisfies $I\subset \scI( p)$ for some $ p$ in $\mathfrak{A'}$, we conclude  egin{equation}  igcup\mathcal{L}= igcup_{ p \in \mathfrak{A}'}\scI( p)\, . \end{equation} Let $\mathcal{L}^*$ be the set of maximal elements in $\mathcal{L}$ with respect to set inclusion. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, the elements in $\mathcal{L}^*$ are pairwise disjoint and we have  egin{equation}  igcup\mathcal{L}^*= igcup_{ p \in \mathfrak{A}'}\scI( p)\, . \end{equation} Using the partition \eqref{eqdecAprime} into elements of $\mathcal{L}$ in \eqref{eqanti0}, it suffices to show for each $L\in \mathcal{L}^*$  egin{equation} \sum_{ p\in\mathfrak{A}'}\mu(E( p)\cap G \cap L) \le 2^{101a^3+aN} \dens_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu(L)\,. \end{equation} Fix $L\in \mathcal{L}^*$. By definition of $\mathcal{L}^*$, there exists an element $ p'\in \mathfrak{A}'$ such that $L\subset \scI( p')$. Pick such an element $ p'$ in $\mathfrak{A}$ with minimal $\ps( p')$. As $\scI( p')
ot \subset L$ by definition of $L$, we have with \eqref{dyadicproperty} that $s(L)< \ps( p')$. In particular $s(L)<S$, thus $L 
e I_0$ and hence by \eqref{subsetmaxcube} there exists a cube $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $L \subsetneq J$. By \eqref{coverdyadic}, there is an $L'\in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(L')=s(L)+1$ and $L \le L'$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have $L\subset L'$. We split the left-hand side of \eqref{eqanti0} as  egin{equation} \sum_{ p\in\mathfrak{A}':\scI( p)=L'}\mu(E( p)\cap G\cap L) \end{equation}  egin{equation} + \sum_{ p\in\mathfrak{A}':\scI( p)
eq L'}\mu(E( p)\cap G\cap L)\, , \end{equation} We first estimate \eqref{eqanti1} with \Cref{stack-density} by  egin{equation} \le \sum_{ p\in\mathfrak{A}':\scI( p)=L'}\mu(E( p)\cap G\cap L')\le 2^{a(N+5)}\dens_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu(L')\, . \end{equation} We turn to \eqref{eqanti2}. Consider the element $ p'\in \mathfrak{A}'$ as above with $L\subset \scI( p')$ and $s(L)<\ps( p')$. As $L\subset L'$ and $s(L')=s(L)+1$, we conclude with the dyadic property that $L'\subset \scI( p')$. By maximality of $L$, we have $L'
ot\in \mathcal{L}$. This together with the existence of the given $ p'\in \mathfrak{A}$ with $L'\subset \scI( p')$ shows by definition of $\mathcal{L}$ that there exists $ p''\in \mathfrak{A}'$ with $\scI( p'')\subset L'$. If $\scI( p'') = L'$, then we set $ p_{\mfa} =  p''$ and note that as $ p'' \in \mathfrak{A}_{\mfa,N}$  egin{equation} \mfa \in B( cc( p''), 2^{N+1})\, . \end{equation} If $\scI( p'') 
e L'$, then it follows that $s( p'') < s(L')$. By the covering property \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}, there exists a unique $ p_{\mfa}$ with  egin{equation*} \scI( p_{\mfa})=L' \end{equation*} such that $\mfa\in  c( p_{\mfa})$. We take this as the definition of $ p_\mfa$ in this case. Note that  egin{equation} \mfa\in B( cc( p_{\mfa}), 1) \end{equation} so by \Cref{tile-reach}, we conclude  egin{equation} 2^{N+3} p'' \lesssim 2^{N+3} p_{\mfa} \, . \end{equation} This clearly also holds in the case $\scI( p'') = L'$, since then $ p'' =  p_\mfa$. Furthermore, in both cases it also holds that  egin{equation} \mfa\in B_{ p_{\mfa}}( cc( p_{\mfa}), 2^{N+1}). \end{equation} As $ p''\in \mathfrak{A}'$, we have by Definition \eqref{definedens1} of $\dens_1$ that  egin{equation} \mu(E_2(2^{N+3},  p_{\mfa}))\le 2^{Na+3a}\dens_1(\mathfrak{A}) {\mu(L')}\, . \end{equation} Now let $ p$ be any tile in the summation set in \eqref{eqanti2}, that is, $ p\in \mathfrak{A}'$ and $\scI( p)
eq L'$. Then $\scI( p)\cap L
eq \emptyset$. It follows by the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty} and the definition of $L$ that $L\subset \scI( p)$ and $L
eq \scI( p)$. By the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have $s(L)<\ps( p)$ and thus $s(L')\le \ps( p)$. By the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty} again, we have $L'\subset \scI( p)$. As $L'
eq \scI( p)$, we conclude $s(L)<\ps( p)$. By \Cref{local-antichain-density}, we can thus estimate \eqref{eqanti2} by  egin{equation} \sum_{ p\in\mathfrak{A}':\scI( p)
eq L'}\mu(E( p)\cap G\cap L') \le \mu (E_2(2^{N+3}, p_{\mfa}))\, . \end{equation} With the decomposition in \eqref{eqanti1} and \eqref{eqanti2} and the estimates \eqref{equanti1.5}, \eqref{eqanti-0.5}, \eqref{pmfadens} we obtain the estimate  egin{equation} \sum_{ p\in\mathfrak{A}'}\mu(E( p)\cap G \cap L) \le (2^{a(N+5)}+2^{Na+3a})\dens_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu(L')\,. \end{equation} Using $s(L')=s(L)+1$ and $D=2^{100a^2}$ and the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $100a^2+4$ times , we obtain  egin{equation} \mu(L')\le 2^{100a^3+4a}\mu(L)\, . \end{equation} Inserting in \eqref{eqanti3.14}, adding the estimate \eqref{eq_minus_S} and using $a\ge 4$ gives \eqref{eqanti0}. This completes the proof of the lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of antichain tile count
nodes.statement: Using that $\mathfrak{A}$ is the disjoint union of the $\mathfrak{A}_{\mfa,N}$ with $N\ge 0$, we estimate the left-hand side \eqref{eq-antichain-Lp} with the triangle inequality by \begin{equation} \le \sum_{N\ge 0} \left\|\sum_{\fp\in \mathfrak{A}_{\mfa,N}} 2^{-N/(2a^2+a^3)}\mathbf{1}_{E(\fp)} \mathbf{1}_G\right\|_{p} \end{equation} We consider each individual term in this sum and estimate its $p$-th power. Using that for each $x\in X$ by \Cref{tile-disjointness} there is at most one $\fp\in \mathfrak{A}$ with $x\in E(\fp)$, we have \begin{equation} \left\|\sum_{\fp\in \mathfrak{A}_{\mfa,N}} 2^{-N/(2a^2+a^3)}\mathbf{1}_{E(\fp)} \mathbf{1}_G\right\|_{p}^p \end{equation} \begin{equation} =\int\Big(\sum_{\fp\in \mathfrak{A}_{\mfa,N}}2^{-N/(2a^2+a^3)}\mathbf{1}_{E(\fp)\cap G}(x)\Big)^p\, d\mu(x) \end{equation} \begin{equation} =\int\sum_{\fp\in\mathfrak{A}_{\mfa,N}}2^{-pN/(2a^2+a^3)}\mathbf{1}_{E(\fp)\cap G}(x)\, d\mu(x) \end{equation} \begin{equation} = 2^{-pN/(2a^2+a^3)} \sum_{\fp\in\mathfrak{A}_{\mfa,N}}\mu(E(\fp)\cap G) \end{equation} Using \Cref{global-antichain-density}, we estimate the last display by \begin{equation} \le 2^{-pN/(2a^2+a^3)+101a^3+Na}\dens_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu\left(\cup_{\fp\in\mathfrak{A}}\scI(\fp)\right) \end{equation} Using that $a\ge 4$ and since $p = 4a^4$, we have $$ pN/(2a^2+a^3)\ge 4a^4N/(3a^3) \ge Na+N\, . $$ Hence we have for \eqref{eqanti21} the upper bound $$ \le 2^{101a^3-N}\dens_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu\left(\cup_{\fp\in\mathfrak{A}}\scI(\fp)\right)\, . $$ Taking the $p$-th root and summing over $N\ge 0$ gives for \eqref{eqanti23} the upper bound $$ \le \left(\sum_{N\ge 0} 2^{-N/p}\right)2^{101a^3/p}\dens_1(\mathfrak{A})^{{\frac{1}{p}}}\mu\left(\cup_{\fp\in\mathfrak{A}}\scI(\fp)\right)^{{\frac{1}{p}}} $$ $$ = \left(1-2^{-1/p}\right)^{-1} 2^{101a^3/p} \dens_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}\mu\left(\cup_{\fp\in\mathfrak{A}}\scI(\fp)\right)^{\frac 1p}\, . $$ Using that $p = 4a^4$ and $a \ge 4$, this proves the lemma.

nodes.name: fixed forest
nodes.statement: Fix a forest $(\fU, \fT)$.

nodes.name: scale set $\sigma(\fu,x)$
nodes.statement:
For $\fu \in \fU$ and $x\in X$, we define
$$
    \sigma (\fu, x):=\{\ps(\fp):\fp\in \fT(\fu), x\in E(\fp)\}\,.
$$

nodes.name: extreme scales $\overline{\sigma}$, $\underline{\sigma}$
nodes.statement:
We set
$$
    \overline{\sigma} (\fu, x) := \max \sigma(\fT(\fu), x)
$$
$$
    \underline{\sigma} (\fu, x) := \min\sigma(\fT(\fu), x)\,.
$$

nodes.name: convex scales
nodes.statement: For each $\fu \in \fU$, we have $$ \sigma(\fu, x) = \mathbb{Z} \cap [\underline{\sigma} (\fu, x), \overline{\sigma} (\fu, x)]\,. $$
nodes.label: convex-scales

nodes.name: Proof of convex scales
nodes.statement: Let $s \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $\underline{\sigma} (\fu, x) \le s \le \overline{\sigma} (\fu, x)$. By definition of $\sigma$, there exists $\fp \in \fT(\fu)$ with $\ps(\fp) = \underline{\sigma} (\fu, x)$ and $x \in E(\fp)$, and there exists $\fp'' \in \fT(\fu)$ with $\ps(\fp'') = \overline{\sigma} (\fu, x)$ and $x \in E(\fp'') \subset \scI(\fp'')$. By property \eqref{coverdyadic} of the dyadic grid, there exists a cube $I \in \mathcal{D}$ of scale $s$ with $x \in I$. By property \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}, there exists a tile $\fp' \in \fP(I)$ with $\tQ(x) \in \fc(\fp')$. By the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty} we have $\scI(\fp) \subset \scI(\fp') \subset \scI(\fp'')$, and by \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic}, we have $\fc(\fp'') \subset \fc(\fp') \subset \fc(\fp)$. Thus $\fp \le \fp' \le\fp''$, which gives with the convexity property \eqref{forest2} of $\fT(\fu)$ that $\fp' \in \fT(\fu)$, so $s \in \sigma(\fu, x)$.
nodes.statement_short: Intermediate scales give intermediate tiles by the grid and tile properties; convexity \eqref{forest2} puts them in the tree.

nodes.name: cubes $\mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$
nodes.statement:
For a nonempty collection of tiles $\mathfrak{S} \subset \fP$ we define
$$
    \mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})
$$
to be the collection of all dyadic cubes $J \in \mathcal{D}$ such that $s(J) = -S$ or
$$
    \scI(\fp) \not\subset B(c(J), 100D^{s(J) + 1})
$$
for all $\fp \in \mathfrak{S}$.

nodes.name: maximal cubes $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$
nodes.statement: We define $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$ to be the collection of inclusion maximal cubes in $\mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$.

nodes.name: cubes $\mathcal{L}_0(\mathfrak{S})$
nodes.statement:
We further define
$$
    \mathcal{L}_0(\mathfrak{S})
$$
to be the collection of dyadic cubes $L \in \mathcal{D}$ such that $s(L) = -S$, or there exists $\fp \in \mathfrak{S}$ with $L \subset \scI(\fp)$ and there exists no $\fp \in \mathfrak{S}$ with $\scI(\fp) \subset L$.

nodes.name: maximal cubes $\mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{S})$
nodes.statement: We define $\mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{S})$ to be the collection of inclusion maximal cubes in $\mathcal{L}_0(\mathfrak{S})$.

nodes.name: dyadic partitions
nodes.statement: For each $\mathfrak{S} \subset \fP$, we have \begin{equation} \bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I = \dot{\bigcup_{J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})}} J \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I = \dot{\bigcup_{L \in \mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{S})}} L\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The maximal cubes $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$ and $\mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{S})$ each partition the union of all cubes.
nodes.label: dyadic-partitions

nodes.name: Equation (374)
nodes.statement: \bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I = \dot{\bigcup_{J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})}} J
nodes.label: eq-J-partition

nodes.name: Equation (375)
nodes.statement: \bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I = \dot{\bigcup_{L \in \mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{S})}} L\,.
nodes.label: eq-L-partition

nodes.name: Proof of dyadic partitions
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$ is the set of inclusion maximal cubes in $\mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$, cubes in $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$ are pairwise disjoint by \eqref{dyadicproperty}. The same applies to $\mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{S})$. If $x \in \bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I$, then there exists by \eqref{coverdyadic} a cube $I \in \mathcal{D}$ with $x \in I$ and $s(I) = -S$. Then $I \in \mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$. There exists an inclusion maximal cube in $\mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$ containing $I$. This cube contains $x$ and is contained in $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$. This shows one inclusion in \eqref{eq-J-partition}, the other one follows from $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S}) \subset \mathcal{D}$. The proof of the two inclusions in \eqref{eq-L-partition} is similar.
nodes.statement_short: Maximal cubes are disjoint; bottom-scale cubes show the cover.

nodes.name: projection operator $P_{\mathcal{C}}$
nodes.statement:
For a finite collection of pairwise disjoint cubes $\mathcal{C}$, define the projection operator
$$
    P_{\mathcal{C}}f(x) :=\sum_{J\in\mathcal{C}}\mathbf{1}_J(x) \frac{1}{\mu(J)}\int_J f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.
$$

nodes.name: cube $I_s(x)$
nodes.statement: Given a scale $-S \le s\le S$ and a point $x \in \bigcup_{I\in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s} I$, there exists a unique cube in $\mathcal{D}$ of scale $s$ containing $x$ by \eqref{coverdyadic}. We denote it by $I_s(x)$.

nodes.name: nontangential maximal operator $T_{\mathcal{N}}^\mfa$
Equation (376)
nodes.statement: T_{\mathcal{N}}^\mfa f(x) := \sup_{-S \le s_1 < S} \sup_{x' \in I_{s_1}(x)} \sup_{\substack{s_1 \le s_2 \le S\\ D^{s_2-1} \le R_Q(\mfa, x')}} \left| \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \int K_s(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right|\,.

nodes.name: auxiliary operator $S_{1,\fu}$

Define for each $\fu \in \fU$ the auxiliary operator
$$
    S_{1,\fu}f(x)
$$
\begin{equation} :=\sum_{I\in\mathcal{D}} \mathbf{1}_{I}(x) \sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))\\
    J\subset B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)})\\ s(J) \le s(I)}} \frac{D^{(s(J) - s(I))/a}}{\mu(B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)}))}\int_J |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.
\end{equation}
