nodes.name: balls $\mathcal{B}$ for trees
nodes.statement:
Define also the collection of balls
$$
    \mathcal{B} = \{B(c(I), 2^s D^{s(I)+t}) \ : \ I \in \mathcal{D}\,, 0 \le s \le S + 5\,, 0 \le t \le 2S+3\}\,.
$$

nodes.name: pointwise tree estimate
nodes.statement: Let $\fu \in \fU$ and $L \in \mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))$. Let $x, x' \in L$. Then for all bounded functions $f$ with bounded support $$ \left|\sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp}[ e(-\fcc(\fu))f](x)\right| $$ \begin{equation} \leq 2^{129a^3}(M_{\mathcal{B},1}+S_{1,\fu})P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}|f|(x')+|T_{\mathcal{N}}^{\fcc(\fu)} P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}f(x')|, \end{equation}
assumptions: Let $\fu \in \fU$ and $L \in \mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))$.
Let $x, x' \in L$.
for all bounded functions $f$ with bounded support
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise bound of a tree operator by maximal, auxiliary and nontangential operators of the projection onto $\mathcal{J}$-cubes.
nodes.label: pointwise-tree-estimate

nodes.name: Equation (378)
nodes.statement: \leq 2^{129a^3}(M_{\mathcal{B},1}+S_{1,\fu})P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}|f|(x')+|T_{\mathcal{N}}^{\fcc(\fu)} P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}f(x')|,
nodes.label: eq-LJ-ptwise

nodes.name: Proof of pointwise tree estimate
nodes.statement: By \eqref{definetp}, if $T_{\fp}[ e(-\fcc(\fu))f](x) \ne 0$, then $x \in E(\fp)$. Combining this with $|e(\fcc(\fu)(x))| = 1$, we obtain $$ |\sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp}[ e(-\fcc(\fu))f](x)| $$ \begin{multline*} = \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma(\fu, x)} \int e(-\fcc(\fu)(y) + \tQ(x)(y) + \fcc(\fu)(x) -\tQ(x)(x))\times\\ K_s(x,y)f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|\,. \end{multline*} Using the triangle inequality, we bound this by the sum of three terms: \begin{multline} \le \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma(\fu, x)} \int (e(-\fcc(\fu)(y) + \tQ(x)(y) + \fcc(\fu)(x) -\tQ(x)(x))-1)\times\\ K_s(x,y)f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \end{multline} \begin{equation} + \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma(\fu, x)} \int K_s(x,y) P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \end{equation} \begin{equation} + \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma(\fu, x)} \int K_s(x,y) (f(y) - P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))} f(y)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|\,. \end{equation} The proof is completed using the bounds for these three terms proven respectively in \Cref{first-tree-pointwise}, \Cref{second-tree-pointwise} and \Cref{third-tree-pointwise}.
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to active scales and split the sum into three terms, bounded by \Cref{first-tree-pointwise}, \Cref{second-tree-pointwise} and \Cref{third-tree-pointwise}.

nodes.name: Equation (379)
nodes.statement: \le \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma(\fu, x)} \int (e(-\fcc(\fu)(y) + \tQ(x)(y) + \fcc(\fu)(x) -\tQ(x)(x))-1)\times\\ K_s(x,y)f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|
nodes.label: eq-term-A

nodes.name: Equation (380)
nodes.statement: + \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma(\fu, x)} \int K_s(x,y) P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|
nodes.label: eq-term-B

nodes.name: Equation (381)
nodes.statement: + \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma(\fu, x)} \int K_s(x,y) (f(y) - P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))} f(y)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|\,.
nodes.label: eq-term-C

nodes.name: first tree pointwise
nodes.statement: For all $\fu \in \fU$, all $L \in \mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))$, all $x, x' \in L$ and all bounded $f$ with bounded support, we have $$ \eqref{eq-term-A} \le 10 \cdot 2^{104a^3} M_{\mathcal{B}, 1}P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}|f|(x')\,. $$
assumptions: For all $\fu \in \fU$, all $L \in \mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))$, all $x, x' \in L$ and all bounded $f$ with bounded support
nodes.statement_short: The modulation error term is bounded by the maximal function of the $\mathcal{J}$-projection.
nodes.label: first-tree-pointwise

nodes.name: Proof of first tree pointwise
nodes.statement:
Let $s \in \sigma( u,x)$. If $x, y \in X$ are such that $K_s(x,y)
eq 0$, then, by \eqref{supp-Ks}, we have $ho(x,y)\leq 1/2 D^s$. By $1$-Lipschitz continuity of the function $t \mapsto \exp(it) = e(t)$ and the property \eqref{osccontrol} of the metrics $d_B$, it follows that  egin{multline*} |e(- cc( u)(y)+	Q(x)(y)+ cc( u)(x)-	Q(x)(x))-1|\ \leq d_{B(x, 1/2 D^{s})}( cc( u), 	Q(x))\,. \end{multline*} Let $ p_s \in  T( u)$ be a tile with $\ps( p_s) = s$ and $x \in E( p_s)$, and let $ p'$ be a tile with $\ps( p') = \overline{\sigma}( u, x)$ and $x \in E( p')$. Using the monotonicity property \eqref{monotonedb}, the doubling property \eqref{firstdb} repeatedly, the definition of $d_{ p}$ and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}, we can bound the previous display by $$ d_{B(x, 4 D^{s})}( cc( u), 	Q(x)) \leq 2^{4a} d_{ p_s}( cc( u), 	Q(x)) \le 2^{4a} 2^{s - \overline{\sigma}( u, x)} d_{ p'}( cc( u), 	Q(x))\,. $$ Since $ cc( u) \in B_{ p'}( cc( p'), 4)$ by \eqref{forest1} and $	Q(x) \in \Omega( p') \subset B_{ p'}( cc( p'), 1)$ by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}, this is estimated by $$ \le 5 \cdot 2^{4a} 2^{s - \overline{\sigma}( u, x)} \,. $$ Using \eqref{eq-Ks-size}, it follows that $$ \eqref{eq-term-A} \le 5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}( u, x)}  rac{1}{\mu(B(x,D^s))}\int_{B(x,0.5D^{s})}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-J-partition}, the collection $\mathcal{J}$ is a partition of $ igcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I$, so this is estimated by $$ 5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}( u, x)}  rac{1}{\mu(B(x,D^s))}\sum_{\substack{J \in \mathcal{J}( T( u))\J \cap B(x, 0.5D^s) 
e \emptyset} }\int_{J}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ This expression does not change if we replace $|f|$ by $P_{\mathcal{J}( T( u))}|f|$. Let $J \in \mathcal{J}( T( u))$ with $B(x, 0.5 D^s) \cap J 
e \emptyset$. By the triangle inequality and since $x \in E( p_s) \subset B(\pc( p_s), 4D^{s})$, it follows that $B(\pc( p_s), 4.5D^s) \cap J 
e \emptyset$. If $s(J) \ge s$ and $s(J) > -S$, then it follows from the triangle inequality, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{defineD} that $\scI( p_s) \subset B(c(J), 100 D^{s(J)+1})$, contradicting $J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{T}( u))$. Thus $s(J) \le s - 1$ or $s(J) = -S$. If $s(J) = -S$ and $s(J) > s - 1$, then $s = -S$. Thus we always have $s(J) \le s$. It then follows from the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} that $J \subset B(\pc( p_s), 16 D^s)$. Thus we can continue our chain of estimates with $$ 5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}( u, x)}  rac{1}{\mu(B(x,D^s))}\int_{B(\pc( p_s),16 D^s)}P_{\mathcal{J}( T( u))}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ We have $B(\pc( p_s), 16D^s)) \subset B(x, 32D^s)$, by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality, since $x \in \scI( p_s)$. Combining this with the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, we obtain $$ \mu(B(\pc( p_s), 16D^s)) \le 2^{5a} \mu(B(x, D^s))\,. $$ Since $a \ge 4$, it follows that \eqref{eq-term-A} is bounded by $$ 5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}( u, x)}  rac{1}{\mu(B(\pc( p_s),16D^s))}\int_{B(\pc( p_s),16D^s)}P_{\mathcal{J}( T( u))}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ Since $L \in \mathcal{L}( T( u))$ and $x\in L \cap \scI( p_s)$, we have $s(L) \le \ps( p_s)$. It follows by \eqref{dyadicproperty} that $L \subset \scI( p_s)$, in particular $x' \in \scI( p_s) \subset B(\pc( p_s), 16D^s)$. Thus $$ \le 5\cdot 2^{104a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}( u, x)} M_{\mathcal{B}, 1}P_{\mathcal{J}( T( u))}|f|(x') $$ $$ \le 10\cdot 2^{104a^3} M_{\mathcal{B}, 1}P_{\mathcal{J}( T( u))}|f|(x')\,. $$ This completes the estimate for term \eqref{eq-term-A}.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the phase error by the frequency distance, which decays geometrically below the top scale; then compare averages to the maximal function of the projected $|f|$.

nodes.name: second tree pointwise
nodes.statement: For all $\fu \in \fU$, all $L \in \mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))$, all $x, x' \in L$ and all bounded $f$ with bounded support, we have $$ \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma(\fu, x)} \int K_s(x,y) P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \le T_{\mathcal{N}}^{\fcc(\fu)} P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))} f(x')\,. $$
assumptions: For all $\fu \in \fU$, all $L \in \mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))$, all $x, x' \in L$ and all bounded $f$ with bounded support
nodes.statement_short: The projected term is bounded by the nontangential operator.
nodes.label: second-tree-pointwise

nodes.name: Proof of second tree pointwise
nodes.statement: Let $s_1 = \underline{\sigma}(\fu, x)$. By definition, there exists a tile $\fp \in \fT(\fu)$ with $\ps(\fp) = s_1$ and $x \in E(\fp)$. Then $x \in \scI(\fp) \cap L$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty} and the definition of $\mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))$, it follows that $L \subset \scI(\fp)$, in particular $x' \in \scI(\fp)$, so $x \in I_{s_1}(x')$. Next, let $s_2 = \overline{\sigma}(\fu, x)$ and let $\fp' \in \fT(\fu)$ with $\ps(\fp') = s_2$ and $x \in E(\fp')$. Since $\fp' \in \fT(\fu)$, we have $4\fp' \lesssim \fu$. Since $\tQ(x) \in \fc(\fp')$, it follows that $$ d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fu), \tQ(x)) \le 5\,. $$ Applying the doubling property \eqref{firstdb} five times, we obtain $$ d_{B(c(\fp), 8D^{s_2})}(\fcc(\fu), \tQ(x)) \le 5 \cdot 2^{5a}\,. $$ By the triangle inequality, we have $B(x, D^{s_2}) \subset B(c(\fp), 8 D^{s_2})$, so by \eqref{monotonedb} $$ d_{B(x, D^{s_2})}(\fcc(\fu), \tQ(x)) \le 5 \cdot 2^{5a}\,. $$ Finally, by applying \eqref{seconddb} $100a$ times, we obtain $$ d_{B(x, D^{s_2-1})}(\fcc(\fu), \tQ(x)) \le 5 \cdot 2^{-95a} < 1\,. $$ Consequently, $D^{s_2 - 1} < R_Q(\fcc(\fu), x)$. The lemma now follows from the definition of $T_{\mathcal{N}}$.
nodes.statement_short: The scale range at $x$ is admissible for the nontangential operator at $x'$ since the frequency distance at the top scale is small.

nodes.name: third tree pointwise
nodes.statement: For all $\fu \in \fU$, all $L \in \mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))$, all $x, x' \in L$ and all bounded $f$ with bounded support, we have \begin{equation*} \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma(\fu, x)} \int K_s(x,y) (f(y) - P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))} f(y)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \end{equation*} \begin{equation*} \le 2^{128a^3} S_{1,\fu} P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}|f|(x')\,. \end{equation*}
assumptions: For all $\fu \in \fU$, all $L \in \mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))$, all $x, x' \in L$ and all bounded $f$ with bounded support
nodes.statement_short: The projection error term is bounded by the auxiliary operator $S_{1,\fu}$.
nodes.label: third-tree-pointwise

nodes.name: Proof of third tree pointwise
nodes.statement:
We have for $J \in \mathcal{J}( T( u))$: $$ \int_J K_{s}(x,y)(1 - P_{\mathcal{J}( T( u))})f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$  egin{equation} = \int_J  rac{1}{\mu(J)} \int_J K_s(x,y) - K_s(x,z) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(z) \,f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. \end{equation} By \eqref{eq-Ks-smooth} and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, we have for $y, z \in J$ $$ |K_s(x,y) - K_s(x,z)| \le  rac{2^{127a^3}}{\mu(B(x, D^s))} \left( rac{8 D^{s(J)}}{D^s}ight)^{1/a}\,. $$ Suppose that $s \in \sigma( u, x)$. If $K_s(x,y) 
e 0$ for some $y \in J \in \mathcal{J}( T( u))$ then, by \eqref{supp-Ks}, $y \in B(x, 0.5 D^s) \cap J 
e \emptyset$. Let $ p \in  T( u)$ with $\ps( p) = s$ and $x \in E( p)$. Then $B(\pc( p_s), 4.5D^s) \cap J 
e \emptyset$ by the triangle inequality. If $s(J) \ge s$ and $s(J) > -S$, then it follows from the triangle inequality, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{defineD} that $\scI( p) \subset B(c(J), 100 D^{s(J)+1})$, contradicting $J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{T}( u))$. Thus $s(J) \le s - 1$ or $s(J) = -S$. If $s(J) = -S$ and $s(J) > s - 1$, then $s = -S$. So in both cases, $s(J) \le s$. It then follows from the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} that $J \subset B(x, 16 D^s)$. Thus, we can estimate \eqref{eq-term-C} by $$ 2^{127a^3 + 3/a}\sum_{ p\in \mathfrak{T}} rac{\mathbf{1}_{E( p)}(x)}{\mu(B(x,D^{\ps( p)}))}\sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}( T( u))\J\subset B(x, 16D^{\ps( p)})\ s(J) \le \ps( p)}} D^{(s(J) - \ps( p))/a} \int_J |f|\,. $$ $$ = 2^{127a^3 + 3/a}\sum_{I \in \mathcal{D}} \sum_{\substack{ p\in \mathfrak{T}\ \scI( p) = I}} rac{\mathbf{1}_{E( p)}(x)}{\mu(B(x, D^{s(I)}))}\sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}( T( u))\J\subset B(x, 16 D^{s(I)})\ s(J) \le s(I)}} D^{(s(J) - s(I))/a} \int_J |f|\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} and \eqref{defineep}, the sets $E( p)$ for tiles $ p$ with $\scI( p) = I$ are pairwise disjoint. It follows from the definition of $\mathcal{L}( T( u))$ that $x \in \scI( p)$ if and only if $x' \in \scI( p)$, thus we can estimate the sum over $\mathbf{1}_{E( p)}(x)$ by $\mathbf{1}_{I}(x')$. If $x \in E( p)$ then in particular $x \in \scI( p)$, so by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} $B(c(I),16D^{s(I)}) \subset B(x, 32D^{s(I)})$. By the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $$ \mu(B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)})) \le 2^{5a} \mu(B(x, D^{s(I)}))\,. $$ Since $a \ge 4$ we can continue our estimate with $$ \le 2^{128a^3}\sum_{I \in \mathcal{D}}  rac{\mathbf{1}_{I}(x')}{\mu(B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)}))}\sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}( T( u))\J\subset B(x, 16 D^{s(I)})\ s(J) \le s(I)}} D^{(s(J) - s(I))/a} \int_J |f| $$ $$ = 2^{128a^3} S_{1, u} P_{\mathcal{J}( T( u))}|f|(x')\,. $$ This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Use cancellation of $f-P_{\mathcal{J}}f$ on each $J$ with kernel smoothness, then reorganize by cubes to recognize $S_{1,\fu}$.

nodes.name: Equation (382)
nodes.statement: = \int_J \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \int_J K_s(x,y) - K_s(x,z) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(z) \,f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.
nodes.label: eq-canc-comp

nodes.name: tree projection estimate
nodes.statement: Let $\fu \in \fU$. Then we have for all $f, g$ bounded with bounded support $$ \Bigg|\int_X \sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} \bar g(y) T_{\fp}f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| $$ \begin{equation} \le 2^{130a^3}\|P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}|f|\|_{2}\|P_{\mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))}|g|\|_{2}. \end{equation}
assumptions: Let $\fu \in \fU$.
for all $f, g$ bounded with bounded support
nodes.statement_short: $L^2$ tree bound in terms of the projections onto $\mathcal{J}$- and $\mathcal{L}$-cubes.
nodes.label: tree-projection-estimate

nodes.name: nontangential operator bound
nodes.statement: For all bounded $f$ with bounded support and all $\mfa \in \Mf$ $$ \|T_{\mathcal{N}}^{\mfa} f\|_2 \le 2^{102a^3} \|f\|_2\,. $$
assumptions: For all bounded $f$ with bounded support and all $\mfa \in \Mf$
nodes.label: nontangential-operator-bound

nodes.name: boundary operator bound
nodes.statement: For all $\fu \in \fU$ and all bounded functions $f$ with bounded support \begin{equation} \|S_{1,\fu}f\|_2 \le 2^{12a} \|f\|_2\,. \end{equation}
assumptions: For all $\fu \in \fU$ and all bounded functions $f$ with bounded support
nodes.label: boundary-operator-bound

nodes.name: Proof of tree projection estimate
nodes.statement: Let $L \in \mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))$. Let $b(x')$ denote the right-hand side of \Cref{pointwise-tree-estimate}. Apply this lemma to $e(\fcc(\fu)) f$, to obtain for all $y, x' \in L$ $$ \Bigg| \sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp} f(y) \Bigg| \le b(x'). $$ Hence, by taking an infimum, we have for $y \in L$ $$ \Bigg| \sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp} f(y) \Bigg| \le \inf_{x' \in L} b(x'). $$ Integrating this estimate yields $$ \int_L |g(y)| \Bigg| \sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp} f(y) \Bigg| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ $$ \le \int_L |g(y)| \times \inf_{x' \in L} b(x') \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ $$ = \int_L P_{\mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))}|g|(y) \times \inf_{x' \in L} b(x') \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ $$ \le \int_L P_{\mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))}|g|(y) \times b(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ By \eqref{definetp}, we have $T_{\fp} f = \mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fp)} T_{\fp} f$ for all $\fp \in \fP$, so $$ \Bigg| \int \bar g(y) \sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| = \Bigg| \int_{\bigcup_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} \scI(\fp)} \bar g(y) \sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|\,. $$ Since $\mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))$ partitions $\bigcup_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} \scI(\fp)$ by \Cref{dyadic-partitions}, we get from the triangle inequality $$ \le \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))} \int_L |g(y)| \Bigg| \sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp} f(y) \Bigg| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ which by the above computation is bounded by $$ \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))} \int_L P_{\mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))}|g|(y) \times b(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ $$ = \int_X P_{\mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))}|g|(y) \times b(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ Applying Cauchy-Schwarz, this is bounded by $\|P_{\mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))}|g|\|_2 \times \|b\|_2$. By Minkowski's inequality, \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood}, \Cref{nontangential-operator-bound} and \Cref{boundary-operator-bound}, $\|b\|_2$ is at most $$ 2^{129a^3} (2^{2a+1} + 2^{12a})\|P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}|f|\|_2 + 2^{103a^3} \|P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}[e(\fcc(\fu))f]\|_2\,. $$ By the triangle inequality we have for all $x \in X$ that $|P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}[e(\fcc(\fu))f]|(x) \le P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}|f|(x)$, thus we can further estimate the above by $$ (2^{129a^3} (2^{2a+1} + 2^{12a}) + 2^{103a^3}) \|P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}|f|\|_2\,. $$ This completes the proof since $a \ge 4$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the pointwise bound of \Cref{pointwise-tree-estimate} over the $\mathcal{L}$-partition, apply Cauchy-Schwarz and the $L^2$ bounds for the three operators.

nodes.name: Proof of nontangential operator bound
nodes.statement: Fix $s_1, s_2$. By \eqref{eq-psisum} we have for all $x \in (0, \infty)$ $$ \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \psi(D^{-s}x) = 1 - \sum_{s < s_1} \psi(D^{-s}x) - \sum_{s > s_1} \psi(D^{-s}x)\,. $$ Since $\psi$ is supported in $[\frac{1}{4D}, \frac{1}{2}]$, the two sums on the right hand side are zero for all $x \in [\frac{1}{2}D^{s_1-1}, \frac{1}{4} D^{s_2 - 1}]$, hence $$ x \in [\frac{1}{2}D^{s_1-1}, \frac{1}{4} D^{s_2}] \implies \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \psi(D^{-s}x) = 1\,. $$ Since $\psi$ is supported in $[\frac{1}{4D}, \frac{1}{2}]$, we further have $$ x \notin [\frac{1}{4}D^{s_1 - 1}, \frac{1}{2}D^{s_2}] \implies \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \psi(D^{-s}x) = 0\,. $$ Finally, since $\psi \ge 0$ and $\sum_{s \in \mathbb{Z}} \psi(D^{-s}x) = 1$, we have for all $x$ $$ 0 \le \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \psi(D^{-s}x) \le 1\,. $$ Let $x' \in I_{s_1}(x)$ and suppose that $D^{s_2 - 1} \le R_Q(\mfa, x')$. By the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, it holds that $\rho(x,x') \le 8D^{s_1}$. We have $$ \Bigg|\sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \int K_s(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\Bigg| $$ $$ = \Bigg|\int \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \psi(D^{-s}\rho(x',y)) K(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\Bigg| $$ \begin{equation} \le \Bigg| \int_{8D^{s_1} < \rho(x',y) \le \frac{1}{4}D^{s_2-1}} K(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \end{equation} \begin{equation} + \int_{\frac{1}{4}D^{s_1-1} \le \rho(x',y) \le 8D^{s_1}} |K(x', y)| |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \end{equation} \begin{equation} + \int_{\frac{1}{4}D^{s_2-1} \le \rho(x',y) \le \frac{1}{2}D^{s_2}} |K(x', y)| |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. \end{equation} The first term \eqref{eq-sharp-trunc-term} is at most $2T_{\tQ}^\mfa f(x)$, using with $R_1 := 8D^{s_1}$, $R_2 := \frac{1}{4}D^{s_2-1}$ and $R_1 < R_2 < R_{\tQ}(\mfa,x')$ the triangle inequality in the form \begin{equation} \left|\int_{R_1 < \rho(x',y) \le R_2} K(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \left|\int_{R_1 < \rho(x',y) < R_{\tQ}(\mfa,x')} K(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right| \end{equation} \begin{equation} + \left|\int_{R_2 < \rho(x',y) < R_{\tQ}(\mfa,x')} K(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right|. \end{equation} The other two terms will be estimated by the finitary maximal function from \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood}. For the second term \eqref{eq-lower-bound-term} we use \eqref{eqkernel-size} which implies that for all $y$ with $\rho(x', y) \ge \frac{1}{4}D^{s_1 - 1}$, we have $$ |K(x', y)| \le \frac{2^{a^3}}{\mu(B(x', \frac{1}{4}D^{s_1 - 1}))}\,. $$ Using $D=2^{100a^2}$ and the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $7 +100a^2$ times estimates the last display by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{7a+101a^3}}{\mu(B(x', 32D^{s_1}))}\, . \end{equation} By the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, we have $$ B(x', 8D^{s_1}) \subset B(c(I_{s_1}(x)), 16D^{s(I_{s_1}(x))}) \subset B(x', 32D^{s_1})\,. $$ Combining this with \eqref{pf-nontangential-operator-bound-imeq}, we conclude that \eqref{eq-lower-bound-term} is at most $$ 2^{7a + 101a^3} M_{\mathcal{B},1} f(x)\,. $$ For \eqref{eq-upper-bound-term} we argue similarly. We have for all $y$ with $\rho(x', y) \ge \frac{1}{4}D^{s_2-1}$ $$ |K(x', y)| \le \frac{2^{a^3}}{\mu(B(x', \frac{1}{4}D^{s_2-1}))}\,. $$ Using the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $7 + 100a^2$ times estimates the last display by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{7a + 101a^3}}{\mu(B(x', 32 D^{s_2}))}\, . \end{equation} Note that by \eqref{dyadicproperty} we have $I_{s_1}(x) \subset I_{s_2}(x)$, in particular $x' \in I_{s_2}(x)$. By the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, we have $$ B(x', 8D^{s_2}) \subset B(c(I_{s_2}(x)), 16D^{s(I_{s_2}(x))}) \subset B(x', 32D^{s_2})\,. $$ Combining this, \eqref{eq-upper-bound-term} is at most $$ 2^{7a+101a^3} M_{\mathcal{B},1} f(x)\,. $$ Using $a \ge 4$, taking a supremum over all $x' \in I_{s_1}(x)$ and then a supremum over all $-S \le s_1 < s_2 \le S$, we obtain $$ T_{\mathcal{N}} f(x) \le 2T_{\tQ}^\mfa f(x) + 2^{102a^3} M_{\mathcal{B},1} f(x)\,. $$ The lemma now follows from assumption \eqref{linnontanbound}, \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood} and $a \ge 4$.

nodes.statement: For every cube $I \in \mathcal{D}$, there exist at most $2^{9a}$ cubes $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(J) = s(I)$ and $B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)}) \cap B(c(J), 16 D^{s(J)}) \ne \emptyset$.
assumptions: For every cube $I \in \mathcal{D}$
conclusions: there exist at most $2^{9a}$ cubes $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(J) = s(I)$ and $B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)}) \cap B(c(J), 16 D^{s(J)}) \ne \emptyset$.

nodes.name: Proof of boundary overlap
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)}) \cap B(c(J), 16 D^{s(J)}) 
e \emptyset$ and $s(I) = s(J)$. Then $B(c(I), 33 D^{s(I)}) \subset B(c(J), 128 D^{s(J)})$. Hence by the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $$ 2^{9a}\mu(B(c(J),  rac{1}{4}D^{s(J)})) \ge \mu(B(c(I), 33 D^{s(I)}))\,, $$ and by the triangle inequality, $B(c(J),  rac{1}{4}D^{s(J)})$ is contained in $B(c(I), 33 D^{s(I)})$. If $\mathcal{C}$ is any finite collection of cubes $J \in \mathcal{D}$ satisfying $s(J) = s(I)$ and  egin{equation*} B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)}) \cap B(c(J), 16 D^{s(J)}) 
e\emptyset\ , \end{equation*} then it follows from \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and pairwise disjointedness of cubes of the same scale \eqref{dyadicproperty} that the balls $B(c(J),  rac{1}{4} D^{s(J)})$ are pairwise disjoint. Hence  egin{align*} \mu(B(c(I), 33 D^{s(I)})) &\ge \sum_{J \in \mathcal{C}} \mu(B(c(J),  rac{1}{4}D^{s(J)}))\ &\ge |\mathcal{C}| 2^{-9a} \mu(B(c(I), 33 D^{s(I)}))\,. \end{align*} Since $\mu$ is doubling and $\mu 
e 0$, we have $\mu(B(c(I), 33D^{s(I)})) > 0$. The lemma follows after dividing by $2^{-9a}\mu(B(c(I), 33D^{s(I)}))$.
nodes.statement_short: Doubling and disjointness of inner balls of same-scale cubes bound their number.

nodes.name: Proof of boundary operator bound
nodes.statement: Note that by definition, $S_{1,\fu}f$ is a finite sum of indicator functions of cubes $I \in \mathcal{D}$ for each locally integrable $f$, and hence is bounded, has bounded support and is integrable. Let $g$ be another function with the same three properties. Then $\bar g S_{1,\fu}f$ is integrable, and we have $$ \Bigg|\int \bar g(y) S_{1,\fu}f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\Bigg| $$ \begin{multline*} = \Bigg|\sum_{I\in\mathcal{D}} \frac{1}{\mu(B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)}))} \int_I \bar g(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\\ \times \sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))\,:\,J\subseteq B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)})\\s(J)\le s(I)}} D^{(s(J)-s(I))/a}\int_J |f(y)| \,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\Bigg| \end{multline*} \begin{multline*} \le \sum_{I\in\mathcal{D}} \frac{1}{\mu(B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)}))} \int_{B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)})} | g(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\\ \times \sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))\,:\,J\subseteq B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)})\\ s(J) \le s(I)}} D^{(s(J)-s(I))/a}\int_J |f(y)| \,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. \end{multline*} Changing the order of summation and using $J \subset B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)})$ to bound the first average integral by $M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|(y)$ for any $y \in J$, we obtain \begin{align} \le \sum_{J\in\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}\int_J|f(y)| M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D} \, : \, J\subset B(c(I),16 D^{s(I)})\\ s(I) \ge s(J)}} D^{(s(J)-s(I))/a}. \end{align} By \Cref{boundary-overlap}, there are at most $2^{9a}$ cubes $I$ at each scale satisfying the inclusion $J \subset B(c(I),16D^{s(I)})$. Since $D^{-1/a}\le\frac12$, $(1 - D^{-1/a})^{-1} \le 2$. Using this estimate for the sum of the geometric series, we conclude that \eqref{eq-boundary-operator-bound-1} is at most $$ 2^{9a+1} \sum_{J\in\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}\int_J|f(y)| M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ The collection $\mathcal{J}$ is a partition of $\bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I$, so this equals $$ 2^{9a+1} \int_X|f(y)| M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ Using Cauchy-Schwarz and \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood}, we conclude $$ \left|\int \bar g S_{1,\fu}f \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right| \le 2^{12a} \|g\|_2\|f\|_2\,. $$ The lemma now follows by choosing $g = S_{1,\fu}f$ and dividing on both sides by the finite $\|S_{1,\fu}f\|_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Duality: swap sums, bound averages of $g$ by the maximal function, count overlapping cubes by \Cref{boundary-overlap} and sum the geometric series.

nodes.name: Proof of densities tree bound
nodes.statement: Denote $$ \mathcal{E}(\fu) = \bigcup_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} E(\fp)\,. $$ Then we have $$ \left| \int_X \bar g \sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp} f \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right| = \left| \int_X \overline{ g\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{E}(\fu)}} \sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp} (\mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fu)}f) \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right|\,. $$ By \Cref{tree-projection-estimate}, this is bounded by \begin{equation} \le 2^{130a^3}\|P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}|f|\|_2 \|P_{\mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))} |\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{E}(\fu)}g|\|_2\,. \end{equation} We bound the two factors separately. We have $$ \|P_{\mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))} |\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{E}(\fu)}g|\|_2 = \left( \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))} \frac{1}{\mu(L)} \left(\int_{L \cap \mathcal{E}(\fu)} |g(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right)^2 \right)^{1/2}\,. $$ By Cauchy-Schwarz and \Cref{local-dens1-tree-bound} this is at most $$ \le \left( \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))} 2^{101a^3} \dens_1(\fT(\fu)) \int_{L \cap \mathcal{E}(\fu)} |g(y)|^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right)^{1/2}\,. $$ Since cubes $L \in \mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu))$ are pairwise disjoint by \Cref{dyadic-partitions}, this is \begin{equation} \le 2^{51 a^3} \dens_1(\fT(\fu))^{1/2} \|g\|_2\,. \end{equation} Similarly, we have \begin{equation} \|P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))}|f|\|_2 = \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))} \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right)^2 \right)^{1/2}\,. \end{equation} By Cauchy-Schwarz, this is $$ \le \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))} \int_J |f(y)|^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right)^{1/2}\,. $$ Since cubes in $\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))$ are pairwise disjoint by \Cref{dyadic-partitions}, this is at most \begin{equation} \|f\|_2\,. \end{equation} Combining \eqref{eq-both-factors-tree}, \eqref{eq-factor-L-tree} and \eqref{eq-factor-J-tree} gives \eqref{eq-cor-tree-est}. If $f \le \mathbf{1}_F$ then $f = f\mathbf{1}_F$, so $$ \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))} \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right)^2 \right)^{1/2} $$ $$ =\left(\sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))} \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_{J \cap F} |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right)^2 \right)^{1/2}\,. $$ We estimate as before, using now \Cref{local-dens2-tree-bound} and Cauchy-Schwarz, and obtain that this is $$ \le 2^{101a^3} \dens_2(\fT(\fu))^{1/2} \|f\|_2\,. $$ Combining this with \eqref{eq-both-factors-tree} and \eqref{eq-factor-L-tree} gives \eqref{eq-cor-tree-est-F}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply \Cref{tree-projection-estimate} to $g\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{E}(\fu)}$ and bound the two projection factors by Cauchy-Schwarz with \Cref{local-dens1-tree-bound} and \Cref{local-dens2-tree-bound}.

nodes.name: Proof of local dens1 tree bound
nodes.statement:
If the set on the right hand side is empty, then \eqref{eq-1density-estimate-tree} holds. If not, then there exists $ p \in  T( u)$ with $L \cap \scI( p) 
e \emptyset$. Suppose first that there exists such $ p$ with $\ps( p) \le s(L)$. Then by \eqref{dyadicproperty} $\scI( p) \subset L$, which gives by the definition of $\mathcal{L}( T( u))$ that $s(L) = -S$ and hence $L = \scI( p)$. Let $ q \in  T( u)$ with $E( q) \cap L 
e \emptyset$. Since $s(L) = -S \le \ps( q)$ it follows from \eqref{dyadicproperty} that $\scI( p) = L \subset \scI( q)$. We have then by \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}  egin{align*} d_{ p}( cc( p),  cc( q)) &\le d_{ p}( cc( p),  cc( u)) + d_{ p}( cc( q),  cc( u))\ &\le d_{ p}( cc( p),  cc( u)) + d_{ q}( cc( q),  cc( u))\,. \end{align*} Using that $ p,  q \in  T( u)$ and \eqref{forest1}, this is at most $8$. Using again the triangle inequality and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}, we obtain that for each $q \in B_{ q}( cc( q), 1)$ $$ d_{ p}( cc( p), q) \le d_{ p}( cc( p),  cc( q)) + d_{ q}( cc( q), q) \le 9\,. $$ Thus $L \cap G \cap E( q) \subset E_2(9,  p)$. We obtain $$ \mu(L \cap G \cap  igcup_{ q \in  T( u)} E( q)) \le \mu(E_2(9,  p))\,. $$ By the definition of $\dens_1$, this is bounded by $$ 9^a \dens_1( T( u)) \mu(\scI( p)) =9^a \dens_1( T( u)) \mu(L)\,. $$ Since $a \ge 4$, \eqref{eq-1density-estimate-tree} follows in this case. Now suppose that for each $ p \in  T( u)$ with $L \cap E( p) 
e \emptyset$, we have $\ps( p) > s(L)$. Since there exists at least one such $ p$, there exists in particular at least one cube $L'' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $L \subset L''$ and $s(L'') > s(L)$. By \eqref{coverdyadic}, there exists $L' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $L \subset L'$ and $s(L') = s(L) + 1$. By the definition of $\mathcal{L}( T( u))$ there exists a tile $ p'' \in  T( u)$ with $\scI( p'') \subset L'$. It suffices to show that there exists a tile $ p' \in  P( T( u))$ with $\scI( p') = L'$, $d_{ p'}( cc( p'),  cc( u)) < 4$ and $9 p'' \lesssim 9 p'$. For then, let $ q \in  T( u)$ with $L \cap E( q) 
e \emptyset$. As shown above, this implies $\ps( q) \ge s(L')$, so by \eqref{dyadicproperty} $L' \subset \scI( q)$. If $q \in B_{ q}( cc( q), 1)$, then by a similar calculation as above, using the triangle inequality, \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and \eqref{forest1}, we obtain $$ d_{ p'}( cc( p'), q) \le d_{ p'}( cc( p'),  cc( q)) + d_{ q}( cc( q), q) \le 9\,. $$ Thus $L \cap G \cap E( q) \subset E_2(9,  p')$. We deduce using the definition \eqref{definedens1} of $\dens_1$ $$ \mu(L \cap G \cap  igcup_{ q \in  T( u)} E( q)) \le \mu(E_2(9,  p')) \le 9^a \dens_1( T( u)) \mu(L')\,. $$ Using the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, and $a \ge 4$ this is estimated by $$ 9^a 2^{100a^3 + 5a}\dens_1( T( u)) \mu(L) \le 2^{101 a^3} \dens_1( T( u))\mu(L)\,. $$ To show existence of $ p'$ with the given properties, if $\scI( p'') = L'$ we can take $ p' =  p''$, which satisfies the distance property by \eqref{forest1} and the other properties trivially. Otherwise, let $ p'$ be the unique tile such that $\scI( p') = L'$ and such that $\Omega( u) \cap \Omega( p') 
e \emptyset$. Since $\scI( p') \subset \scI( p)$ and $ p \in  T( u)$, we have $ p' \in  P( T( u))$. Since by \eqref{forest1} $\ps( p') = s(L') \le \ps( p) < \ps( u)$, we have by \eqref{dyadicproperty} and \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic} that $\Omega( u) \subset \Omega( p')$, and hence the distance property. $9 p'' \lesssim 9 p'$ follows by the triangle inequality, \eqref{forest1}, \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}. This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Find a tile at the cube $L$ or its parent whose $E_2(9,\cdot)$ contains all relevant $E(\fq)$, and use the definition of $\dens_1$ with doubling.

nodes.name: Proof of local dens2 tree bound
nodes.statement: We prove the inequality with the constant $2^{201a^3}$ replaced by $2 ^ {200a^3 + 14a}$; this is stronger because $a \geq 4$. It suffices to show the existence of a tile $\fp \in \fT(\fu)$ and an $r \geq 4 D ^ {\ps(\fp)}$ such that $J \subset B(\pc(\fp), r)$ and $\mu(B(\pc(\fp), r)) ≤ 2 ^ {200a^3 + 14a} \mu(J)$, because then it follows from the definition \eqref{definedens2} of $\dens_2$ that $$ \mu(F \cap J) \le \mu(F \cap B(\pc(\fp), r)) $$ $$ \le \dens_2(\fT(\fu)) \mu(B(\pc(\fp), r)) \le 2^{200a^3 + 14a} \dens_2(\fT(\fu))\mu(J)\,. $$ In particular, these criteria are satisfied, with $r = 4 D ^ {\ps(\fp)}$, by any $\fp \in \fT(\fu)$ such that $J \subseteq B(\pc(\fp, 4 D ^ {\ps(\fp)}))$ and $\mu(\scI(\fp)) \le 2^{100a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)$, because then by the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, $$ \mu(B(\pc(\fp), 4 D ^ {\ps(\fp)})) \le 2^{4a} \mu(B(\pc(\fp), D ^ {\ps(\fp)} / 4)) $$ $$ \le 2^{4a} \mu(\scI(\fp)) \le 2^{100a^3 + 14a} \mu(J)\,. $$ Suppose first that $s(J) = S$. Then $J = I_0$, so \eqref{subsetmaxcube} and the fact that $J \in \mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu)) \subseteq \mathcal{J}_0(\fT(\fu))$ imply that $s(J) = -S$. Thus $S = 0$. It follows that $J$ is the only dyadic cube, so any $\fp \in \fT(\fu)$ has $\scI(\fp) = J$, and therefore satisfies $J \subseteq B(\pc(\fp, 4 D ^ {\ps(\fp)}))$ and $\mu(\scI(\fp)) \le 2^{100a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)$. It remains to consider the case $s(J) < S$. Then, by \eqref{coverdyadic} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}, there exists some cube $J' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(J') = s(J) + 1$ and $J \subset J'$. By definition of $\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu))$ there exists some $\fp \in \fT(\fu)$ such that $\scI(\fp) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})$. Since $c(J) \in J \subset J' \subset B(c(J'), 4D^{s(J')})$, the triangle inequality, $s(J') = s(J) + 1$ and $D=2^{100a^2}$ imply $$ B(c(J'), 204D^{s(J')+1}) \subset B(c(J), 204D^{s(J') + 1} + 4D^{s(J')}) \subset B(c(J), 2^8 D^{s(J) + 2})\,. $$ From the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, $D=2^{100a^2}$ and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, we obtain \begin{equation} \mu(B(c(J'), 204D^{s(J') + 1})) \leq 2 ^ {200a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)\,. \end{equation} If $J \subset B(\pc(\fp), 4 D^{\ps(\fp)})$, then we need only check that $\mu(\scI(\fp)) \le 2^{100a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)$. This follows immediately from $\scI(\fp) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})$ and \eqref{measure-comparison}. From now on we assume $J \not \subset B(\pc(\fp), 4 D^{\ps(\fp)})$. Since \begin{equation*} \pc(\fp) \in \scI(\fp) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})\, , \end{equation*} we have by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality $$ J \subset J' \subset B(c(J'), 4D^{s(J')}) \subset B(\pc(\fp), 104 D^{s(J') + 1})\,. $$ In particular this implies $104 D^{s(J') + 1} > 4D^{\ps(\fp)}$. By the triangle inequality we also have $$ B(\pc(\fp), 104 D^{s(J') + 1}) \subset B(c(J), 204 D^{s(J') + 1})\,, $$ so from \eqref{measure-comparison}, $$ \mu( B(\pc(\fp), 104 D^{s(J') + 1})) \le 2^{200a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)\,, $$ which proves $\fp$ satisfies the needed criteria with $r=104 D^{s(J') + 1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Find a tile of the tree near the parent cube of $J$ and a ball around it containing $J$ with comparable measure; then use the definition of $\dens_2$.

nodes.name: adjoint tile operator $T_{\fp}^*$
Equation (402)
nodes.statement: T_{\fp}^* g(x) = \int_{E(\fp)} \overline{K_{\ps(\fp)}(y,x)} e(-\tQ(y)(x)+ \tQ(y)(y)) g(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.
nodes.label: definetp*

nodes.name: adjoint tile support
nodes.statement: For each $\fp \in \fP$, we have $$ T_{\fp}^* g = \mathbf{1}_{B(\pc(\fp), 5D^{\ps(\fp)})} T_{\fp}^* \mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fp)} g\,. $$ For each $\fu \in \fU$ and each $\fp \in \fT(\fu)$, we have $$ T_{\fp}^* g = \mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fu)} T_{\fp}^* \mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fu)} g\,. $$
nodes.statement_short: The adjoint tile operator localizes to $B(\pc(\fp),5D^{\ps(\fp)})$ and, inside a tree, to $\scI(\fu)$.
nodes.label: adjoint-tile-support

nodes.name: Proof of adjoint tile support
nodes.statement: By \eqref{forest1}, $E(\fp) \subset \scI(\fp) \subset \scI(\fu)$. Thus by \eqref{definetp*} $$ T_{\fp}^* g(x) = T_{\fp}^* (\mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fp)} g)(x) $$ $$ = \int_{E(\fp)} \overline{K_{\ps(\fp)}(y,x)} e(-\tQ(y)(x) + \tQ(y)(y)) \mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fp)}(y) g(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ If this integral is not $0$, then there exists $y \in \scI(\fp)$ such that $K_{\ps(\fp)}(y,x) \ne 0$. By \eqref{supp-Ks}, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality, it follows that \begin{equation*} x \in B(\pc(\fp), 5 D^{\ps(\fp)})\, . \end{equation*} Thus $$ T_{\fp}^* g(x) = \mathbf{1}_{B(\pc(\fp), 5D^{\ps(\fp)})}(x) T_{\fp}^* (\mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fp)} g)(x)\,. $$ The second claimed equation follows now since $\scI(\fp) \subset \scI(\fu)$ and by \eqref{forest6} we have $B(\pc(\fp), 5D^{\ps(\fp)}) \subset \scI(\fu)$.
nodes.statement_short: Unfold the adjoint and use kernel support with \eqref{forest6}.

nodes.name: adjoint tree estimate
nodes.statement: For all bounded $g$ supported on $G$ we have that $$ \left\| \sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp}^* g\right\|_2 \le 2^{181a^3} \dens_1(\fT(\fu))^{1/2} \|g\|_2\,, $$ $$ \left\| \mathbf{1}_F \sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp}^* g\right\|_2 \le 2^{282a^3} \dens_1(\fT(\fu))^{1/2} \dens_2(\fT(\fu))^{1/2} \|g\|_2\,. $$
assumptions: For all bounded $g$ supported on $G$
nodes.statement_short: Adjoint tree operator bounds with decay in $\dens_1$ (and $\dens_2$ after restricting to $F$).
nodes.label: adjoint-tree-estimate

nodes.name: Proof of adjoint tree estimate
nodes.statement: By \Cref{densities-tree-bound}, we have for all bounded $f$ and $g$ with $|g| \le \mathbf{1}_G$ that $$ \left| \int_X \overline{\sum_{\fp\in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp}^* g} f \,\mathrm{d}\mu \right| = \left| \int_X \overline{g} \sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp} f \,\mathrm{d}\mu \right| $$ \begin{equation} \le 2^{181a^3} \dens_1(\fT(\fu))^{1/2} \|g\|_2 \|f\|_2\,. \end{equation} Let $f = \sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp}^* g$. Since $|g| \le \mathbf{1}_G$, $f$ is bounded and has bounded support. In particular $\|f\|_2 < \infty$. Dividing \eqref{eq-adjoint-bound} by $\|f\|_2$ completes the proof. The proof of the second part is similar with $f = \mathbf{1}_F \sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp}^* g$.

nodes.name: auxiliary operator $S_{2,\fu}$
nodes.statement:
We define
$$
    S_{2,\fu}g := \left|\sum_{\fp \in \fT(\fu)} T_{\fp}^*g \right| + M_{\mathcal{B},1}g + |g|\,.
$$

nodes.name: adjoint tree control
nodes.statement: We have for all $\fu \in \fU$ and all bounded $g$ supported on $G$ $$ \|S_{2, \fu} g\|_2 \le 2^{182a^3} \|g\|_2\,. $$
assumptions: We have for all $\fu \in \fU$ and all bounded $g$ supported on $G$

nodes.name: Proof of adjoint tree control
nodes.statement: This follows immediately from Minkowski's inequality, \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood} and \Cref{adjoint-tree-estimate}, using that $a \ge 4$.

nodes.name: correlation separated trees
nodes.statement: For any $\fu_1 \ne \fu_2 \in \fU$ and all bounded $g_1, g_2$ with bounded support, we have \begin{equation} \left| \int_X \sum_{\fp_1 \in \fT(\fu_1)} \sum_{\fp_2 \in \fT(\fu_2)} T^*_{\fp_1}g_1 \overline{T^*_{\fp_2}g_2 }\,\mathrm{d}\mu \right| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{512a^3-4n} \prod_{j =1}^2 \| S_{2, \fu_j} g_j\|_{L^2(\scI(\fu_1) \cap \scI(\fu_2))}\,. \end{equation}
assumptions: For any $\fu_1 \ne \fu_2 \in \fU$ and all bounded $g_1, g_2$ with bounded support
nodes.statement_short: Almost orthogonality: correlations of adjoint operators of distinct trees decay like $2^{-4n}$.

nodes.name: Proof of correlation separated trees
nodes.statement: By \Cref{adjoint-tile-support} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}, the left hand side \eqref{eq-lhs-sep-tree} is $0$ unless $\scI(\fu_1) \subset \scI(\fu_2)$ or $\scI(\fu_2) \subset \scI(\fu_1)$. Without loss of generality we assume that $\scI(\fu_1) \subset \scI(\fu_2)$. Define \begin{equation} \mathfrak{S} := \{\fp \in \fT(\fu_1) \cup \fT(\fu_2) \ : \ d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2)) \ge 2^{Zn/2}\,\}. \end{equation} \Cref{correlation-separated-trees} follows by combining the definition \eqref{defineZ} of $Z$ with the following two lemmas.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to nested tree cubes, split the second tree by the frequency-separated set $\mathfrak{S}$ and apply the two correlation lemmas.

nodes.statement: \mathfrak{S} := \{\fp \in \fT(\fu_1) \cup \fT(\fu_2) \ : \ d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2)) \ge 2^{Zn/2}\,\}.

nodes.name: overlap implies distance
nodes.statement: Let $\fu_1 \ne \fu_2 \in \fU$ with $\scI(\fu_1) \subset \scI(\fu_2)$. If $\fp \in \fT(\fu_1) \cup \fT(\fu_2)$ with $\scI(\fp) \cap \scI(\fu_1) \ne \emptyset$, then $\fp \in \mathfrak{S}$. In particular, we have $\fT(\fu_1) \subset \mathfrak{S}$.
assumptions: Let $\fu_1 \ne \fu_2 \in \fU$ with $\scI(\fu_1) \subset \scI(\fu_2)$.
If $\fp \in \fT(\fu_1) \cup \fT(\fu_2)$ with $\scI(\fp) \cap \scI(\fu_1) \ne \emptyset$
nodes.label: overlap-implies-distance

nodes.name: Proof of overlap implies distance
nodes.statement: Suppose first that $\fp \in \fT(\fu_1)$. Then $\scI(\fp) \subset \scI(\fu_1) \subset \scI(\fu_2)$, by \eqref{forest1}. Thus we have by the separation condition \eqref{forest5}, \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}, \eqref{forest1} and the triangle inequality \begin{align*} d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2)) &\ge d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp), \fcc(\fu_2)) - d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp), \fcc(\fu_1))\\ &\ge 2^{Z(n+1)} - 4\\ &\ge 2^{Zn/2}\,, \end{align*} using that $Z= 2^{12a}\ge 4$. Hence $\fp \in \mathfrak{S}$. Suppose now that $\fp \in \fT(\fu_2)$. If $\scI(\fp) \subset \scI(\fu_1)$, then the same argument as above with $\fu_1$ and $\fu_2$ swapped shows $\fp \in \mathfrak{S}$. If $\scI(\fp) \not \subset \scI(\fu_1)$ then, by \eqref{dyadicproperty}, $\scI(\fu_1) \subset \scI(\fp)$. Pick $\fp' \in \fT(\fu_1)$, we have $\scI(\fp') \subset \scI(\fu_1) \subset \scI(\fp)$. Hence, by \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and the first paragraph $$ d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2)) \ge d_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2)) \ge 2^{Zn}\,, $$ so $\fp \in \mathfrak{S}$.
nodes.statement_short: Separation \eqref{forest5} with the triangle inequality, and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} for large tiles of the second tree.

nodes.name: notation $T_{\fC}$, $T_{\fC}^*$
nodes.statement:
To simplify the notation, we will write at various places throughout the proof of Lemmas \ref{correlation-distant-tree-parts} and \ref{correlation-near-tree-parts} for a subset $\fC \subset \fP$
$$
    T_{\fC} f := \sum_{\fp \in \fC} T_{\fp} f\,, \quad\quad T_{\fC}^* g := \sum_{\fp\in\fC} T_{\fp}^* g\,.
$$

nodes.name: cubes $\mathcal{J}'$
nodes.statement:
Define
    $$
        \mathcal{J}' = \{J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S}) \ : \ J \subset \scI(\fu_1)\}\,.
    $$

nodes.name: dyadic partition 1
nodes.statement: We have that $$ \scI(\fu_1) = \dot{\bigcup_{J \in \mathcal{J}'}} J\,. $$
nodes.label: dyadic-partition-1

nodes.name: Proof of dyadic partition 1
nodes.statement: By \Cref{dyadic-partitions}, it remains only to show that each $J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$ with $J \cap \scI(\fu_1) \ne \emptyset$ is in $\mathcal{J}'$. But if $J \notin \mathcal{J}'$, then by \eqref{dyadicproperty} $\scI(\fu_1) \subset J$. Pick $\fp \in \fT(\fu_1) \subset \mathfrak{S}$. Then $\scI(\fp) \subset J$. This contradicts the definition of $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$.
nodes.statement_short: Cubes meeting $\scI(\fu_1)$ but not inside it would contain a tile of $\mathfrak{S}$, contradicting the definition of $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$.

nodes.statement:
For each cube $J \in \mathcal{J}$ let $$ 	ilde\chi_J(y) = \mathbf{1}_{\scI( u_1)}(y)\max\{0, 8 - D^{-s(J)} ho(y, c(J))\}\,, $$ and set $$ a(y) = \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} 	ilde \chi_J(y)\,. $$ We define \[ \chi_J(y) :=  rac{	ilde \chi_J(y)}{a(y)}\,. \] Then, due to \eqref{forest6} and \eqref{def-BJ}, the properties \eqref{eq-pao-1} and \eqref{eq-pao-2} are clearly true. Estimate \eqref{eq-pao-3} follows from \eqref{eq-pao-2} if $y, y' 
otin B(J)$. Thus we can assume that $y \in B(J)$. We have by the triangle inequality $$ |\chi_J(y) - \chi_J(y')| \le  rac{|	ilde \chi_J(y) - 	ilde \chi_J(y')|}{a(y)} +  rac{	ilde \chi_J(y')|a(y) - a(y')|}{a(y)a(y')} $$ Since $	ilde \chi_J(z) \ge 4$ for all $z \in B(c(J),4D^{s(J)}) \supset J$ and by \Cref{dyadic-partition-1}, we have that $a(z) \ge 4$ for all $z \in \scI( u_1)$. So we can estimate the above further by $$ \le 2^{-2}(|	ilde \chi_J(y) - 	ilde \chi_J(y')| + 	ilde \chi_J(y')|a(y) - a(y')|)\,. $$ If $y' 
otin B(\pc( p), 8D^{\ps( p)})$ then the second summand vanishes. Else, we can estimate the above, using also that $|	ilde \chi_J(y')| \le 8$, by $$ \le 2^{-2} |	ilde \chi_J(y) - 	ilde \chi_J(y')| + 2 \sum_{\substack{J' \in \mathcal{J}'\ B(J') \cap B(J) 
e \emptyset}}|	ilde \chi_{J'}(y) - 	ilde \chi_{J'} (y')|\,. $$ By the triangle inequality, we have for all dyadic cubes $I$ $$ |	ilde \chi_I(y) - 	ilde \chi_I(y')| \le ho(y, y') D^{-s(I)}\,. $$ Using this above, we obtain $$ |\chi_J(y) - \chi_J(y')| \le ho(y,y') \Big(  rac{1}{4} D^{-s(J)} + 2 \sum_{\substack{J' \in \mathcal{J}'\ B(J') \cap B(J) 
e \emptyset}} D^{-s(J')}\Big)\,. $$ By \Cref{moderate-scale-change}, this is at most $$  rac{ho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}} \left(  rac{1}{4} + 2D |\{J' \in \mathcal{J}' \ : \ B(J') \cap B(J) 
e \emptyset\}|ight)\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \Cref{dyadic-partition-1}, the balls $B(c(J'),  rac{1}{4} D^{s(J')})$ are pairwise disjoint. By the triangle inequality and \Cref{moderate-scale-change}, each such ball for $J'$ in the set of the last display is contained in $$ B(c(J), 9 D^{s(J) + 1})\,. $$ By the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, we further have $$ \mu(B(c(J), 9 D^{s(J) + 1})) \le 2^{200a^3 + 7a} \mu\Big(B(c(J'),  rac{1}{4}D^{s(J')})\Big) $$ for each such ball. Thus $$ |\{J' \in \mathcal{J}' \ : \ B(J') \cap B(J) 
e \emptyset\}| \le 2^{200a^3 + 7a}\,. $$ Recalling that $D=2^{100a^2}$, we obtain $$ rac{1}{4} + 2D |\{J' \in \mathcal{J}' \ : \ B(J') \cap B(J) 
e \emptyset\}|\leq 2^{200a^3 + 100a^2 + 7a + 2}.$$ Since $a\ge 4$, \eqref{eq-pao-3} follows.

nodes.name: Proof of moderate scale change
nodes.statement: Suppose that $s(J') < s(J) - 1$. Then $s(J) > -S$. Thus, by the definition of $\mathcal{J}'$ there exists no $\fp \in \mathfrak{S}$ with \begin{equation} \scI(\fp) \subset B(c(J), 100D^{s(J) + 1})\,. \end{equation} Since $s(J') < s(J)$, there exists a cube $J'' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $J \subset J''$ and $s(J'') = s(J') + 1$. By the definition of $\mathcal{J}'$, there exists a tile $\fp \in \mathfrak{S}$ with \begin{equation} \scI(\fp) \subset B(c(J''), 100 D^{s(J')+2})\,. \end{equation} But by the triangle inequality and \eqref{defineD}, we have $$ B(c(J''), 100 D^{s(J')+2}) \subset B(c(J), 100D^{s(J) + 1})\,, $$ which contradicts \eqref{eq-tile-incl-1} and \eqref{tile-incl-2}.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: a large scale gap would place a tile of $\mathfrak{S}$ inside the forbidden ball of $J$.

nodes.name: Proof of Hölder correlation tile
nodes.statement: By \eqref{definetp*}, we have $$ |e(\fcc(\fu)(y)) T_{\fp}^* g(y) - e(\fcc(\fu)(y')) T_{\fp}^* g(y')| $$ \begin{multline*} =\bigg| \int_{E(\fp)} e(\tQ(x)(x) - \tQ(x)(y) + \fcc(\fu)(y)) \overline{K_{\ps(\fp)}(x, y)} g(x) \\ - e(\tQ(x)(x) - \tQ(x)(y') + \fcc(\fu)(y')) \overline{K_{\ps(\fp)}(x, y')} g(x) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\bigg| \end{multline*} \begin{multline*} \leq\int_{E(\fp)} |g(x)| |e(\tQ(x)(y) - \tQ(x)(y') - \fcc(\fu)(y) + \fcc(\fu)(y'))\overline{K_{\ps(\fp)}(x, y)}\\ - \overline{K_{\ps(\fp)}(x, y')}| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \end{multline*} \begin{multline} \leq\int_{E(\fp)} |g(x)| |e(-\tQ(x)(y) + \tQ(x)(y') + \fcc(\fu)(y) - \fcc(\fu)(y')) - 1| \\ \times |\overline{K_{\ps(\fp)}(x, y)}|\, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \end{multline} \begin{equation} + \int_{E(\fp)} |g(x)| |\overline{K_{\ps(\fp)}(x, y)} - \overline{K_{\ps(\fp)}(x, y')} |\, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. \end{equation} By the oscillation estimate \eqref{osccontrol}, we have $$ |-\tQ(x)(y) + \tQ(x)(y') + \fcc(\fu)(y) - \fcc(\fu)(y')| $$ \begin{equation} \le d_{B(y, 1.6\rho(y,y'))}(\tQ(x), \fcc(\fu))\,. \end{equation} Suppose that $y, y' \in B(\pc(\fp), 5D^{\ps(\fp)})$, so that $\rho(y,y') \le 10D^{\ps(\fp)}$. Let $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ be such that $2^{ak}\rho(y,y') \le 10D^{\ps(\fp)}$ but $2^{a(k+1)} \rho(y,y') > 10D^{\ps(\fp)}$. In particular, $k \ge 0$. Then, using \eqref{seconddb} followed by \eqref{firstdb}, we can bound \eqref{eq-lem-tile-Holder-comp} from above by $$ 2^{-k} d_{B(\pc(\fp), 16 D^{\ps(\fp)})}(\tQ(x), \fcc(\fu)) \le 2^{6a - k} d_{\fp}(\tQ(x), \fcc(\fu))\,. $$ Since $x \in E(\fp)$ we have $\tQ(x) \in \Omega(\fp) \subset B_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp), 1)$, and since $\fp \in \fT(\fu)$ we have $\fcc(\fu) \in B_{\fp}(\fcc(\fp), 4)$, so this is estimated by $$ \le 5 \cdot 2^{6a - k}\,. $$ By definition of $k$, we have $$ -k < 1 - \frac{1}{a} \log_2\left(\frac{10 D^{\ps(\fp)}}{\rho(y,y')}\right)\,, $$ which gives \begin{equation} |-\tQ(x)(y) + \tQ(x)(y') + \fcc(\fu)(y) - \fcc(\fu)(y')| \le 10 \cdot 2^{6a} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{10 D^{\ps(\fp)}}\right)^{1/a}\,. \end{equation} For all $x \in \scI(\fp)$, we have by \eqref{doublingx} that $$ \mu(B(x, D^{\ps(\fp)})) \ge 2^{-3a} \mu(B(\pc(\fp), 4D^{\ps(\fp)}))\,. $$ Combining the above with \eqref{eq-Ks-size}, \eqref{eq-Ks-smooth} and \eqref{eq-lem-Tile-holder-im1}, we obtain $$ \eqref{T*Holder1b}+\eqref{T*Holder1} \le \frac{2^{3a}}{\mu(B(\pc(\fp), 4D^{\ps(\fp)}))} \int_{E(\fp)}|g(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \times $$ $$ (2^{102a^3} \cdot 10 \cdot 2^{6a} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{ D^{\ps(\fp)}}\right)^{1/a} + 2^{127a^3} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{\ps(\fp)}}\right)^{1/a}) $$ Since $\rho(y,y') \le 10 D^{\ps(\fp)}$, we conclude $$ \eqref{T*Holder1b}+\eqref{T*Holder1} \le \frac{2^{128a^3}}{\mu(B(\pc(\fp), 4D^{\ps(\fp)}))} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{\ps(\fp)}}\right)^{1/a} \int_{E(\fp)}|g(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. $$ Next, if $y,y' \notin B(\pc(\fp), 5D^{\ps(\fp)})$, then $T_{\fp}^*g(y) = T_{\fp}^*g(y') = 0$, by \Cref{adjoint-tile-support}. Then \eqref{T*Holder2} holds. Finally, if $y \in B(\pc(\fp), 5D^{\ps(\fp)})$ and $y' \notin B(\pc(\fp), 5D^{\ps(\fp)})$, then $$ |e(\fcc(\fu)(y)) T_{\fp}^* g(y) - e(\fcc(\fu)(y')) T_{\fp}^* g(y')| = |T_{\fp}^* g(y)| $$ $$ \le \int_{E(\fp)} |K_{\ps(\fp)}(x,y)| |g(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. $$ By the same argument used to prove \eqref{eq-Ks-aux}, this is bounded by \begin{equation} \le 2^{102a^3} \int_{E(\fp)} \frac{1}{\mu(B(x, D^s))} \psi(D^{-s} \rho(x,y)) |g(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. \end{equation} It follows from the definition of $\psi$ that $$ \psi(x) \le \max\{0, (2 - 4x)^{1/a}\}\,. $$ Now for all $x\in E(\fp)$, it follows by the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} that \begin{multline*} 2 - 4D^{-\ps(\fp)}\rho(x,y)\leq 2 - 4D^{-\ps(\fp)}\rho(y, \pc(\fp)) + 4 D^{-\ps(\fp)}\rho(x, \pc(\fp))\\\leq 18 - 4 D^{-\ps(\fp)} \rho(y, \pc(\fp)) \leq 4 D^{-\ps(\fp)}\rho(y,y') - 2 . \end{multline*} Combining the above with the previous estimate on $\psi$, we get $$ \psi(D^{-\ps(\fp)}\rho(x,y)) \le 4 (D^{-\ps(\fp)}\rho(y,y'))^{1/a}. $$ Further, we obtain from the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} that $$ \mu(B(x, D^{\ps(\fp)})) \ge 2^{-3a} \mu(B(\pc(\fp), 4D^{\ps(\fp)}))\,. $$ Plugging this into \eqref{eq-lem-Tile-holder-im2} and using $a \ge 4$, we get $$ |T_{\fp}^* g(y)| \le \frac{2^{103a^3}}{\mu(B(\pc(\fp), 4D^{\ps(\fp)}))} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{\ps(\fp)}}\right)^{1/a} \int_{E(\fp)} |g(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,, $$ which completes the proof of the lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of limited scale impact
nodes.statement: For the first estimate, assume that $\ps(\fp) < s(J)$, then in particular $\ps(\fp) \le \ps(\fu_1)$. Since $\fp \notin \mathfrak{S}$, we have by \Cref{overlap-implies-distance} that $\scI(\fp) \cap \scI(\fu_1) = \emptyset$. Since $B\Big(c(J), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(J)}\Big) \subset \scI(J) \subset \scI(\fu_1)$, this implies $$ \rho(c(J), \pc(\fp)) \ge \frac{1}{4}D^{s(J)}\,. $$ On the other hand $$ \rho(c(J), \pc(\fp)) \le \frac{1}{8} D^{s(J)} + 8 D^{\ps(\fp)}\,, $$ by our assumption. Thus $D^{\ps(\fp)} \ge 64^{-1} D^{s(J)}$, which contradicts \eqref{defineD} and $a \ge 4$. For the second estimate, assume that $\ps(\fp) > s(J) + 3$. Since $J \in \mathcal{J}'$, we have $J \subsetneq \scI(\fu_1)$. Thus there exists $J' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $J \subset J'$ and $s(J') = s(J) + 1$, by \eqref{coverdyadic} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}. By definition of $\mathcal{J}'$, there exists some $\fp' \in \mathfrak{S}$ such that $\scI(\fp') \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J) + 2})$. On the other hand, since $B(\scI(\fp)) \cap B^\circ(J) \ne \emptyset$, by the triangle inequality it holds that $$ B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J) + 3}) \subset B(\pc(\fp), 10 D^{\ps(\fp)})\,. $$ Using the definition of $\mathfrak{S}$, we have $$ 2^{Zn/2} \le d_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2)) \le d_{B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J) + 2})}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2))\,. $$ By \eqref{seconddb}, this is $$ \le 2^{-100a} d_{B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J) + 3})}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2)) $$ $$ \le 2^{-100a} d_{B(\pc(\fp), 10 D^{\ps(\fp)})}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2))\,, $$ and by \eqref{firstdb} and the definition of $\mathfrak{S}$ $$ \le 2^{-94a} d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2)) \le 2^{-94a} 2^{Zn/2}\,. $$ This is a contradiction, the second estimate follows.

nodes.name: Proof of local tree control
nodes.statement:
By the triangle inequality and since $T_{ p}^* g = \mathbf{1}_{B(\pc( p), 5D^{\ps( p)})} T_{ p}^* g$, we have $$ \sup_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{ T( u_2) \setminus\mathfrak{S}}^* g| \leq \sup_{B^\circ{}(J)} \sum_{\substack{ p \in  T( u_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}\ B(\scI( p)) \cap B^\circ(J) 
e \emptyset}} |T_{ p}^*g|\,. $$ By \Cref{limited-scale-impact}, this is at most  egin{equation} \sum_{s = s(J)}^{s(J) + 3} \sum_{\substack{ p \in  P, \ps( p) = s\ B(\scI( p)) \cap B^\circ(J) 
e \emptyset}} \sup_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{ p}^* g|\,. \end{equation} If $x \in E( p)$ and $B(\scI( p)) \cap B^\circ(J) 
e \emptyset$, then $$ B(c(J), 16D^{\ps( p)}) \subset B(x, 32 D^{\ps( p)})\,, $$ by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality. Using the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, it follows that $$ \mu(B(x, D^{\ps( p)})) \ge 2^{-5a} \mu(B(c(J), 16D^{\ps( p)}))\,. $$ Using \eqref{definetp*}, \eqref{eq-Ks-size} and that $a \ge 4$, we bound \eqref{eq-sep-tree-aux-3} by $$ 2^{103a^3}\sum_{s = s(J)}^{s(J) + 3} \sum_{\substack{ p \in  P, \ps( p) = s\B(\scI( p)) \cap B^\circ(J) 
e \emptyset}}  rac{1}{\mu(B(c(J), 16 D^s)} \int_{E( p)} |g| \, \mathrm{d}\mu\,. $$ For each $I \in \mathcal{D}$, the sets $E( p)$ for $ p \in  P$ with $\scI( p) = I$ are pairwise disjoint by \eqref{defineep} and \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}. Further, if $B(\scI( p)) \cap B^\circ(J) 
e \emptyset$ and $\ps( p) \ge s(J)$, then $E( p) \subset B(c(J), 16 D^{\ps( p)})$. Thus the last display is bounded by $$ 2^{103a^3}\sum_{s = s(J)}^{s(J) + 3}  rac{1}{\mu(B(c(J), 16 D^s))} \int_{B(c(J), 16 D^s)} |g| \, \mathrm{d}\mu\,. $$ $$ \le \inf_{x' \in J} 2^{103a^3 +2} M_{\mathcal{B}, 1} |g|\,. $$ The lemma follows since $a \ge 4$.

Then for $i = 1,2$ and each $J \in \mathcal{J}'$ and all bounded $g$ with bounded support, we have \begin{align} \sup_{B'(J)} |T_{\fC_i}^*g| \leq \inf_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T^*_{\fC_i} g| + 2^{128a^3+4a+3} \inf_{J} M_{\mathcal{B}, 1} |g| \end{align} and for all $y,y' \in B'(J)$ $$ |e(\fcc(\fu_i)(y)) T_{\fC_i}^* g(y) - e(\fcc(\fu_i)(y')) T_{\fC_i}^* g(y')| $$ \begin{equation} \le 2^{128a^3+4a+1} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}}\right)^{1/a} \inf_J M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g|\,. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof of global tree control 1
nodes.statement: Note that \eqref{TreeUB} follows from \eqref{TreeHolder}, since for $y'\in B^\circ{}(J)$, by the triangle inequality, $$\left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}}\right)^{1/a}\le \Big(16 + \frac{1}8\Big)^{1/a}\le 2^2.$$ By the triangle inequality, \Cref{adjoint-tile-support} and \Cref{Holder-correlation-tile}, we have for all $y, y' \in B'(J)$ \begin{equation} |e(\fcc(\fu_i)(y)) T_{\fC_i}^* g(y) - e(\fcc(\fu_i)(y')) T_{\fC_i}^* g(y')| \end{equation} $$ \le \sum_{\substack{\fp \in \fC_i\\ B(\scI(\fp)) \cap B'(J) \neq \emptyset}} |e(\fcc(\fu_i)(y)) T_{\fp}^* g(y) - e(\fcc(\fu_i)(y')) T_{\fp}^* g(y')| $$ $$ \le 2^{128a^3}\rho(y,y')^{1/a} \sum_{\substack{\fp \in \fC_i\\ B(\scI(\fp)) \cap B'(J) \neq \emptyset}} \frac{D^{- \ps(\fp)/a}}{\mu(B(\pc(\fp), 4D^{\ps(\fp)}))} \int_{E(\fp)} |g| \, \mathrm{d}\mu\,. $$ By \Cref{scales-impacting-interval}, we have $\ps(\fp) \ge s(J)$ for all $\fp$ occurring in the sum. Further, for each $s \ge s(J)$, the sets $E(\fp)$ for $\fp \in \fP$ with $\ps(\fp) = s$ are pairwise disjoint by \eqref{defineep} and \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}, and contained in $B(c(J), 32D^{s})$ by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality. Using also the doubling estimate \eqref{doublingx}, we obtain that the expression in the last display can be estimated by $$ 2^{128a^3}\rho(y,y')^{1/a} \sum_{S \ge s \ge s(J)} D^{-s/a} \frac{2^{4a}}{\mu(B(c(J), 32D^{s}))} \int_{B(c(J), 32D^{s})} |g| \, \mathrm{d}\mu $$ $$ \le 2^{128a^3+4a} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}}\right)^{1/a} \sum_{S \ge s \ge s(J)} D^{(s(J) - s)/a} \inf_J M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g|\,. $$ Since $D^{-1/a}\le\frac12$, we have $$ \sum_{S \ge s \ge s(J)} D^{(s(J) - s)/a} \le 2. $$ Estimate \eqref{TreeHolder}, and therefore the lemma, follow.

nodes.name: Proof of Hölder correlation tree
nodes.statement: Let $P$ be the product on the right hand side of \eqref{hHolder}, and $h_J$ be as defined in \eqref{def-hj}. By \eqref{eq-pao-2} and \Cref{adjoint-tile-support}, the function $h_J$ is supported in $B'(J) \cap \scI(\fu_1)$. By \eqref{eq-pao-2}, \Cref{global-tree-control-1} and \Cref{global-tree-control-2}, we have for all $y \in B'(J)$: $$ |h_J(y)| \le 2^{257a^3+4a+3} P\,. $$ We have by the triangle inequality \begin{align} &|h_J(y) - h_J(y')|\nonumber\\ &\le |\chi_J(y) - \chi_J(y')| |T_{\fT(\fu_1)}^* g_1(y)| |T_{\fT(\fu_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y)|\\ & + |\chi_J(y')| |e(\fcc(\fu_1)(y)) T_{\fT(\fu_1)}^* g_1(y) - e(\fcc(\fu_1)(y')) T_{\fT(\fu_1)}^* g_1(y')| |T_{\fT(\fu_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y)|\\ & + |\chi_J(y')| |T_{\fT(\fu_1)}^* g_1(y')| |e(\fcc(\fu_2)(y)) T_{\fT(\fu_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y) - e(\fcc(\fu_2)(y')) T_{\fT(\fu_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y')|\,. \end{align} As $h_J$ is supported in $\scI(\fu_1)$, we can assume without loss of generality that $y' \in \scI(\fu_1)$. If $y \notin \scI(\fu_1)$, then \eqref{eq-h-Lip-1} vanishes. If $y \in \scI(\fu_1)$ then we have by \eqref{eq-pao-3}, \Cref{global-tree-control-1} and \Cref{global-tree-control-2} $$ \eqref{eq-h-Lip-1} \le 2^{484a^3+4a+3} \frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}} P\,, $$ where $P$ denotes the product on the right hand side of \eqref{hHolder}. By \eqref{eq-pao-2}, \Cref{global-tree-control-1} and \Cref{global-tree-control-2}, we have $$ \eqref{eq-h-Lip-2} \le 2^{257a^3+4a+1} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}}\right)^{1/a} P\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-pao-2}, and twice \Cref{global-tree-control-1}, we have $$ \eqref{eq-h-Lip-3} \le 2^{256a^3+8a+5} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}}\right)^{1/a} P\,. $$ Using that $\rho(y,y') \le 32D^{s(J)}$ and $a \ge 4$, the lemma follows.

nodes.statement_short: Product rule for the Hölder norm with the partition-of-unity bounds and \Cref{global-tree-control-1}, \Cref{global-tree-control-2}.

nodes.name: Equation (429)
nodes.statement: &|h_J(y) - h_J(y')|\nonumber\\ &\le |\chi_J(y) - \chi_J(y')| |T_{\fT(\fu_1)}^* g_1(y)| |T_{\fT(\fu_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y)|\\ & + |\chi_J(y')| |e(\fcc(\fu_1)(y)) T_{\fT(\fu_1)}^* g_1(y) - e(\fcc(\fu_1)(y')) T_{\fT(\fu_1)}^* g_1(y')| |T_{\fT(\fu_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y)|\\ & + |\chi_J(y')| |T_{\fT(\fu_1)}^* g_1(y')| |e(\fcc(\fu_2)(y)) T_{\fT(\fu_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y) - e(\fcc(\fu_2)(y')) T_{\fT(\fu_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y')|\,.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators
nodes.label: eq-h-Lip-1

nodes.name: lower oscillation bound
nodes.statement: For all $J \in \mathcal{J}'$, we have that $$ d_{B(J)}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2)) \ge 2^{-201a^3} 2^{Zn/2}\,. $$
assumptions: For all $J \in \mathcal{J}'$
nodes.label: lower-oscillation-bound

nodes.name: Proof of lower oscillation bound
nodes.statement: Since $\emptyset \ne \fT(\fu_1) \subset \mathfrak{S}$ by \Cref{overlap-implies-distance}, there exists at least one tile $\fp \in \mathcal{S}$ with $\scI(\fp) \subsetneq \scI(\fu_1)$. Thus $\scI(\fu_1) \notin \mathcal{J}'$, so $J \subsetneq \scI(\fu_1)$. Thus there exists a cube $J' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $J \subset J'$ and $s(J') = s(J) + 1$, by \eqref{coverdyadic} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}. By definition of $\mathcal{J'}$ and the triangle inequality, there exists $\fp \in \mathfrak{S}$ such that $$ \scI(\fp) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1}) \subset B(c(J), 128 D^{s(J)+2})\,. $$ Thus, by definition of $\mathfrak{S}$: \begin{align*} 2^{Zn/2} \le d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2)) \le d_{B(c(J), 128 D^{s(J)+2})}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2))\,. \end{align*} By the doubling property \eqref{firstdb}, this is $$ \le 2^{200a^3 + 4a} d_{B(J)}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2))\,, $$ which gives the lemma using $a \ge 4$.
nodes.statement_short: A tile of $\mathfrak{S}$ lies near the parent of $J$; compare its metric to $d_{B(J)}$ by doubling.

nodes.name: Proof of correlation distant tree parts
nodes.statement: We have $$ \eqref{eq-lhs-big-sep-tree} = \left| \int_{X} T_{\fT(\fu_1)}^* g_1 \overline{T_{\fT(\fu_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2 }\right|\,. $$ By \Cref{adjoint-tile-support}, the right hand side is supported in $\scI(\fu_1)$. Using \eqref{eq-pao-1} of \Cref{Lipschitz-partition-unity} and the definition \eqref{def-hj} of $h_J$, we thus have $$ \le \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \left|\int_{X} e(\fcc(\fu_2)(y) - \fcc(\fu_1)(y)) h_J(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right|\,. $$ Using \Cref{Holder-van-der-Corput} with the ball $B(J)$, we bound this by $$ \le 2^{7a} \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \mu(B(J)) \|h_J\|_{C^{\tau}(B'(J))} (1 + d_{B(J)}(\fcc(\fu_2), \fcc(\fu_1)))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}\,. $$ Using \Cref{Holder-correlation-tree}, \Cref{lower-oscillation-bound} and $a \ge 4$, we bound the above by \begin{multline} \le 2^{485a^3+7a+3a^3+3a} 2^{-Zn/(4a^2 + 2a^3)} \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \mu(B(J)) \\ \times \prod_{j=1}^2 (\inf_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{\fT(\fu_j)}^* g_j| + \inf_J M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j)\,. \end{multline} By the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $$ \mu(B(J)) \le 2^{6a} \mu(B^\circ{}(J))\,, $$ thus $$ \mu(B(J)) \prod_{j=1}^2 (\inf_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{\fT(\fu_j)}^* g_j| + \inf_J M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j) $$ $$ \le 2^{6a} \int_{B^\circ{}(J)} \prod_{j=1}^2 ( |T_{\fT(\fu_j)}^* g_j|(x) + M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j(x)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) $$ $$ \le 2^{6a} \int_J \prod_{j=1}^2 ( |T_{\fT(\fu_j)}^* g_j|(x) + M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j(x)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. $$ Summing over $J \in \mathcal{J}'$, we obtain $$ \eqref{eq-big-sep-1} \le 2^{499a^3} 2^{-Zn/(4a^2 + 2a^3)} \int_X \prod_{j=1}^2 ( |T_{\fT(\fu_j)}^* g_j|(x) + M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j(x)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. $$ Applying the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, \Cref{correlation-distant-tree-parts} follows.
nodes.statement_short: Localize with the partition of unity, apply \Cref{Holder-van-der-Corput} on each $B(J)$ using \Cref{Holder-correlation-tree} and \Cref{lower-oscillation-bound}, then sum and apply Cauchy-Schwarz.

nodes.name: Equation (432)
nodes.statement: \le 2^{485a^3+7a+3a^3+3a} 2^{-Zn/(4a^2 + 2a^3)} \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \mu(B(J)) \\ \times \prod_{j=1}^2 (\inf_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{\fT(\fu_j)}^* g_j| + \inf_J M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j)\,.
nodes.label: eq-big-sep-1

nodes.name: cubes $\mathcal{J}'$ (remaining tiles)
nodes.statement:
We define
    $$
        \mathcal{J}' = \{J \in \mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu_1)) \, : \, J \subset \scI(\fu_1)\}\,,
    $$
    note that this is different from the $\mathcal{J}'$ defined in the previous subsection.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: dyadic partition 2
nodes.statement: We have $$ \scI(\fu_1) = \dot{\bigcup_{J \in \mathcal{J}'}} J\,. $$
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.label: dyadic-partition-2

nodes.name: Proof of dyadic partition 2
nodes.statement: By \Cref{dyadic-partitions}, it remains only to show that each $J \in \mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu_1))$ with $J \cap \scI(\fu_1) \ne \emptyset$ is in $\mathcal{J}'$. But if $J \notin \mathcal{J}'$, then by \eqref{dyadicproperty} $\scI(\fu_1) \subsetneq J$. Pick $\fp \in \fT(\fu_1)$. Then $\scI(\fp) \subsetneq J$. This contradicts the definition of $\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu_1))$.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.statement_short: A cube meeting $\scI(\fu_1)$ but not inside it would contain a tile of the tree, contradicting the definition of $\mathcal{J}$.

nodes.name: bound for tree projection
nodes.statement: We have for all bounded $f$ with bounded support $$ \|P_{\mathcal{J}'}|T_{\fT(\fu_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2|\|_2 \le 2^{102a^3+21a+5} 2^{-\frac{25}{101a}Zn\kappa} \|\mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fu_1)} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|\|_2 $$
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
assumptions: We have for all bounded $f$ with bounded support
nodes.statement_short: The $\mathcal{J}'$-projection of the non-separated part of the second tree decays like $2^{-cZn\kappa}$ relative to the maximal function.
nodes.label: bound-for-tree-projection

nodes.name: Proof of correlation near tree parts
nodes.statement: By \Cref{tree-projection-estimate} and \Cref{adjoint-tile-support}, we have \begin{align*} \eqref{eq-lhs-small-sep-tree} \le 2^{130a^3} \|P_{\mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu_1))} |\mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fu_1)}g_1| \|_2 \|P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu_1) )}|\mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fu_1)} T_{\fT(\fu_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2|\|_2\,. \end{align*} It follows from the definition of the projection operator $P$ and Jensen's inequality that $$ \|P_{\mathcal{L}(\fT(\fu_1))} |g_1\mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fu_1)}| \|_2 \le \|g_1 \mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fu_1)}\|_2\,. $$ By \Cref{dyadic-partition-2}, a cube $J \in \mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu_1))$ intersects $\scI(\fu_1)$ if and only if $J \in \mathcal{J}'$. Thus $$ P_{\mathcal{J}(\fT(\fu_1) )}|\mathbf{1}_{\scI(\fu_1)} T_{\fT(\fu_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2| = P_{\mathcal{J}'}|T_{\fT(\fu_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2|\,. $$ Combining this with \Cref{bound-for-tree-projection}, the definition \eqref{definekappa} and $a \ge 4$ proves the lemma.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Apply \Cref{tree-projection-estimate} to the pair, bound the $g_1$ factor by Jensen and the $g_2$ factor by \Cref{bound-for-tree-projection}.

nodes.name: thin scale impact
nodes.statement: If $\fp \in \fT(\fu_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}$ and $J \in \mathcal{J'}$ with $B(\scI(\fp)) \cap B(J) \ne \emptyset$, then $$ \ps(\fp) \le s(J) + 2 - \frac{Zn}{202a^3}\,. $$
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
assumptions: If $\fp \in \fT(\fu_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}$ and $J \in \mathcal{J'}$ with $B(\scI(\fp)) \cap B(J) \ne \emptyset$
nodes.label: thin-scale-impact

nodes.name: Proof of thin scale impact
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\ps(\fp) > s(J) + 2 -\frac{Zn}{202a^3} =: s(J) - s_1$. Then, we have $s_1 + 2 \ge 0$ so $$ \rho(\pc(\fp), c(J)) \le 8D^{s(J)}+8D^{\ps(\fp)} \le 16 D^{\ps(\fp) + s_1 + 2}\,. $$ There exists a tile $\fq \in \fT(\fu_1)$. By \eqref{forest1}, it satisfies $\scI(\fq) \subsetneq \scI(\fu_1)$. Thus $\scI(\fu_1) \notin \mathcal{J}'$. It follows that $J \subsetneq \scI(\fu_1)$. By \eqref{coverdyadic} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}, there exists a cube $J' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $J \subset J'$ and $s(J') = s(J) + 1$. By definition of $\mathcal{J}'$, there exists a tile $\fp' \in \fT(\fu_1)$ with $$ \scI(\fp') \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})\,. $$ By the triangle inequality, the definition \eqref{defineD} and $a \ge 4$, we have $$ B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J')+1}) \subset B(\pc(\fp), 128 D^{\ps(\fp) + s_1 + 2})\,. $$ Since $\fp' \in \fT(\fu_1)$ and $\scI(\fu_1) \subset \scI(\fu_2)$, we have by \eqref{forest5} $$ d_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fp'), \fcc(\fu_2)) > 2^{Z(n+1)}\,. $$ Hence, by \eqref{forest1}, the triangle inequality and using that by \eqref{defineZ} $Z(n+1) = 2^{12a}(n+1) \ge 3$ $$ d_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2)) > 2^{Z(n+1)} - 4 \ge 2^{Z(n+1) - 1}\,. $$ It follows that $$ 2^{Z(n+1)-1} \le d_{\fp'}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2)) \le d_{B(\pc(\fp), 128 D^{\ps(\fp) + s_1+ 2})}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2))\,. $$ Using \eqref{firstdb}, we obtain $$ \le 2^{9a + 100a^3 (s_1+3)} d_{\fp}(\fcc(\fu_1), \fcc(\fu_2))\,. $$ Since $\fp' \notin \mathfrak{S}$ this is bounded by $$ \le 2^{9a + 100a^3 (s_1+3)} 2^{Zn/2}\,. $$ Thus $$ Z n/2 + Z - 1 \le 9a + 100a^3(s_1 + 3)\,, $$ contradicting the definition of $s_1$.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: a large tile near $J$ would make the separation of $\fu_1,\fu_2$ at a nearby tile of $\fT(\fu_1)$ too small.

nodes.name: square function count
nodes.statement: For each $J \in \mathcal{J}'$ and all $s$, we have $$ \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \int_J \Bigg(\sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\\ I \cap \scI(\fu_1) = \emptyset\\ J \cap B(I) \ne \emptyset}} \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}\bigg)^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu \le 2^{14a+1} (8 D^{-s})^\kappa\,. $$
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
assumptions: For each $J \in \mathcal{J}'$ and all $s$
nodes.statement_short: Average square overlap of small balls near the boundary of $J$ is small, by the small boundary property.
nodes.label: square-function-count

nodes.name: Proof of square function count
nodes.statement: Since $J \in \mathcal{J}'$ we have $J \subset \scI(\fu_1)$. Thus, if $B(I) \cap J \ne \emptyset$ then \begin{equation} B(I) \cap J \subset \{x \in J \ : \ \rho(x, X \setminus J) \le 8D^{s(I)}\}\,. \end{equation} Furthermore, for each $s$ the balls $B(I)$ with $s(I) = s$ have bounded overlap: Consider the collection $\mathcal{D}_{s,x}$ of all $I \in \mathcal{D}$ with $x \in B(I)$ and $s(I) = s$. By \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}, the balls $B(c(I), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(I)})$, $I \in \mathcal{D}_{s,x}$ are disjoint, and by the triangle inequality, they are contained in $B(x, 9 D^{s})$. By the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, we have $$ \mu(B(x, 9D^{s})) \le 2^{7a} \mu(B(c(I), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(I)})) $$ for each $I \in \mathcal{D}_{s,x}$. Thus $$ \mu(B(x, 9D^{s})) \ge \sum_{I \in \mathcal{D}_{s,x}} \mu(B(c(I), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(I)})) \ge 2^{-7a} |\mathcal{D}_{s,x}| \mu(B(x, 9D^{s}))\,. $$ Dividing by the positive $\mu(B(x, 9D^{s}))$, we obtain that for each $x$ \begin{equation} \Bigg(\sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\\ I \cap \scI(\fu_1) = \emptyset\\ J \cap B(I) \ne \emptyset}} \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}(x) \bigg)^2 \le |\mathcal{D}_{s(J) - s,x}|^2 \le 2^{14a} \,. \end{equation} Combining \eqref{eq-sep-small-incl}, \eqref{eq-sep-small-bound} and the small boundary property \eqref{eq-small-boundary}, noting that $8D^{s(I)}=8D^{-s}D^{s(J)}$, the lemma follows.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Bounded overlap of same-scale balls plus the small boundary property.

nodes.name: Equation (433)
nodes.statement: B(I) \cap J \subset \{x \in J \ : \ \rho(x, X \setminus J) \le 8D^{s(I)}\}\,.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.label: eq-sep-small-incl

nodes.name: Equation (434)
nodes.statement: \Bigg(\sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\\ I \cap \scI(\fu_1) = \emptyset\\ J \cap B(I) \ne \emptyset}} \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}(x) \bigg)^2 \le |\mathcal{D}_{s(J) - s,x}|^2 \le 2^{14a} \,.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.label: eq-sep-small-bound

nodes.name: Proof of bound for tree projection
nodes.statement:
Expanding the definition of $P_{\mathcal{J}'}$, we have $$ \|P_{\mathcal{J}'}|T_{ T( u_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2|\|_2 $$ $$ = \left(\sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'}  rac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J \left| \sum_{ p \in  T( u_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}} T_{ p}^* g_2(y) ight| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) ight)^2 ight)^{1/2}\,. $$ By \Cref{adjoint-tile-support}, the innermost sum in the last display is $0$ if $J \cap B(\scI( p)) = \emptyset$. Then we split that sum according to the scale of $ p$ relative to the scale of $J$. By \Cref{thin-scale-impact}, $s_1 \le s(J) - \ps( p) \le 2S$ with $s_1 := \lfloor rac{Zn}{202a^3} - 2floor$: $$ = \left(\sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'}  rac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J \left| \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \sum_{\substack{ p \in  T( u_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}\ \ps( p) = s(J) - s\ J \cap B(\scI( p)) 
e \emptyset}} T_{ p}^* g_2(y) ight| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) ight)^2 ight)^{1/2}\,. $$ Then we apply the triangle inequality and Minkowski's inequality to get  egin{equation} \le \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'}  rac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J \sum_{\substack{ p \in  T( u_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}\ \ps( p) = s(J) - s\ J \cap B(\scI( p)) 
e \emptyset}} |T_{ p}^* g_2(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) ight)^2ight)^{1/2}\,. \end{equation} We have by \Cref{adjoint-tile-support} and \eqref{eq-Ks-size} $$ |T_{ p}^* g_2(y)| \le 2^{102a^3} \mathbf{1}_{B(\pc( p), 8D^{\ps( p)})}(y) \int_{E( p)}  rac{1}{\mu(B(x, D^{\ps( p)}))} |g_2(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. $$ Using the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, it follows that $$ \mu(B(\pc( p), 8D^{\ps( p)})) \le 2^{4a} \mu(B(x, D^{\ps( p)}))\,. $$ Thus, using also $a \ge 4$ $$ |T_{ p}^* g_2(y)| \le 2^{102a^3+4a} \mathbf{1}_{B(\pc( p), 8D^{\ps( p)})}(y)  rac{1}{\mu(B(\pc( p), 8D^{\ps( p)}))} \int_{E( p)} |g_2(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. $$ Since for each $I \in \mathcal{D}$ the sets $E( p),  p \in  P(I)$ are disjoint, it follows that $$ \int_J \sum_{\substack{ p \in  T( u_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}\ \scI( p) = I\ J \cap B(\scI( p)) 
e \emptyset}} |T_{ p}^* g_2(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu $$ $$ \le 2^{102a^3+4a} \int_J \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}  rac{1}{\mu(B(\pc( p), 8D^{\ps( p)}))} \int_{B(\pc( p), 8D^{\ps( p)})} |g_2(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) $$ $$ \le 2^{102a^3+4a} \int_J M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|(y) \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ By \Cref{overlap-implies-distance}, we have $\scI( p) \cap \scI( u_1) = \emptyset$ for all $ p \in  T( u_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}$. Thus we can estimate \eqref{eq-sep-tree-small-1} by $$ 2^{102a^3+4a} \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'}  rac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J \sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\ I \cap \scI( u_1) = \emptyset\ J \cap B(I) 
e \emptyset}} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2| \mathbf{1}_{B(I)} \, \mathrm{d}\mu ight)^2ight)^{1/2}\,, $$ which is by Cauchy-Schwarz at most  egin{equation} 2^{102a^3+4a} \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \int_J ( M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|)^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu 	imes  rac{1}{\mu(J)} \int_J \left(\sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\ I \cap \scI( u_1) = \emptyset\ J \cap B(I) 
e \emptyset}} \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}ight)^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu ight)^{1/2}\,. \end{equation} Using \Cref{square-function-count}, we bound \eqref{eq-sep-tree-small-2} by $$ 2^{102a^3+4a} \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left(2^{14a+1} (8 D^{-s})^\kappa \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \int_J (M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|)^2ight)^{1/2}\,, $$ and since dyadic cubes in $\mathcal{J}'$ form a partition of $\scI( u_1)$ by \Cref{dyadic-partition-2}, $\kappa \le 1$ by \eqref{definekappa}, and $a \ge 4$ $$ \le 2^{102a^3+11a+2} \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} D^{-s\kappa/2} \|\mathbf{1}_{\scI( u_1)} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|\|_2 $$ $$ \le 2^{102a^3+11a+2} D^{-s_1 \kappa /2}  rac{1}{1 - D^{-\kappa/2}} \|\mathbf{1}_{\scI( u_1)} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|\|_2\,. $$ By convexity of $t \mapsto D^{-t}$ and since $D \ge 2$, we have for all $0 \le t \le 1$ $$ D^{-t} \le 1 - t(1 - 1/D) \le 1 -  rac{1}{2}t\,. $$ Using this for $t = \kappa/2$ and using that $s_1 =  rac{Zn}{202a^3} - 2$ and the definitions \eqref{defineD} and \eqref{definekappa} of $\kappa$ and $D$ $$ \le 2^{102a^3+11a+2} 2^{-100a^2( rac{Zn}{202a^3} - 3)  rac{\kappa}{2}}  rac{2}{\kappa} \|\mathbf{1}_{\scI( u_1)} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|\|_2 $$ $$ = 2^{102a^3+21a+4} 2^{150a^2\kappa} 2^{- rac{100}{404a}Zn\kappa} \|\mathbf{1}_{\scI( u_1)} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|\|_2\,. $$ Using the definition \eqref{definekappa} of $\kappa$ and $a \ge 4$, the lemma follows.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Split by relative scale (only scales $\ge s_1$ occur by \Cref{thin-scale-impact}), bound each tile by the maximal function, use Cauchy-Schwarz and \Cref{square-function-count}, and sum a geometric series.

nodes.name: Equation (435)
nodes.statement: \le \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J \sum_{\substack{\fp \in \fT(\fu_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}\\ \ps(\fp) = s(J) - s\\ J \cap B(\scI(\fp)) \ne \emptyset}} |T_{\fp}^* g_2(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right)^2\right)^{1/2}\,.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.label: eq-sep-tree-small-1

nodes.name: Equation (436)
nodes.statement: 2^{102a^3+4a} \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \int_J ( M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|)^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu \times \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \int_J \left(\sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\\ I \cap \scI(\fu_1) = \emptyset\\ J \cap B(I) \ne \emptyset}} \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}\right)^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right)^{1/2}\,.
